n0.text:
{Sensors picked up a weird growth at {place}. It's spreading fast in an inward spiral, covering nine hectares, and {instrument} says it's already doubled in size.|There's a massive, aggressive organism growing at {place}. It's closing inward like a tightening knot, and {instrument} shows it's expanding at an alarming rate.}
The spiral has been tightening at a constant rate, which means it started somewhere, on a day, and the day can be worked out.

choices.text: {Walk to the centre|Head into the middle|Push toward the core|Advance to the center} of the spiral.
{Take a sample|Collect a specimen|Scrape off a sample|Bag a piece} from the edge.
{Burn a firebreak|Torch the perimeter|Ignite a controlled burn|Drop a thermal line} and watch what it does.

n0.emText: {Something's growing at {place} in a tight spiral that closes inward. It's the only living thing on the entire rock, and it's expanding way too fast for comfort.|You recognize this pattern-it's an aggressive growth enclosing something at the center. Whatever's in the middle, it's definitely trapped.}
n0.bubba: Bubba will not step on it. "It's growed itself inward, sugar. Roba ca se chiude 'ncoppa a quaccosa. Somethin's in there."

a.text: The growth gets {denser and quieter|thicker and quieter} towards the middle. {At the core, the growth has enveloped a solid object|In the dead center, the biomass has sealed around an alien relic|At the middle of the spiral sits an encased metal artifact} that it did not grow, and has been careful about it.

choices.text: Cut it out.
Leave it and log the position.

a.emText:
The growth goes quiet towards the middle, the way a street goes quiet outside a hospital.
At the centre it has grown around a thing it did not grow, patiently, over years, the way a hedge grows round a bicycle. Whatever is in there has been kept the way you keep a wallet in an inside pocket on a bad street.

b.text:
{The sample fights the knife.|The sample argues with the knife.} It's not tough; it is unwilling.
In the tube it goes on moving, and by the time the team is back at the lander it has arranged itself into the same spiral, {one centimetre|a centimetre|half an inch} across.

choices.text: Keep it aboard.
Put it back where it came from.

c.text:
The firebreak burns {a clean line|a clean lane} across the spiral's arm.
The growth does not try to cross it. It goes round, in both directions, and meets itself behind the away team in under {few} minutes.

choices.text: Stand and fight it back to the lander.
Drop everything and run.

a1.text: It comes free in {a wet handful|a wet double handful} of stems and what is inside has been kept alive, {on purpose|deliberately}, by something with no reason to keep anything alive.

a2.text: The team backs out along its own trail. Behind them the spiral closes over the gap at walking pace, and the centre is {exactly|precisely} where it was, and {exactly|precisely} as hidden.

b1.text: Sealed, monitored, and worth {a great deal|a good deal|rather a lot} to the right laboratory. The ship's biology bay is a livelier place than it was, and {nobody|no one} sleeps quite as well.

b2.text:
It is taken back and set down at the edge, and the whole spiral shifts a metre towards the lander {and then|then|and after that} stops, which everyone agrees to record as wind.
Something's left on {ground} where the sample lay.

c1.text: {It's not a plant|Whatever it is, it is not a plant} and it does not burn a second time.

c2.text:
{Everyone gets aboard.|Everybody gets aboard.} The sample kits, the cutter and one boot do not.
{leader} is last up the ladder and does not look back, and says afterwards that it was not chasing them, it was seeing them off.

c_m.text:
The firebreak burns {a clean line|a clean lane} across the spiral's arm and the growth does not try to cross it. It goes round, in both directions, and meets itself.
What that leaves is a ring of unburnt ground in the middle with the growth sealed outside it, and the ring is {nine metres|about ten metres|a good size} across, and nothing in it is moving.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{We have just built it a wall.|It let us do that.|Nine metres of somewhere it cannot go, and it is not trying.}"
asides.any: {member} {walks the burn line once, all the way round|watches the ring rather than the fire|puts the torch down}

choices.text: Walk into the ring.
Burn the whole thing, ring included.
Work out when the spiral started.

c_ring.text:
Inside the ring the ground is {bare|clean|scoured}, and in the middle of it there is a hollow the exact shape of something that is no longer in it.
The growth outside the line stops growing that night. All of it, everywhere, at once, which is how the party learns that the spiral was never the organism: it was {the search|the digging|what the organism does when it is looking for something}.

c_date.text:
Growth rate against the inward pitch of the spiral gives a date, and the date is {eleven years ago|the spring of a year the party can name|a specific week}, and the survey record for this rock has an entry for that week.
The entry is a landing. One vessel, three days, and a departure that is logged as having taken off {four hours|some hours|a while} later than the vessel's own log says it did.

n0.text:
The transmission is a voice, in a language the ship's tables get to eighty per cent of, and it is asking for help by name. Not the ship's name. {leader}'s.
The source is a shelter at {place}, dug in against {hazard} and holding pressure.
There is a second survival beacon in the kit and it has never been switched on, which takes {a decision|deciding|somebody deciding} rather than an accident.

choices.text: Knock.
Cut the power to the shelter first.
Ask it how it knows the name.

n0.emText:
The voice is asking for help by name, and the name is yours, and it is using the one that only eight per cent of you can hear properly.
The tables get it to eighty per cent. The other twenty per cent is a sound like somebody saying a word into a coat. It has been saying it for a long time out of a shelter the size of a bus stop on a world with no bus routes.
n0.bubba: "It's sayin' your name," says Bubba, very quietly, on the ladder. "Nun rispunnere subito. Let it say it twice."

a.text:
{The door cycles before anyone touches it.|The door cycles before a hand goes near it.} Inside is one room, one chair, one light, and a person in a suit {two generations|a generation|three generations} out of date sitting with their back to the door.
They do not turn around. They say they have been practising this for {a long time|a good while|longer than anybody says}.

choices.text: Sit down and listen.
Turn the chair around.

b.text:
{The team traces the feed and pulls it.|The team follows the feed back and pulls it.} The shelter goes dark; the voice does not stop.
It has not been using the shelter's power for a {very|remarkably} long time. {It is being polite.|It has been being polite.}

choices.text: Go in anyway.
Strip the shelter for parts and leave.

c.text:
The question gets {a long pause|a very long pause}, at least that part was honest.
Then: it does not know the name. It knows the shape of whoever is listening, and it fits a name to it. It has been fitting names to listeners {since before this world had an atmosphere|since before there was air on this world}.

choices.text: Ask what it wants.
Stop transmitting. Walk away.

a1.text:
It takes {an hour|the better part of an hour|two hours}. They were on a survey that never filed, they have been alone since before the party was born, and they are not asking to be rescued. {They are asking to be remembered.|What they are asking for is to be remembered.}
They give {leader} everything they have left, which is not much, and it is more than the ship deserves.

a2.text: {The suit is empty|There is nobody in the suit} and has been empty for a {very|remarkably} long time, and the voice keeps talking out of the chair, out of the walls, out of the away team's own helmets.

b1.text: Inside is {lots} years of somebody's handwriting on {every flat surface|every flat surface in the place}, and at the end of it, in the last clear space by the door, an apology addressed to whoever came.

b2.text: Good hardware, well maintained, and the team is up and away in {ninety minutes|an hour and a half|two hours}. The voice is still on the band when the ship makes its burn out of orbit.

c1.text: It wants what it has always wanted, and it explains this at length, and none of it survives the trip back up as anything the crew can repeat. What survives is in {leader}'s hands, and {nobody|no one} remembers being handed it.

c2.text: {The band goes quiet.|The band goes flat and quiet.} The team walks back across {ground} in a silence that everybody is grateful for, and the shelter does not call after them, which is somehow the unkindest part.

a1_m.text:
It takes {an hour|the better part of an hour|two hours}. They were on a survey that never filed, they have been alone since before the party was born, and they are not asking to be rescued.
What they are asking for takes another {twenty minutes|quarter of an hour|while} to arrive at, because they have not had to phrase it for anybody before and the phrasing keeps coming out as {an apology|an excuse|a list of reasons}.

asides.nurturing: {member} has moved a chair across the floor without anybody hearing it and is sitting where the light is.
asides.any: {member} {checks the suit's own clock and lets it run|does not interrupt|keeps their hands where they can be seen}

choices.text: Let them finish. However long it takes.
Ask about the second beacon.
Read the suit before believing any of it.

a1_beacon.text:
The second beacon has never been switched on because switching it on is the end of the arrangement, and the arrangement is the only thing out here that has been keeping to its side.
What the arrangement is takes {nine minutes|the rest of the hour|a while} to explain and is not madness, which is the part that costs everybody sleep. It is also, in its own terms, {holding|working|entirely stable}, and the party is now the third party to it.

a1_suit.text:
The suit is {two generations|a generation|three generations} old and the person in it is the right shape for it and is breathing at the right rate and is, on every reading anybody can take through a faceplate, alive.
The thing that is wrong is the hands. They have been in the same position for the whole hour, including through {two|three} gestures that should have moved them, and once that is noticed the conversation ends very quickly on both sides.

c1_m.text:
It wants what it has always wanted, and it explains this at length, and about {two thirds|halfway|most of the way} through the explanation it stops and asks whether the party would prefer the short version.
The short version is {four words|one sentence|very short}. The long one has been running for {years|a very long time|longer than the shelter has been here} and has not been heard by anybody.

choices.text: The long version. All of it.
The short version.
Neither. Ask what it would take to make it stop wanting it.

c1_short.text:
Four words, and they are ordinary words in an ordinary order, and none of the away team can repeat them afterwards to anybody including each other.
What survives the trip back up is in {leader}'s hands and is very small and is warm. The band is quiet all the way to orbit, which is the first time it has been quiet since the ship arrived.

c1_stop.text:
Nobody has asked it that. It takes {a long pause|a very long pause|the longest pause of the afternoon} to answer, and the answer is a condition, and the condition is small and specific and can actually be met by four people with a shuttle.
It is met. The shelter goes quiet {that evening|within the hour|before the ship lifts} and stays quiet, and the band it was using is clear for the first time in {years|a decade|a long while}.

choices.text: Cut into the pressure hull.
Follow the cable running out of the wreck.
Strip the wreck and leave.

n0.emText:
A distress carrier that has outlived two power plants, running out of a hull lying on {ground} like a piece of junk dumped on the rocks.
It is very tidy inside. That is the thing about wrecks that have been thought about: they are always tidier than the people who left them.
n0.bubba: Bubba pats the hull like a man patting a horse. "She's been dead a long time an' she's still hollerin'. Overo? That's somebody's mamma callin' 'em in for tea."

a.text: {You torch through the main hatch.|Cutting through the emergency airlock reveals the cargo deck.|Prying the blast doors open gives access to the hold.} {The interior smells of stale nitrogen and rusted plating.|Dead electronics and frozen condensation coat every surface.|Emergency lighting flickers in the gloom.}

choices.text: Open the locker.
Take the log recorder and go.

b.text: {Climbing into the upper superstructure brings you to the transmitter mast.|The access ladder leads directly to the beacon housing.|You scramble up the outer hull toward the antenna array.} {The beacon is buzzing loudly, radiating a greasy electromagnetic field.|Sparks spit from the damaged dish.|The transmitter is running hot despite the sub-zero cold.}

choices.text: Cut the mast down and take the core.
Point the mast at the ship and listen.

c.text:
The team works the wreck the way a wreck is meant to be worked: panels off, cells out, anything with a serial number into the bags. {It goes quickly.|It goes quickly enough.}
Halfway through, {instrument} shows {a second heat source|a second source of heat} under the hull.

choices.text: Dig it out.
Take what is in the bags and lift.

a1.text: {The seal gives.|The seal lets go.} Whatever the crew shut in there had been waiting with the patience of a thing that does not need to breathe, and it comes out at {leader} first.

a2.text:
The recorder comes out with its casing intact. Two hundred hours of watch reports, {and then|then|and after that} one voice, on the last day, saying that the ship is not where the ship thinks it is.
{Nobody|No one} opens the locker. The team is back aboard inside the hour.

b1.text: The core comes out of the mast {in one piece|whole|in a single piece}, heavier than it has any business being, and the distress carrier stops the moment it is clear of the housing. The silence afterwards is the loudest thing on the recording.

b2.text:
Turned around, the mast plays back the last {many} seconds of everything the away team has said, in their own voices, before they have finished saying it.
{leader} calls the walk short. The team comes up shaken and one of them will not talk about it.

c1.text: Under the hull is a reactor {the size of a barrel|no bigger than a barrel}, still lit, still governed, and salvage of that quality does not come along {twice|two separate times} in a career.

c2.text: The bags come up heavy with {cells, plate and cable|cells, plate, cable}. {Nobody|No one} looks at the second heat source again, and the ship is out of the system before anybody decides they should have.

c1_m.text:
Under the hull is a reactor {the size of a barrel|no bigger than a barrel}, still lit, still governed, and salvage of that quality does not come along {twice|two separate times} in a career.
It is also bolted to something. Not to the ship: through the ship, into whatever is under it, by somebody who had the tools and the time and did it {after|well after|a long time after} the crash.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Somebody moored a reactor to this rock.|That is not salvage, that is an installation.|Bolted down. After. Think about that.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts a light on the bolts|steps back a pace without deciding to|counts the fixings}

choices.text: Cut the bolts and take it.
Read the installation before touching it.
Leave it lit. Take the bags and lift.

c1_read.text:
It is not a salvage job, it is a power station: the reactor feeds a run of cable that goes down into the ground, and the run is {four hundred metres|a long way|further than the survey covers} and is still carrying.
Whatever is at the other end has had power for as long as this wreck has been here. The party can take the reactor, or follow the cable, and there is no honest way to do both in the daylight available.

c1_arc.text:
The first bolt comes off fine. The second one is not a bolt: it is a conductor, and it has been at potential for {years|a very long time|the whole of the wreck's stay here}.
The arc takes the cutter, the glove and about {four hours|the rest of the shift|half a day} out of everybody's afternoon. The reactor stays exactly where it is, humming, unimpressed.

b1_m.text:
The core comes out of the mast {in one piece|whole|in a single piece}, heavier than it has any business being, and the distress carrier stops the moment it is clear of the housing.
The silence afterwards is {four seconds|a few seconds|brief}, and then the mast starts again, on the same carrier, with no core in it.

choices.text: Take the core and go. Quickly.
Find out what is driving the mast now.
Put the core back.

b1_drive.text:
Nothing on the ship is driving it. The mast is being driven from {somewhere else|off-hull|a bearing}, and the bearing is {a hundred and eleven degrees|fixed|constant} and does not move with the sky, which means it is not orbital and it is not far.
That bearing is worth more than the core, and the party has both, and the walk back to the shuttle is done facing the right way the entire time.

b1_back.text:
The core goes back into the housing and seats with {a click|a noise|a sound} that is far too satisfied for a piece of hardware.
The carrier changes. It is the same signal and it is now {stronger|considerably stronger|going somewhere}, and the away team is off the wreck inside {four minutes|no time at all|two minutes} and does not discuss it until orbit.

choices.text: Match its depth and hold.
Go below it and look up.
Grapple it and haul it up.

n0.emText:
No ground. The signal holds station at a fixed depth in {place} hovering dead still in the atmosphere.
You take the capsule down and the atmosphere closes over the ports at nine kilometres, and it does not feel like sinking. It feels like a lift going down into a building that has more basements than it has floors.
n0.bubba: "Nine kilometres," says Bubba, watching the ports go dark. "An' still goin'. Sto' palazzo tene troppe cantine, sugar."

a.text: {Descending through the atmospheric soup, the shape resolves:|Dropping lower through the clouds, you spot it:|Sensors clear up as you approach:} {an intact station|a massive floating platform|a floating industrial rig}, not a wreck, {anchored directly in the dense gas layers|holding station against the hurricane winds|silently humming with backup power}.

choices.text: Dock.
Photograph everything and climb out.

b.text: Below it the pressure is at the capsule's rating and the view up is {worth it|worth the rating}: the thing is not floating. It is standing on a column of something that goes down past the capsule, past the sounder's range, {past any floor this world has|past any bottom this world has}.

choices.text: Follow the column down.
{Take a sample|Collect a specimen|Scrape off a sample|Bag a piece} of the column and go.

c.text:
The grapple takes hold on the {second|third|first} pass. Whatever it is masses far less than it should and comes up easily for {six|five|seven} kilometres.
At six kilometres it stops coming, and the winch keeps running, and the cable keeps paying in.

choices.text: Keep winching.
Cut the cable.

a1.text: The dock takes the capsule like it was built for it, because it was. Inside there is air, and gravity, and a single corridor with a door at the end of it, and the door opens for {leader} and for {nobody|no one} else.

a2.text: Two hundred frames of a floating city that {nobody|no one} will believe, and a rise back through {hazard} that takes {many} hours and costs a heat shield.

b1.text: The capsule goes past its rating on the way to finding out what the column stands on. It comes back up with {two ports crazed|both ports crazed}, one crew member's ribs gone, and the answer, which {nobody|no one} has been able to write down.

b2.text: The sample arm comes back with three grams of the column in the pot, and the pot weighs {many} kilos, {and it is still cooling|and it has not finished cooling}.

c1.text: What comes up on the end of the cable is {not what the grapple took hold of|nothing like what the grapple took hold of}.

c2.text: The cutter takes the cable and the capsule goes up {like a cork|the way a cork goes up}. Snagged in the last metre of cable, still attached, is a plate of something that will not scratch.

a1_m.text:
The dock takes the capsule like it was built for it, because it was, and inside there is air, and gravity, and a single corridor with a door at the end of it.
The corridor is {ninety metres|long|longer than the platform looked from outside}, and the door at the end of it opens for {leader} and for nobody else, and everybody has a good deal of time to think about that on the walk down.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{It opened for one of us. One.|Do not go through alone.|A door that knows which of us is which.}"
asides.any: {member} {walks the corridor with a hand on the wall|counts the paces|puts a wedge in the airlock behind them}

choices.text: Go through the door.
Send the whole team through at once, door or no door.
Read the corridor before going any further down it.

a1_all.text:
Four people go through a door that opens for one, which it permits, in the sense that it does not stop them.
What is on the other side is arranged for one person and does not rearrange. Everybody comes back out. {Three of them|The other three|Three} agree about what was in there and the fourth does not, and the fourth is {leader}.

a1_corr.text:
Paced and measured, the corridor is {longer inside than the platform is across|four metres longer than the hull allows|not a length the outside of this thing can contain}, and the discrepancy is constant rather than growing, which makes it a fact rather than a fault.
The door opens. What is behind it is what was always behind it, and the party goes in knowing exactly how much of this platform is not on the outside of it, which is the difference between a find and a survey.

b2_m.text:
The sample arm comes back with three grams of the column in the pot, and the pot weighs {many} kilos, and it is still cooling.
While it cools, the column does something it has not done in the {forty minutes|hour|while} the capsule has been under it: it {narrows|draws in|closes} by about a metre, from the bottom up, at the rate a thing moves when it has noticed something.

choices.text: Take the pot and climb, now.
Put the three grams back.
Hold position and watch it come.

b2_back.text:
Three grams go back out of the pot and onto the column, which is {harder|considerably harder|a great deal more fiddly} than taking them off was, and the column stops narrowing before the arm is fully retracted.
The capsule climbs out with an empty pot, two hundred frames of the column, and the single most useful piece of information anybody has ever brought back off this world, which is that it can be asked.

b2_watch.text:
Holding still while something the size of a weather system closes on the capsule is a decision that has to be made {four|five|several} separate times as it gets nearer.
It stops {nine metres|a hundred metres|short}, and holds, and for {eleven minutes|a quarter of an hour|some time} the two of them sit there. What is recorded in those minutes will be argued about by people who were not there for the rest of the party's lives.

n0.text:
{The heat here will cook you alive in seconds.|The heat here will melt your suit seals in seconds.|The heat here will scorch your eyebrows off in seconds.|Thermal sensors are screaming at maximum.|The surface temperature is completely unhinged.} {The signal is transmitting out of the hottest point on the sweep.|Something is broadcasting directly from the center of the magma field.|A beacon is screaming from inside the hottest vent.}
The cool phase is on a cycle, and the cycle is {regular|exact|good to the minute}, which nothing on this rock has any business being.

choices.text: Go in with the suit at full cooling.
Send the drone in and stay out.
Wait for the cool phase.

n0.emText:
The heat here would finish an argument in under a second and something is transmitting out of the hottest point on the survey.
It's not hiding from the fire. It is plugged into it, the way a chip shop is plugged into a street: this is where the power is, so this is where you put your business.
n0.bubba: Bubba checks the suit seals four times, which for Bubba is a panic attack. "Somethin' down there's usin' the fire like a stove. Cucina, insomma."

a.text: {Approaching the magma vent, the radiation counters spike violently.|Heat shields glow cherry red as you push closer to the source.|The ground crunches like breaking glass under your boots.} {At the center of the caldera sits a glowing cylinder, totally unfazed by the lava.|The source is a solid metal beacon submerged in molten rock.|An alloy housing sits in the middle of the magma flow.}

choices.text: Reach out to it.
Get out while the suit still holds.

b.text:
The drone lasts {few} minutes, which is three and a half more than expected, and sends back a picture of {remnant} standing in the fire, unmarked.
Then something takes the drone. Gently. The signal ends without breaking up.

choices.text: Go and get the drone back.
Log it as lost.

c.text:
The cool phase comes {many} hours later and lasts {lots} minutes, and the team walks in over ground that is merely lethal.
The source is a cavity, and the cavity is lined, and the lining is not natural.

choices.text: Strip the lining.
Get inside the cavity.

a1.text: The glove does not burn. Something's put into it, {deliberately|on purpose}, by something with no hands, and {leader} walks out of the heat carrying an object that is cold.

a2.text: The suit holds all the way out and fails in the airlock, which is {the best possible place|the one good place} for a suit to fail. The scans taken on the way are worth the replacement.

b1.text: The drone is at the edge of the heat, {set down facing outwards|set down with its face turned outwards}, with its recorder full and its casing packed with something that should not exist at that temperature.

b2.text: The loss goes in the log with the rest of the year's losses. The {few} minutes of footage get {quietly|without fuss} copied by three separate people before the ship reaches the next system.

c1.text: It peels off in sheets, {light as foil|as light as foil}, and every sheet holds temperature like it has an opinion about it. There is enough here to line a ship.

c2.text: The cavity is occupied, and the cool phase is not a phase. {It is a habit|It is a habit of the place}, and the away team has just walked into the middle of it.

c1_m.text:
The lining peels off in sheets, {light as foil|as light as foil}, and every sheet holds temperature like it has an opinion about it. There is enough here to line a ship.
Under the third layer the sheets stop being blank. There is work on the back of them: {figures|lines|a pattern}, repeated, and the repetition runs across sheets, which means the whole cavity is one surface saying one thing.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{We are stripping a page.|That is writing and we are selling it as insulation.|Somebody is going to want the order these came off in.}"
asides.any: {member} {starts numbering the sheets as they come off|photographs the cavity before another sheet moves|stops peeling}

choices.text: Keep stripping. It is worth more as plate.
Number every sheet and take the lining in order.
Stop. Take four sheets and leave the rest standing.

c1_order.text:
Numbering {a hundred and forty|a great many|every} sheets as they come off a cavity wall in a suit at full cooling adds {three hours|half a day|most of a shift} to a job that was already at the edge of the suit's endurance.
Reassembled on a hangar floor it is one continuous document, and it is not a language, and it is readable anyway, which is the part that takes {two years|a long time|several careers} to explain.

c1_four.text:
Four sheets, taken from the top layer where nothing is written, and the cavity left standing with its wall intact.
It is a fraction of what could have been carried out and it is enough to line a cockpit, and the party is the only crew who will ever be able to say that they found that cavity and left it whole, which turns out to matter {later|a great deal, later|to somebody}.

b1_m.text:
The drone is at the edge of the heat, {set down facing outwards|set down with its face turned outwards}, with its recorder full and its casing packed with something that should not exist at that temperature.
It has also been repaired. The rotor arm that was cracked on the way in is not cracked, and the repair is {better than the original|neat|done with material that is not in the drone's manifest}.

choices.text: Pick it up and get out of the heat.
Look at the repair properly before touching the casing.
Leave it. Send a second drone to watch the first.

b1_fix.text:
The repair is not a repair in any sense a workshop would recognise. The arm has been {grown back|continued|finished}, out of the same alloy, in the same section, with the crack closed from the inside.
Whatever did it was working from the drone's own structure as a specification. What that implies about the {remnant} standing unmarked in the fire is the single most valuable paragraph in the ship's report that year.

b1_hot.text:
The casing is picked up at the edge of a heat that is {coming back|rising|not staying where it was}, and the suit's timer becomes the only thing anybody is listening to.
Everybody gets out. The drone gets out. What is packed in the casing does not survive the pressure change at the lock, and what is left is {a stain|a residue|three grams of glass} and a recorder full of very good footage.

b1_watch.text:
The second drone flies a slow orbit at the edge of the heat for {four hours|the rest of the phase|as long as its cells hold} with its camera on the first one.
Nothing comes for it. At {the end of the fourth hour|the end of the phase|dusk} the first drone stands up on its own gear, turns to face the second, and holds that position until the cells run out.

n0.text:
{A graveyard of {vessel} hulls scattered across {ground}.|Dozens of dead {vessel} wrecks littering the area.|A junkyard of broken hulls rusting on {ground}.} {Nobody came back for them.|Every single one was stripped of parts years ago.|It's basically a monument to bad piloting.} {instrument} flags {one ship with a live signature|a faint power reading in the largest wreck|a working distress transponder in the rubble}.
The hulls are laid out in rows. Not scattered: {rows|ranks|lines}, with room between them for something to pass down.

choices.text: Board the oldest.
Board the newest.
Find out who does the sweeping.

n0.emText:
{many} ships moored in a row at {place}, none of them from any registry the ship carries, all of them parked rather than wrecked.
Somebody sweeps between them. It is a car park. It is a residents' car park on a world with no residents, and the bays are marked, and yours is not one of them.
n0.bubba: Bubba counts the moorings. "They's all parked nice. Nisciuno ha parcheggiato malamente. That's the part I don't like."

a.text:
The oldest is stone, or something that has become stone, and its hatch is a hole cut {by hand|by somebody's hand} from the outside.
The inside is one room, {and the room is a nest|and the room has been made into a nest}, and it has been used since long after the ship stopped flying.

choices.text: Search the nest.
Wait outside for whatever lives there.

b.text:
The newest has been here {many} years by its own clock and its hull is in better order than the party's own ship.
The crew log ends {on the day they arrived|the day they arrived|on their day of arrival}, mid-sentence, in the middle of a supply count.

choices.text: Take the ship's stores.
Try to bring the ship back up.

c.text:
The sweeping is done {at a set hour|to a set hour|on the hour, every time}, and the away team is in cover for it.
What comes out to sweep is small, and old, and does the whole anchorage in {ninety minutes|an hour and a half}, and stops at each ship to check the mooring line.

choices.text: Offer it a mooring line of your own.
Follow it home.

a1.text: Under the bedding there are {few} hundred small objects, {sorted by size|graded by size|laid out by size}, and every one of them came off a different ship. The best of them is the last one in the row.

a2.text: {It comes home at the end of its round|It comes back at the end of its round} and it is not pleased to find the door open.

b1.text: {many} years of stores, packed by people who {knew what they were doing|knew the work}, and the away team takes as much as the lander will lift.

b2.text:
The reactor lights on the {third|second|fourth} try and the ship comes up all the way, every board green, {and then|then|and after that} it will not release the moorings, and nothing on any panel explains why.
It is put back to sleep. It goes willingly.

c1.text: It takes the line, tests it, coils it {properly|correctly}, and moors the lander with it, {and then|then|and after that} it hands {leader} the thing it has been carrying since the first ship arrived.

c2.text: Home is a hole under the anchorage, and inside it is every mooring line that has ever failed, {spliced back together|spliced whole again}, and the tools that did the splicing.

b2_m.text:
The reactor lights on the {third|second|fourth} try and the ship comes up all the way, every board green, and for {four minutes|a few minutes|a while} it is the most alive thing on this rock.
Then it will not release the moorings. Not a fault: the release is powered, and healthy, and it is being {held|refused|answered with a no} from somewhere that is not the bridge.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{The ship does not want to go.|Something else has the moorings.|Every board green and it will not slip a line.}"
asides.any: {member} {goes and looks at the moorings from the outside|reads the release circuit twice|puts a hand on the console and leaves it there}

choices.text: Cut the moorings and lift.
Find out what is holding them.
Shut it back down and leave it as it was.

b2_hold.text:
The release circuit has been {spliced|extended|run out} through the hull and down into the anchorage, and at the other end of the splice, under the ground, something is holding a switch open.
It is the sweeper's work: the splice is the same splice that mends every failed line in the yard. The ship is not impounded. It is {being looked after|moored properly|kept}, and the party is the first crew in years to understand that.

b2_burn.text:
The circuit is traced with the reactor up, which is how the party learns that the splice is carrying, and the tester goes {black|out|to slag} in one hand.
The moorings are cut in the end anyway. The ship lifts on somebody else's mooring lines trailing off it, and the yard is {four hulls|one hull|a row} shorter and considerably less friendly to the next crew that lands there.

b2_down.text:
Every board green, and then every board off, in the correct order, by somebody who takes the {twenty minutes|quarter of an hour|time} to do the shutdown properly rather than pulling the breaker.
The hull is left exactly as found with the log closed and the hatch dogged. {Nine days|A fortnight|Some time} later, out on the band, a carrier comes up on the yard's frequency and says thank you in a format that stopped being used {a century|a very long time} ago.

c2_m.text:
Home is a hole under the anchorage, and it takes {an hour|the whole of the sweep|some following} to get to and is not hidden so much as simply not looked at.
Inside is every mooring line that has ever failed in this yard, {spliced back together|spliced whole again}, coiled, hung in order, and at the back there is a rack with {four|five} empty hooks on it and the labels still under them.

choices.text: Take the tools and go.
Read the labels on the empty hooks.
Leave a line of our own on an empty hook.

c2_hooks.text:
The labels are ship names and the ships are in the yard, and the four with empty hooks are the four hulls that are {stone|oldest|not from anywhere the party's tables recognise}.
It has not mended their lines. It cannot: their lines are not line. What it has been doing instead, for as long as the yard has existed, is waiting for somebody to bring it something it can splice, and the party is carrying {several hundred metres|plenty|exactly that}.

c2_hang.text:
A coil of the party's own line goes on an empty hook, properly, with a whipping on the end, which takes {ten minutes|a quarter of an hour|longer than it looks}.
Nothing happens while anybody is watching. The lander's own moorings, checked at dawn out of habit, have been {re-tied|redone|reworked} to a standard nobody aboard could match, and there is something coiled on the ramp that was not there at dusk.

n0.text:
{The ground underfoot sounds hollow, like walking on a rusted tin roof.|Subsurface radar shows massive empty cavities directly below {place}.|The crust here is paper-thin and honeycombed with tunnels.} {Something is broadcasting from sixty meters down.|A clear transmission is pulsing from inside the subterranean void.|Audio sensors pick up metallic clicks echoing from below.}
The cavities are not random. Laid out on the survey they make a shape, and the shape has {one axis of symmetry|a symmetry|an axis}.

choices.text: Go down the shaft.
Sound the whole body first.
Blow the shaft wider and send the drone.

n0.emText:
The body weighs a third of what it should and the survey pulse comes back off an inside face.
It is a shell with a room in it. Every so often the universe turns out to have been built by a landlord: a nice frontage, and behind the frontage a stairwell with somebody living in it.
n0.bubba: "A shell," says Bubba, kicking the collar of the shaft. "'Nu palazzo cu 'na sola scala. Somebody's home, sugar, an' the door's open."

a.text:
{few} hundred metres of shaft, {and then|then|and after that} it opens out. The inside of the body is a single space with a floor curving up on all sides, and it is not empty.
There is weather in here. There should not be weather in here.

choices.text: Cross to the middle.
Keep to the wall and map it.

b.text:
Sounding takes {a day|a whole day|two days} and turns up the shape of it: chambers, and passages between chambers, and one chamber that returns nothing at all, {as though the pulse goes in and stays|as though the pulse goes in and does not come out}.
{wrongness}.

choices.text: Open the silent chamber.
Mine the ones that answered.

c.text: The charge opens the collar and the drone goes down with the light on. It sends back {many} minutes of an interior {nobody|no one} will ever be allowed to visit, {and then|then|and after that} its telemetry ends mid-frame, without any of the usual warnings.

choices.text: Go down after it.
Sell the footage and never come back.

a1.text: At the middle is the thing the whole body was built around, hanging at the centre of gravity, {turning slowly|turning, slowly|turning at a walking pace}, and it lets {leader} take one piece of itself without any argument at all.

a2.text: The map takes {six|five|eight} hours and is worth every minute: a complete interior survey of an artificial world, with the machinery of it laid bare along the wall like an anatomy.

b1.text: {It's not a chamber.|That is not a chamber.} It is an occupant, and it has been folded into that space for longer than the body has been in this orbit, and it unfolds.

b2.text: {The answering chambers are stores|The chambers that answered are stores}, and the stores are full, and whoever packed them expected to come back for them.

c1.text: The drone is {lots} metres down, undamaged, and pointing back up the shaft. Something set it down {carefully|with care}, and put something next to it, and left.

c2.text: {many} minutes of the inside of a hollow world sells for {what a small moon sells for|the price of a small moon}. The buyer does not give a name and does not haggle. That tells you enough.

a1_m.text:
Crossing to the middle of a hollow world means crossing {four hundred metres|a long way|the width of the inside} of floor that curves up on all sides, in the dark, with the lamps only reaching so far.
Halfway across, the lamps pick up the crossing point of {two|three} other sets of tracks, all of them heading the same way, all of them {old|very old|older than the survey}, and none of them coming back.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Three lots in. None out.|Nobody has ever walked back across this floor.|We are not the first and the first are still here.}"
asides.any: {member} {takes a bearing back to the shaft and writes it on a glove|counts the sets|does not stop walking}

choices.text: Keep going to the middle.
Follow the oldest set of tracks instead.
Lay a line back to the shaft before going another metre.

a1_old.text:
The oldest set does not go to the middle. It goes {three quarters of the way|most of the way|nearly there} and then turns and walks a circle round it, twice, and then goes back to the wall at a different point from the shaft.
At that point in the wall there is a hatch, and the hatch is on the inside of a world that nobody built a door into, and it opens.

a1_line.text:
Four hundred metres of line paid out across a floor that curves up on all sides, anchored at both ends, which takes {an hour|a long time|most of the air budget}.
The thing at the middle lets {leader} take what {leader} takes, exactly as it would have anyway. The difference is that the walk back is a walk rather than {a search|four hours of lamps|the rest of everybody's air}, and everybody is standing on the ramp before dark.

c1_m.text:
The drone is {lots} metres down, undamaged, and pointing back up the shaft. Something set it down {carefully|with care}, and put something next to it, and left.
The something next to it is {the size of a fist|small|about the size of a helmet} and is the only object in the whole interior that is not part of the interior, and it has been placed where a drone's camera would see it.

choices.text: Take it and climb out.
Photograph everything about how it was placed first.
Put something of ours next to it and leave both.

c1_place.text:
It has been placed at the drone's focal distance, squared to the lens, on a surface that was {swept|cleared|prepared} first. Everything about the placement is an answer to a camera.
Which means it was left for whoever sent the drone rather than for whoever finds it, and that is a different object entirely, and it is worth reporting as one.

c1_swap.text:
A tool off the party's own belt, set down at the same focal distance, squared to the same lens, on the same swept surface.
The drone is left running. It sends for {eleven hours|most of a day|a long time} and then stops, and what it sent in the last four minutes is the reason the ship stays in this system another {fortnight|three weeks|month}.

n0.text:
{The scanner is picking up an exact duplicate of {vessel}'s transponder signature.|Something down on {ground} is broadcasting our exact ship ID and callsign.|Sensor telemetry is mirroring our own ship data with zero delay.} {It's either a severe sensor glitch, a very weird relay, or someone trying to mock us.|Either the electronics are fried, or something down there is copying our homework.}
The duplicate signature is not identical. It is {half a second|a fraction|slightly} ahead, and the gap has been closing since the lander touched.

choices.text: Follow the other team's tracks.
Set up and wait for them to arrive.
Talk to them on the suit channel.

n0.emText:
Your own suit telemetry, five channels, correct headers, correct names, arriving from {place} {many} minutes before you land there.
Somebody has already done this. Someone's doing it now, slightly ahead, wearing your headers. You are the last person in this universe entitled to be squeamish about a copy of a woman turning up where the original has not arrived yet.
n0.bubba: Bubba looks at the telemetry and then at you and puts his hand on your shoulder. "Whatever's wearin' our names down there, it ain't us. Ricordatelo. Whatever it says."

a.text:
The tracks are the away team's own boots, in the away team's own sizes, laid down in {ground} before the lander touched.
They lead away from the landing site, do everything the team is about to do, and stop.

choices.text: Walk to where they stop.
Do something the tracks did not do.

b.text:
{They arrive on schedule|They arrive exactly on schedule}, from the direction the telemetry said, five of them, in the same suits, walking the way the away team walks.
They stop {lots} metres out and wait to be spoken to.

choices.text: Trade with them.
Do not let them any closer.

c.text:
The channel is open both ways and the voice on it is {leader}'s, half a second early, getting every word right before it is said.
It asks the away team not to come to {place}. It is {very|remarkably} calm about it.

choices.text: Ask what happens there.
Go there.

a1.text: Where they stop there is a cache, packed by people {with the same hands|whose hands were the same as theirs}, and a note in {leader}'s handwriting that says only: it is worth it, take it, do not stay.

a2.text:
{leader} sits down in {ground} and refuses to move for {few} minutes, out of spite.
It works. The tracks stop being ahead of them. Everything since landing has to be done again, {properly|correctly}, and the team is tired in a way sleep does not touch.

b1.text: They trade fairly, and hard, and they know {exactly|precisely} what the team can spare, which is the most frightening thing about the whole exchange.

b2.text: {They come closer.|They come closer than that.}

c1.text: It tells them. It takes {four|three|five} minutes and the team does not go, and on the walk back the voice thanks them, once, and stops half a second before it should.

c2.text: At {place} there is nothing but {remnant} and a {very|remarkably} clear view, and everybody comes back, and the count is right, and the ship's log will record that the count was right.

b1_m.text:
They trade fairly, and hard, and they know {exactly|precisely} what the team can spare, which is the most frightening thing about the whole exchange.
What they offer for it is {four|five} items, laid out on a sheet, and one of them is something the party has not lost yet: it is on somebody's belt right now, and there is a second one on the sheet.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Do not pick that up.|That is mine. That is on me. Now.|They are trading us our own week.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts a hand over their own belt|counts the items on the sheet twice|steps back off the sheet}

choices.text: Trade. Take all four.
Take everything except the duplicate.
Ask how they came by the one that is still on our belt.

b1_three.text:
Three items off the sheet and the fourth left lying there, which they accept without comment and without picking it up.
It is still on the sheet when the party looks back from {two hundred metres|the ridge|a distance}, and the sheet is still there the next day, and the day after that it is not, and neither is the thing on it, and neither is the one that was on the belt.

b1_ask.text:
The question is asked plainly and the answer is given plainly, which is the only time either side does that: they came by it the same way the party is about to come by it, which is {backwards|from the other end|in the order they are standing in}.
The trade is completed. Both parties walk away. On the way back to the lander {member} works out what the answer means and has to sit down on {ground} for a minute, and does not explain.

c2_m.text:
At {place} there is nothing but {remnant} and a {very|remarkably} clear view, and the walk out to it takes {two hours|the afternoon|longer than the map says}.
The view is clear in every direction including the one the party came from, and from here it is possible to see the lander, and the away team's own tracks, and {five|four} figures at the lander who are not there yet.

choices.text: Walk back. Count everybody at the ramp.
Stay at {place} until the figures are gone.
Watch them through the glass and work out what they are doing.

c2_wait.text:
Sitting at {place} with a clear view for {four hours|the rest of the light|a long time}, watching a lander that has four people at it and four people walking towards it and four people sitting on a ridge.
The figures at the lander go inside at dusk. The party walks back in the dark, finds the hatch dogged from inside, and opens it, and there is nobody aboard and the kettle is warm.

c2_watch.text:
Through the glass, at {four kilometres|that distance|a long way}, the five of them are doing exactly what the party did at landing: the same checks, in the same order, with the same one going round the gear twice.
And then one of them stops, and turns, and looks up at {place}, at the ridge, at the glass. The party leaves before the others arrive. The ship's log records a clean departure and a crew count that is right.

n0.text:
{The transponder signal is moving fast across {ground}, heading on a direct intercept course.|Something is tracking us, carrying an obsolete distress beacon as bait.|A fast-moving radar contact is closing the distance across {place}.} {It's not broadcasting for help; it's using the signal to hunt.|Whatever's carrying that beacon definitely isn't a stranded crew member.}
The beacon it is carrying was logged as destroyed {eleven years|a decade|a long time} ago, with the wreck, with everybody aboard.

choices.text: {Set an ambush|Take cover and wait|Hide behind the rocks|Prepare an ambush} and wait for it.
{Circle round|Flank it from behind|Sneak up on its blind side|Come around the back} and come at it from behind.
{Broadcast on the same frequency|Hail them on the open band|Answer the signal|Open a comms channel}.

n0.emText:
A ship-standard transponder on a frequency nobody has used in decades, moving over {ground} on a line that will cross yours.
It stops when you stop. It has done this before and it has done it enough times to have got polite about it, the way a man following you home keeps a consistent distance so that neither of you has to say anything.
n0.bubba: "It stopped when we stopped," says Bubba. "Aoh. Nun e' curiosa. It's got a method."

a.text:
{Two hours|Three hours|An hour and a half} in cover at {place}. The transponder comes on at last light and it is being carried, not worn, by something the size of a lander leg that moves {like it has all the time in the world|as though nothing is chasing it}.
It is dragging a net, and the net is full.

choices.text: {Take the shot|Open fire|Pull the trigger|Shoot first}.
{Let it pass|Hold fire and wait|Stay hidden until it moves on|Let it walk by} and follow the net.

b.text:
{Coming at it from behind works|Coming up behind it works}, in that the team gets to see it before it sees them.
It is sitting in a scrape it has made for itself, and it is surrounded by suit helmets, arranged in a circle, {all facing inwards|every one facing inwards}.

choices.text: Take a helmet.
Back off quietly.

c.text:
{leader} keys the old frequency and says the standard hail.
The answer is the standard reply, word perfect, in {leader}'s own voice, and it is coming from {about|something like|roughly} sixty metres away.

choices.text: {Answer it again|Send another reply|Hail them back|Repeat the response}.
{Go to it|Approach the source|Move in closer|Head toward the signal}.

a1.text: {The first shot is good|The first shot goes exactly where it should} and does nothing at all except make it put the net down.

a2.text: It drags the net to a cache under an overhang and {stows it with the others|puts it away with the others}. There are {lots} years of others. The team lifts one and is gone before it comes back.

b1.text: There is a name {stencilled|stencilled in paint} inside the helmet and a recorder still in the collar with {many} seconds on it. Getting out with both is the hardest walking anyone does that year.

b2.text: {Nobody|No one} speaks until the lander hatch is shut. The transponder is still moving out there, and the ship logs the position, and marks the whole hemisphere as {a place to not go back to|somewhere nobody returns to}.

c1.text:
{Three|Four|Two} exchanges and it runs out of recorded phrases and starts making its own, badly, and the badness is what everybody remembers.
It leaves. It leaves a thing behind, on {ground}, halfway between.

c2.text: It has been waiting {a long time|a good while|longer than anybody says} for {somebody|someone} to walk towards it.

a2_m.text:
It drags the net past the cover at {four metres|close range|arm's length} and does not look, and keeps going, and the team gets to breathe again about a minute later.
It stows the net at a cache under an overhang, with the others. There are {lots} years of others, and they are stacked in date order, and the oldest ones at the back have been {opened|gone through|sorted} and the newest have not.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{It is keeping them for something.|Date order. That is a collection.|Nothing hunts and then files.}"
asides.any: {member} {reads the dates off the outside of the nets|lifts one and finds it heavier than expected|works out how many years are in the stack}

choices.text: Lift one and be gone.
Open the oldest one, at the back.
Work out what order it is actually keeping them in.

a2_old.text:
The oldest net has been opened before and closed again, carefully, and what is in it has been {arranged|laid out|sorted} rather than stored.
It is a crew. All of it, every member, with each person's own kit beside them in the order they wore it. The team lifts nothing from that one. What they lift instead is {the log|a plate|the name}, which is enough to close a file that has been open for a decade.

a2_order.text:
Not date order. {Size|Mass|Weight} order, and inside that, date order, and the whole stack is graded so finely that the gaps in it are as legible as the contents.
There are {three|four} gaps. Three nets have been taken out of this cache and not put back, by something that is not the one with the beacon, and that is the most useful thing anybody has learned on this rock.

b1_m.text:
Getting to the helmet means {four metres|crossing the scrape|going in} while it is sitting in its own hollow doing something with its hands that nobody wants described.
There is a name {stencilled|stencilled in paint} inside the helmet and a recorder still in the collar. There is also, under the helmet, a second one, and a third, and the pile goes down further than the light does.

choices.text: Take the top helmet and get out.
Take the recorder out of every helmet you can reach.
Read the names without moving anything.

b1_all.text:
{Nine|Eleven|Seven} recorders out of {nine|eleven|seven} collars, one at a time, by touch, with something breathing {four metres|a few feet|not far enough} away.
The eighth one clicks. What happens after the click is four minutes long and is the reason two of the party will not go first through a hatch ever again, and everybody gets out, and the recorders come with them.

b1_names.text:
The names are read off {four|five} collars without a finger being laid on any of them, which takes patience and a good light and the willingness to lie still in a scrape.
They are all off the same ship and the ship is {one the party has heard of|on the registry|not a wreck: it is listed as in service}. The last part is what they carry out of there, and it is worth more than any of the helmets.

n0.text:
{place} holds {an abandoned town|a ruined settlement|a cluster of collapsed stone buildings}. {Streets, broken drains, a central square, and {remnant} sitting in the middle.|A crumbling ghost town where nobody has lived for centuries.|Toppled archways and cracked stone foundations under a dead sky.}
Nothing here fell down. Every building that is open is open because {a wall was taken out|somebody removed a wall|it was opened}, from the inside, {neatly|carefully|without hurry}.

choices.text: Go into the largest building.
{Follow the drains|Head down the drain tunnels|Climb down into the drainage conduit|Follow the sewer pipe} down.
Read the square.

n0.emText:
Streets, drains, a square, and {remnant} where a monument would go. Nothing burned. Nothing fell. They stopped, all at once, like a market at closing.
You walk down a road that was built to be walked down and every doorway you pass is the right size for you, which is either a coincidence or the single most frightening piece of information available on this world.
n0.bubba: Bubba stands in the middle of the square and turns round slowly. "Doors are our size. Steps are our size. Chi ll'ha fatte, sti scale?"

a.text:
It is a hall, and it is full of seats facing a stage, and on the stage is a machine that has been running the same {six|four|nine} seconds of something for as long as it has had power.
{Every seat is occupied.|Every seat in the hall is occupied.} They are not bodies. They are the shapes bodies leave in a room that has not been disturbed.

choices.text: Let the machine finish.
{Take the machine|Dismantle the device|Haul the hardware back|Pry the machine loose}.

b.text:
The drains are {dry, walkable|dry and walkable}, and better built than the streets above them. {Two hundred|Three hundred|A hundred and fifty} metres in they stop being drains and start being a corridor.
{sound}, from further along.

choices.text: {Keep going|Push deeper|Continue forward|Press on}.
Blow the tunnel entrance.

c.text:
{The square is a record.|The square itself is the record.} Every flat surface carries names, and the names are in columns, and the columns are dated, and the dates stop.
{leader} works out the last column is not a list of the dead. It is a rota.

choices.text: Check the names on the wall.
{Copy the record and go|Download the archives and leave|Grab the data and retreat|Log the data and extract}.

a1.text: It takes {nine|seven|eleven} minutes. It is a message, and it is an apology, and at the end of it the seats are empty in a way they were not before, and everybody in the away team feels it happen.

a2.text: It comes off the stage in {few} pieces and every piece is worth more than the lander. The hall is {very|remarkably} quiet on the way out, and the seats are still occupied.

b1.text: The corridor ends at a door that was locked from this side, by hand, {in a hurry|and in a hurry}, and whatever they locked in has had a {very|remarkably} long time to get used to the idea.

b2.text: The charge brings the roof down {neatly|cleanly|square} across the corridor mouth. On the walk back up, the team lifts a plate of worked metal out of the drain wall: a street sign, or a prayer.

c1.text: Whatever needed watching is under the square, it is still there, and the last name on the rota {never got relieved|was never relieved}. The team relieves them, in the only way left, and takes the post's kit up.

c2.text: {many} thousand names in the ship's archive, none of which can be pronounced. {Somebody|Someone} in the crew starts reading them out loud on the trip home, and does not stop.

a1_m.text:
The machine is let run. It takes {nine|seven|eleven} minutes, and it is a message, and it is an apology, and about {two thirds|halfway|most of the way} through it stops being addressed to whoever was in the seats and starts being addressed to whoever would be standing where the party is standing.
It describes them. Not by name: by {number|posture|how many of them there are}, and it is correct.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{It is counting us.|Four. It said four.|That was recorded before anybody here was born.}"
asides.any: {member} {sits down in one of the seats|looks at the empty rows rather than the stage|lets it run}

choices.text: Let it finish and take what it leaves.
Answer it. It is a message; messages are answered.
Stop the machine before the last minute.

a1_reply.text:
Answering a recording is not a sensible act and it is done anyway, in the same construction, in the same order, standing in the aisle with the seats {empty|watching|behind}.
The machine stops before its own ending. It runs a second track that has never been played, which is {four minutes|shorter|much shorter}, and which is not an apology at all, and which is worth carrying home in full.

a1_stop.text:
The machine is stopped with {a hand|a lever|the obvious control} at eight minutes and change, which is the first time in a very long time that anybody has interrupted it.
The hall is {immediately|at once|instantly} a different room. The seats are only seats. On the way out, at the door, the last thing anybody hears is the machine starting again from the beginning, for nobody, exactly as before.

c2_m.text:
Copying the record is {four hours|an afternoon|a long job} of photographing walls, and somewhere in the third hour the columns stop being a rota and start being something else: the dates run past the last name and keep going, in the same hand, {into next year|forward|past today}.
The columns ahead are blank. The headings are not.

choices.text: Copy the lot and go. It is only a record.
Read the headings of the columns that have not happened.
Put a name in the next blank.

c2_head.text:
The headings are duties, and they are ordinary duties: watching, feeding, {turning something|keeping something|the same three verbs}, allocated in a rota that has run without interruption for as long as the square has stood and has {four|three} centuries of blanks ahead of it.
What that implies about the thing under the square is written up on the way home and is the most-read document the Foundation publishes that year.

c2_sign.text:
A name goes in the next blank in the column, in chalk, by somebody who says at the time that it is a joke.
It is still there {a year later|when anybody next checks|in the photographs}, in a hand that is not chalk any more. Nothing comes for anybody. That is the part that is hardest to live with, over the following seasons: nothing comes, and the rota goes on being correct.

n0.text:
{At {place} stands an alien monument that clearly doesn't belong here, completely untouched by the local weather.|There's an intact structure at {place}, looking pristine despite being in the middle of a barren wasteland.|A strange, seamless monolith rises out of {ground}, completely clean of dust or corrosion.}
The step is worn. Not weathered: {walked on|worn by feet|used}, in a place where nothing walks.

choices.text: {Walk in|Step through the entrance|Cross the threshold|Head inside}.
Toss some junk on the step.
Scan it from a safe distance.

n0.emText:
Something at {place} that nothing here could have made and nothing here has touched, and the ground around it swept clean by something that comes back to sweep it.
It is kept. Not worshipped: kept, the way a difficult relative's flat is kept, by somebody who comes round on a Tuesday, does what has to be done, and leaves before dark.
n0.bubba: Bubba puts his hat on, which he does when he is being respectful. "Somebody cleans this. So somebody's comin' back. Nun tuccammo niente 'e sbagliato."

a.text:
The inside is one room and the room is much larger than the outside allows. The far wall is {a long way off|further off than it can be} and there is a queue of {maker} standing at it, with their backs turned, in perfect order.
They have been standing there long enough to have worn {grooves|hollows} into the floor.

choices.text: {Join the queue|Stand in line|Wait your turn|Step into formation}.
{Take something from the wall and run|Grab a relic and sprint for the door|Rip hardware off the wall and bolt|Snatch a piece and retreat}.

b.text:
{leader} puts a ration tin on the step, because it is what there is.
The tin is gone before the team has walked ten paces, and in its place, arranged with care, is a set of tools that are the right size for hands {nobody|no one} aboard has.

choices.text: {Take the tools|Grab the salvage gear|Pocket the equipment|Take the hardware}.
{Leave them and put down something better|Trade for a better offering|Leave a higher-value item|Swap with a better piece of scrap}.

c.text:
{Three hours of scanning|After three hours running the sensors|Three hours of mapping data|Logging sensor sweeps for three hours} from {lots} metres out. The structure has no seams, no foundations, and a mass that changes depending on which way it is measured from.
On the way back, {leader} finds a track in {ground} that goes round the whole site. It is fresh.

choices.text: {Follow the track|Track the trail|Shadow the footprints|Follow the path}.
{File the survey and lift|Log the coordinates and lift off|Pack up the sensors and launch|Upload the report and extract}.

a1.text: {leader} stands in line for what the suit clock calls {few} minutes and the crew above calls six hours. At the front there is a slot, and whatever is on the other side of it takes one memory and leaves something in its place.

a2.text: {The queue turns around all|The whole queue turns around all} {at once|all at the same time|together}, and none of them are facing the way faces should face.

b1.text: They come apart and go together in ways the ship's workshop will be arguing about for months. Two of them are missing a use {nobody|no one} has found yet.

b2.text:
The second offering is {a photograph|a photograph out of somebody's locker}, which is the most expensive thing anyone is carrying.
What comes back for it is not an object. It is a length of quiet in the middle of the away team, and everybody who walks through it comes out of it well.

c1.text: The track goes round the site nine times {and then|then|and after that} straight out to a cache buried {a metre|two metres|a half-metre} down, packed and labelled by whoever does the sweeping, as though for collection.

c2.text: The survey is the most valuable document the ship has filed all year, and it will be argued over by people who were not there. {Nothing follows the lander up.|Nothing comes up after the lander.}

b2_m.text:
The second offering is {a photograph|a photograph out of somebody's locker}, which is the most expensive thing anyone is carrying, and putting it down on the step takes {longer than it should|a moment|some doing}.
It is not taken. It sits there for {nine seconds|a count of nine|a while}, and then it is turned over, by nothing, so that the picture faces up, and then it is left.

asides.nurturing: {member} does not look away from the step for the whole nine seconds.
asides.any: {member} {puts a hand on the shoulder of whoever owns the photograph|says nothing|writes the time down}

choices.text: Take the photograph back and go.
Leave it. Put down something to go with it.
Ask, out loud, what it is for.

b2_pair.text:
A second photograph, out of a different locker, put down beside the first, face up, in the same orientation.
Both are gone in the morning and what is on the step in their place is {small|not large|about the size of a hand} and warm, and everybody who looks at it sees something different in it, and all of them are correct.

b2_ask.text:
Asking a building a question out loud in front of your own crew is {a thing you only do once|a decision|not nothing}, and the answer comes in the only way the place has of answering, which is by exchange.
What is put on the step in reply is a photograph. It is not one of the party's. It is of {this place|the shrine|the step}, taken from where the party is standing, by somebody who has not been born yet.

c1_m.text:
The track goes round the site nine times and then straight out, and following it takes {two hours|the rest of the light|a long walk} across ground that gets progressively harder to cross.
It ends at a cache buried {a metre|two metres|a half-metre} down, packed and labelled by somebody with a system, and the labels are in {two|three} hands, and one of the hands is much more recent than the other.

choices.text: Dig it up and take the lot.
Sort the recent labels from the old ones first.
Re-bury it and mark the position for the ship.

c1_sort.text:
The old hand packed a cache. The recent hand has been {adding to it|keeping it|maintaining it}, and the most recent addition is {this season|weeks old|not old at all}, and it is a survival kit of a make the party recognises.
Somebody has been alive out here, alone, using this cache, for a while. The party leaves a note in it and takes only what is spoiling, which is the correct answer and is not the profitable one.

c1_mark.text:
It goes back in the hole exactly as it came out, and the position goes to the ship with a note that it is not to be lifted.
That note is ignored {eleven months|the following year|eventually} by somebody else's crew, and the party reads about what happened to them in a bulletin, and does not say anything at the table for a while afterwards.

n0.text:
{It's not a distress call. It's {tone}, broadcasting from {place} on an endless loop.|An automated transmission ({tone}) is pulsing from {place} every few seconds.|An automated transmission ({tone}) is pulsing from {place} every many seconds.|A rhythmic signal is broadcasting out of {place}, clear and unbothered by atmospheric static.}
The loop is not quite a loop. Every {nine|eleven} repetitions it {drops a beat|adds one|changes in one place}, and the change is not in the same place twice.

choices.text: {Answer it in the same pattern|Echo the signal rhythm|Transmit the matching code|Mirror the transmission frequency}.
{Find the transmitter and open it|Locate the beacon and pry it open|Track down the transmitter hatch|Dig up the broadcasting unit}.
Jam it.

n0.emText:
Not a distress call: a count, going out of {place} for longer than the catalogue admits.
Counts are the oldest magic there is. Somebody said a number here and then kept saying the next one, and the universe took it seriously, and it has been going ever since like a tap somebody left running in an empty flat.
n0.bubba: "It's countin'," says Bubba. "An' it ain't stopped for us. Chill' sta' cuntanno pe' quaccheduno ato."

a.text:
{leader} keys the pattern back, one beat late, {deliberately|on purpose} wrong in the last place.
The count stops. Nine seconds later it starts again, corrected, and now it is answering the mistake rather than repeating itself.

choices.text: Keep the conversation going.
Shut the radio off and back away.

b.text:
The transmitter is buried in {ground} with only its collar showing, and the collar is a hatch. It opens by hand. It was built to open by hand.
Inside: a mechanism with no moving parts, and {remnant} laid neatly on top of it, like an offering.

choices.text: {Take the mechanism|Pry out the core assembly|Salvage the internal clockwork|Strip the mechanism for parts}.
{Take the offering and close the hatch|Grab the cache and seal the lid|Take the prize and lock the hatch|Pocket the goods and shut the door}.

c.text:
The jammer goes up on a tripod and the band flattens out. For {many} minutes there is nothing across the whole spectrum but the sound of the away team breathing.
Then {hazard} makes itself felt, and the count comes back at three times the power.

choices.text: {Hold the position and burn it out|Keep the jammer running at maximum|Overload the frequency until it pops|Burn out the transmitter}.
{Pull back to the lander|Retreat to the ship|Pack up and get to safety|Evacuate the area}.

a1.text: It takes {few} hours to build a shared count and another two to trade nouns. What is on the other end is not close, is not alive in any sense the team can use, and gives {leader} a set of coordinates as a gift for the trouble.

a2.text: {The radio goes dark.|The comms cut out completely.|Static dies on the channel.|The signal flatlines.|The radio goes dead.|The channel goes completely silent.|Dead air on the frequency.|The receiver drops to zero.} The count keeps on over {ground} behind them all the way back to the lander, and the team walks the last hundred metres faster than they walked the first.

b1.text: {It lifts out easily.|The assembly slides out smoothly.|It pops free without any resistance.|The module unlatches cleanly.|It lifts out without any trouble.} The count stops, and every instrument the away team is carrying reports the same time to the same tenth of a second for the first time since they left Earth.

b2.text: The hatch shuts {sweetly|cleanly|the way it should}, the way a well-made thing does. The count carries on, and the team goes up with something in a bag that {nobody|no one} has a word for yet.

c1.text: The jammer wins, {eventually|in the end|sooner or later}, and the source dies with a noise like {a held breath let go|a breath finally let out}. The team digs the emitter out of the slag afterwards: it is beautiful, and it is worth a fortune.

c2.text: Whatever the count belongs to gets to the lander {before the team does|ahead of the team}, and it is standing between them and the hatch when they come over the last rise.

b1_m.text:
Inside the collar the mechanism is {beautiful|absurdly well made|the work of somebody who had time}: a count, mechanical, geared, driving a transmitter that has been fed by the ground itself for longer than anybody can estimate.
Under it, in a recess, there is an offering. Something has been putting one there, regularly, and the older ones underneath have {rotted|gone to powder|turned to nothing} and the newest is {fresh|recent|this season's}.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Somebody feeds this.|That is maintenance, and it has a schedule.|We are standing in somebody's chapel.}"
asides.any: {member} {counts the layers in the recess|photographs the recess before anything is touched|does not reach in}

choices.text: Take the mechanism. It is the valuable part.
Work out how often the offerings are left.
Leave an offering of our own and close the hatch.

b1_rate.text:
Layer by layer it comes out at {once a season|four times a local year|regularly}, and the layers go down {nine hundred|a great many|further than the core sample}, and the top one is not the last one: there is a gap, and then this season's.
Something stopped coming for {eleven years|a decade|a long while} and then started again. Working out what changed in that gap is the single most publishable thing anybody brings back off this rock.

c1_m.text:
The jammer wins, {eventually|in the end|sooner or later}, and the source dies with a noise like {a held breath let go|a breath finally let out}, and the band across the whole spectrum goes properly flat.
And stays flat. Including the party's own channels, including the lander's beacon, including {the ship|orbit|the link up}, which was not part of the plan and does not come back when the jammer is switched off.

choices.text: Dig out the emitter and get off this rock.
Restart the count. Put it back the way it was.
Walk back to the lander without radio and without hurrying.

c1_restart.text:
Restarting a mechanical count that has been running since before the species that built it had a word for counting takes {four hours|the rest of the day|a long time} and a great deal of care about the phase.
It comes up. Two seconds later so does everything else: the lander, the beacon, the ship, all of it, all at once. Nobody aboard ever files a full account of why the link was down, because there is no way to write it that does not sound like an apology to a machine.

c1_walk.text:
{Four kilometres|A long walk|The whole way back} across open ground with no radio, at a deliberate pace, because running would be an admission.
The lander is where it was left. The hatch is shut, and it was left open, and it opens on a cabin where every channel is live again and the count is on all of them, at {four times|twice|a great deal more than} its old rate.

n0.text:
{Thousands of small machine drones are crawling across {ground} like iron ants.|A massive swarm of tiny autonomous automatons is busy dismantling {place}.|Automated salvage drones are crawling over {place} in tight, synchronized patterns.}
They are taking the place apart in the reverse of the order it was built in, which means they have {the plans|a copy of the plans|something to work from}.

choices.text: Figure out what they're up to.
{Catch one|Snag a drone with a net|Trap one of the units|Grab a specimen}.
{Put something in their way|Drop an obstacle on their path|Block their line with a crate|Set down a barrier}.

n0.emText:
Thousands of machines, none bigger than a hand, working over {ground} at {place} on a job that has been running for centuries.
They ignore you completely. That is the insult and the information: a work party that has been told what the job is does not stop for a woman with no papers, and you have spent eleven months being exactly that everywhere you go.
n0.bubba: Bubba squats down among them and lets four of them walk over his boot. "They got a job. Tenene 'a fatica. Sugar, don't get in the way of folks workin'."

a.text:
{Two hours of surveillance|After watching for two hours|Two solid hours of observation|Watching the line for a couple of hours} and the pattern comes clear. They are not building. They are taking something apart, {very|remarkably} slowly, {very|remarkably} {carefully|with care}, and putting the pieces in order along a line that runs to the horizon.
The thing being taken apart is the world.

choices.text: {Follow the line|Track the cable|Trace the conduit|Follow the route} to the far end.
Take a piece off the line.

b.text:
It comes up in a glove {without a fight|without any argument}, folds its legs, and goes still.
Every other machine within sight stops at the same instant, and stays stopped, {and turns to face the glove|and every one of them turns to face the glove}.

choices.text: Put it down.
Pocket it and walk.

c.text:
{leader} sets a sample case down across their line and steps back.
The swarm stops at it, considers it for nine seconds, {and then|then|and after that} goes round. On the way past, one of them measures the case and writes the measurement on it.

choices.text: {Give them something worth measuring|Toss a high-tech tool into their line|Offer an alloy sample|Drop a piece of advanced composite}.
{Take the case back and leave them to it|Pick up your gear and walk away|Retrieve the case and back off|Pack your tools and leave}.

a1.text: The far end is a stack, sorted by material, {taller than the lander|higher than the lander}, and at the top of it is the first thing they ever took off this world, labelled in a notation that predates the swarm.

a2.text: The line closes the gap in {many} seconds and does not react otherwise. The piece is a machined block of something the ship's assay cannot name, and there are {few} hundred kilometres of them.

b1.text: The moment it touches {ground} the whole field goes back to work {as though nothing happened|as though nothing at all had happened}. Where it was standing there is now a small object that was not there before, and it is a gift, or a receipt.

b2.text: {few} hundred metres from the lander the field decides how it feels about theft.

c1.text: The cutter goes down on the line. They swarm it, measure it, take it apart, and put it back together {improved|better than it was}, and leave it on {ground} pointing at the lander.
