c2.text: The case comes back with a number on it in a base {nobody|no one} uses, {and the swarm carries on|and the swarm goes back to work}, and the away team is up and gone before anybody has to find out what the number means.

a1_m.text:
The far end of the line is a stack, sorted by material, {taller than the lander|higher than the lander}, and it has been growing for a very long time.
At the top of it, alone on a levelled platform, is the first thing they ever took off this world, and it is not raw material and it has not been sorted. It has been {kept|set aside|put somewhere it can be seen}.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{That is not a stack, that is a monument.|Everything else is sorted. That is displayed.|They kept the first one.}"
asides.any: {member} {works out the height of the stack|counts the material bands down the side|looks at the platform rather than the object}

choices.text: Climb it and take the thing off the top.
Read the stack from the bottom up.
Add something of ours to the stack in the right band.

a1_read.text:
The bands going up the stack are the materials of this world in the order they were taken, and the order is the order a builder dismantles in, and the last band is {half finished|thin|only just started}.
Which means they are nearly done, and what happens to a swarm that finishes is a question with {two|three} possible answers, and the party has about {a season|a year|not long} to decide who to sell that question to.

a1_give.text:
A plate off the lander's own skin, cut to size, carried to the stack and set into the correct material band by hand while the line goes round the party's boots.
The swarm stops. All of it, everywhere, for {nine seconds|a count of nine|the length of the placement}. Then it goes back to work, and the plate stays where it was put, and one drone follows the party to the lander and does not come aboard and does not leave.

c1_m.text:
The cutter goes down on the line. They swarm it, measure it, take it apart, and put it back together {improved|better than it was}, and leave it on {ground} pointing at the party.
The improvement is not a repair. There is a component in it that was not in it, and the component is not machined: it is {grown|the same material as the swarm|part of one of them}.

choices.text: Pick it up. A better cutter is a better cutter.
Take the new component out before using it.
Put another tool down and see what they do with that one.

c1_part.text:
It comes out cleanly, which is itself informative, and under the glass it is {one of them|a drone|a member of the swarm}, folded down to the size of a component and doing the job the component did.
The cutter still works without it. The thing in the jar is worth considerably more than the cutter and will be the subject of {four|five} papers, all of which disagree about whether it was a gift or a passenger.

c1_keep.text:
Taking it out goes wrong in the way that things go wrong when you do not know what you are holding, and what comes out is {in pieces|no longer whole|dead, if that is the word}.
The cutter is worse than it was before the swarm touched it. The line goes round it now rather than towards it, and nothing on this rock will come near the party for the rest of the survey.

c1_more.text:
A second tool goes down, then a third, then a ration tin, then a helmet, and each comes back {improved|altered|better} in a way that is more specific to its owner than the last one.
By the fourth it is unmistakable: they are not improving the tools. They are learning the party, one object at a time, and the helmet comes back with an adjustment in it that nobody has ever mentioned to anybody.

e_ocean.title: {The Bell Buoy That Is Not On The Chart|Something Is Ringing Out There|A Door Painted On A Can}

n0.emText: {A bell is clanging out across the water with an annoying, repetitive rhythm. The buoy is bobbing in the chop with a ladder welded on and a fake door painted onto the steel. In this line of work, weird doors are usually trouble.|The buoy rings out over the swell. Up close it has a ladder and a painted door with a real handle. Definitely suspicious.}
n0.bubba: Bubba leans over the rail with his hat in his hand. "Sugar, that's a door on a can. Uh-uh. Back home we got a word for openin' that, an' the word is {funerale|stupidaggine}."

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.paranoid: {member} {mutters that someone's definitely watching us from the shadows|checks their six three times and grips their holster|hisses that the signal frequency is rigged|whispers: "They knew we were coming. Look around."}
asides.scholarly: {member} {is already logging sensor anomalies with an annoyed grunt|scans the alloy and mutters about obsolete manufacturing dates|checks the survey records and complains about missing documentation|notes that the readings make zero thermodynamic sense}
asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.melancholic: {member} says bells at sea used to mean somebody was being counted, and stops there.
asides.mischievous: {member} {grins: "Dibs on whatever looks shiny and dangerous."|is already trying to pick the maintenance lock with a wire|wonders aloud what happens if we press all the buttons at once|smirks and taps the console to see if it sparks}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Come alongside and climb the ladder.
Circle it once and read everything written on it.
Cut the buoy loose and tow it in.
Log the position and go on.

a.text:
The ladder is warm. Suspicious.
The painted door has a painted handle, and when you take hold of the paint your hand closes on brass. Inside is a stairwell, dry, lit, going down further than the water is deep. {sound|Somewhere below, a radio playing under a floor} comes up the stairs to meet you.
a.bubba: "Well, madonna santa," says Bubba, testing the top step with his boot. "Stairs in the ocean. Jamme, then. You first, on accounta you float better."

asides.nervous: {member} {sweats inside their helmet and asks how much air we have left|keeps looking back toward the lander with wide eyes|jumps at every creak in the hull|wonders aloud if we can just leave right now}
asides.stoic: {member} {says nothing and checks the seals on their suit|nods once and takes up a defensive position|stands guard by the door, completely silent|keeps their eyes on the horizon without a word}
asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Go all the way down.
Take what is on the first landing and get out.

b.text:
Three languages, four hands, and one of them recent.
A name and a date, twice. A tide table for a port that does not exist. A phone number with the {Britannia|Varlenia|Collective} code. And under the waterline, where you have to hang off the ladder to read it: {rumour}.

asides.scholarly: {member} {is already logging sensor anomalies with an annoyed grunt|scans the alloy and mutters about obsolete manufacturing dates|checks the survey records and complains about missing documentation|notes that the readings make zero thermodynamic sense}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Ring the number from the boat's set.
Note it all down and sell the notes to somebody who wants them.

c.text:
It cuts easier than it should, and it tows like something that wants to come.
Half a mile in, the bell stops. Two miles in, {a cormorant|a gull|something with too many joints} lands on it and stays there, facing the way you came. The harbourmaster at {region} takes one look and pays you to take it away again.

d.text:
You write the position in the log with the time next to it and you go on.
Two days later, in a bar in {region}, a man who says he is a hydrographer buys the page off you. He does not want the page. He wants to know if the bell was ringing on the swell or against it.
Against it, you tell him. He pays you and leaves without his coat.

a1.text:
Eleven landings down, the stairwell opens into a room with a table, a chair, a lamp and a sea chart with your own course pencilled on it in a hand you do not know, ending where you are standing.
On the table, in {relicWord}, is the thing the bell was for.
a1.emText:
Eleven landings down there is a table, a chair, a lamp, and a chart with your own course already drawn on it, ending under your feet. The pencil is still warm. Ninety-two per cent of your life is filed somewhere you cannot get to and somebody down here has better records than you do.
On the table, in {relicWord}, is the thing the bell was ringing for. It's not a spellbook. You check twice.
a1.bubba: "Don't touch the chart," says Bubba, touching the chart. "Mannaggia. Okay. Touched it."

a2.text:
The first landing is a store: rope, tinned food, a crate of lamp oil, and four boxes of the kind of hardware nobody sells to a boat.
You take what two of you can carry and you are back in daylight before the tide turns, which is the only sensible thing anybody has done all week.

b1.text:
It rings four times. Then a woman's voice, flat as a chart datum, says a bearing, a depth and a time, and hangs up.
You are at that bearing at that time because you are the kind of crew that turns up. Something comes up out of the dark to meet the boat, and it is not interested in talking about it.

asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.timid: {member} asks, reasonably, whether anybody wrote down where we are.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

b2.text:
The Foundation office in {region} takes the whole notebook, gives you a receipt in a language that is not one of the four on the buoy, and pays you for it in {coin}.
They ask you to stop writing things down. They ask it very politely.

c_m.text:
It cuts easier than it should, and it tows like something that wants to come, and half a mile in the bell stops.
Two miles in the tow goes light. Not parted: {light|slack|weightless}, as though the buoy has stopped being in the water without stopping being on the end of the line.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Cut it. Cut it now.|Nothing tows like that.|We are not towing that thing. It is coming.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts a hand on the tow and takes it off again|watches the wake where the buoy should be|goes aft without being asked}

choices.text: Keep towing. It is salvage and salvage is money.
Get the line off and let it go.
Take a bearing on where the weight went.

c_cut.text:
The line goes over the side and the buoy is astern and {then it is not|then it is not astern|then the water is empty}, inside the length of time it takes to coil a rope.
The bell starts again about {four hundred metres|a cable|some distance} off the port bow, which is the wrong side, and keeps station there until the coast comes up.

c_bear.text:
Two bearings, four minutes apart, off a boat that is making way: it is rough work and it gives a position, and the position is {eleven miles|a long way|well} off the tow line and is in water the chart calls {four hundred fathoms|deep|unsounded}.
The buoy comes in on the end of the line an hour later, wet, ordinary, and worth what a buoy is worth. The position is worth considerably more and there are {three|four} offices that will pay for it.

d_m.text:
You write the position in the log with the time next to it and you go on, and that is the whole of it for {two days|a day and a half|the rest of the passage}.
In a bar in {region} a man who says he is a hydrographer offers to buy the page. He has the money on the table before the sentence is finished and he knows which page it is without being told.

choices.text: Sell him the page.
Find out how he knew which page.
Keep the log. Sell him a drink instead.

d_how.text:
He is not a hydrographer and he does not pretend to be one for longer than {four questions|a minute|it takes}, and what he is is the third man this year sent round the coast bars buying pages out of logs.
Who sends them is worth knowing. He gives it up in exchange for the page, which he gets, and both sides consider it a good evening's work.

d_keep.text:
The page stays in the log, the drink is bought, and he takes it and is pleasant about the whole thing and leaves before closing.
The log is in the wheelhouse. The page is not in it in the morning, and no lock has been touched, and the entry either side of the gap is undisturbed in a way that is {worse|more unpleasant|harder to think about} than a torn spine would be.

a2_m.text:
The first landing is a store: rope, tinned food, a crate of lamp oil, and four boxes of the kind of hardware nobody sells to a boat.
It is all {dated|stamped|marked}, and the dates are recent, and the oldest thing on the landing is {a fortnight|three weeks|not old}. Somebody restocks this, from below, and the stairwell goes down eleven landings.

choices.text: Take what two of you can carry and go.
Read the stamps on the hardware boxes.
Leave payment on the landing for what you take.

a2_stamp.text:
The stamps are naval, and they are current, and the contract number on the side of the crate is one that is {still running|live|being invoiced against this year}.
Somebody is supplying a stairwell inside a buoy in water the chart says is empty. That is not a salvage job and it is not a story for a bar, and the party takes the boxes and the numbers both.

a2_pay.text:
Coins on the crate, counted out at what the goods are worth ashore and then a bit over, which everybody in the boat agrees afterwards was either {sensible|superstition|good manners} and none of them will say which.
The money is gone the next time anybody looks, and in its place there is a chart, folded, of water the party has not sailed yet, with the safe line on it marked in pencil.

e_fields.title: {The Standing Crop|The Square They Never Cut|{lots} Paces On A Side}

n0.text:
The field was cut a month ago. One square of it is still standing.
{lots} paces on a side, corners sharper than any plough has ever managed, and inside it {sound_field}. Outside it, in the stubble, nothing at all is moving, not even the {crows|gulls|pigeons} that ought to be here.
There is a gate, and a farmhouse {distance}, and a tractor parked exactly where somebody stopped it.
The standing square is {exactly|precisely} square, and the corners point at the compass points, and the farm does not.
n0.emText:
One square of crop still standing in a cut field, sides too straight to be an accident, and you can feel it the way you feel a held note: something in there has been left deliberately unharvested, the way you were left deliberately unfinished.
Inside it {sound_field}. Outside, the stubble is not doing anything at all. The tractor is parked where somebody stopped it and got out and did not come back for it.
n0.bubba: Bubba squints at the corners. "That's surveyed, sugar. Somebody paid a fella with a stick an' a chain. Uh-huh. That ain't fairies, that's paperwork."

asides.scholarly: {member} {is already logging sensor anomalies with an annoyed grunt|scans the alloy and mutters about obsolete manufacturing dates|checks the survey records and complains about missing documentation|notes that the readings make zero thermodynamic sense}
asides.nervous: {member} {sweats inside their helmet and asks how much air we have left|keeps looking back toward the lander with wide eyes|jumps at every creak in the hull|wonders aloud if we can just leave right now}
asides.adventurous: {member} {grins: "Now this is what I signed up for."|is already climbing the rubble to see what's on the other side|can't wait to see what's behind the blast door|rushes ahead to get the first look}
asides.disciplined: {member} {follows standard breach protocol by the book|clears every corner with military precision|keeps a steady firing stance and monitors the sensors|checks the ammo count and maintains position}
asides.artistic: {member} says the standing square looks like a word with all the other letters mown off.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Walk into the middle of it.
Go and find whoever farms this.
Cut a sheaf and take it away.
Burn it, and stand upwind.

a.text:
The stalks {lean away|part|bend aside} as you come on and close again behind you, politely, like a crowd letting somebody through to the front.
In the middle there is a patch of bare packed earth with a hollow in it, about the size of {a sleeping dog|a sleeping child|something that sleeps curled up}. It is warm. The crop around the hollow has come up a second time this year, out of season, and it has come up heavy.

asides.nurturing: {member} puts a hand flat on the warm earth and keeps it there.
asides.paranoid: {member} {mutters that someone's definitely watching us from the shadows|checks their six three times and grips their holster|hisses that the signal frequency is rigged|whispers: "They knew we were coming. Look around."}
asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Lie down in the hollow.
Dig it out.
Fill it in and walk away.

b.text:
The farmhouse smells of {smell}. The man there does not want to talk about the square.
He wants to talk about his father, who left it standing for {lots} years, and about the two dry summers that followed the one time it got cut. He talks with his hands flat on the table, the way you talk when the table is the only steady thing in the room.
He will pay for it to be left alone. He will pay a good deal more if somebody will go in and look and come back and tell him it is nothing.
b.bubba: Bubba is already eating this man's bread. "Signo', don't you fret. We're professionals. Mostly her. Uh-huh."

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.grumpy: {member} {complains loudly about the freezing temperature|curses under their breath at the terrible footing|mutters that this job isn't worth the hazard pay|kicks a piece of debris and grunts in frustration}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Take his money to leave it standing.
Take his money to go and look.
Take his tools and cut it flat.

c.text:
The sheaf comes away easily, like something handed over.
It stays green for {many} days in a pack where bread goes mouldy in three. The grain is heavier than the grain around it and it seeds true. The agricultural office in {region} takes the whole sheaf, asks no questions worth answering, and pays on the spot rather than by the usual cheque in April.

e.text:
It goes up like it was waiting to.
The fire keeps the square. It burns to the exact edge and stops, and what walks out of the middle of it is on fire too, and does not appear to consider that a problem worth discussing with you.

asides.aggressive: "There," says {member}, with enormous satisfaction, about four seconds too early.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

a1.text:
It is the length of a person and it fits the way a coat fits when somebody has had it made for you.
{leader} is out for {many} minutes by the watch and comes up with a taste of copper, a scar closed that has been open since the spring, and everybody standing over them looking rested for the first time in a month.
a1.emText:
It is the length of a person, and it fits you the way nothing has fitted you since the first of January.
You are out for {many} minutes. You do not get a memory back. You get the shape of one, the dent where it was, and something in the field turns over in its sleep and gives you back a scar closed and a night's rest you did not pay for.
a1.bubba: Bubba is holding your hat when you come up. "Nah, don't say nothin'. You was smilin'. Ain't seen that. Uh-uh."

a2.text:
{A foot down|Two feet down|Half a spade down}, the earth stops being earth.
What comes up out of the hollow has slept through several harvests and it wants {the rest of its year|the rest of the year it is owed|the winter it was promised}. It's not angry. It is worse than angry: it is awake early.

a3.text:
You fill the hollow with the loose earth around it and tread it down, and the crop closes over the top of it, and the field lets you leave.
The farmer will not take a penny back off you. In the yard he gives you {payment} instead and stands in the road watching until you are out of sight.

b1.text:
He pays in notes his father kept back from {three|two|four} good years, and shakes every hand twice.
The square is still standing. Everything around it will be, too, and in a bad year three villages will not know why they came through it.

b2.text:
You cut it in an afternoon, with his own machine, and he watches from the gate with his cap in his hands.
The grain fills more sacks than the field has any business filling. It sells for a great deal. The following spring is very dry, and the spring after that is worse, and nobody in that parish ever says your name out loud again, though they all know it.

c_m.text:
The sheaf comes away easily, like something handed over, and it stays green in a pack where bread goes mouldy in three days.
On the fourth day it has {put out a root|rooted|started growing} through the canvas, into whatever is under the pack, and it is not fussy about what that is.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{It is not a souvenir, it is a passenger.|That has gone through the pack.|Whatever we took, it is still farming.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts the sheaf in a tin|holds it up to the light|cuts the root and watches it go again}

choices.text: Keep it. Sell it. Somebody will pay.
Plant it somewhere it can be watched.
Take it back to the square and put it where it came from.

c_plant.text:
A pot, a frame, a wall to stand it against, and {four months|a season|a winter} of writing down what it does.
What it does is grow in a square. Not in a pot: it puts out one runner in each of four directions at the compass points, exactly, and by spring there is a {nine-pace|small|perfect} square of it and the ground inside the square is the best ground on the plot.

c_spread.text:
It goes in the ground in a corner of somewhere the party is staying, which is a decision made in {four seconds|haste|the way these decisions are made}.
By the {third week|month|spring} it has a square of its own and the square has taken in a wall, half a shed and somebody's washing line, and the people who live there have stopped using that end of the garden and will not say why.

c_back.text:
It is {four days|a long way|two days} back to the field and the sheaf is put down inside the square, in the standing crop, which closes over it {politely|the way it closed before|without comment}.
The farmer sees the party at the gate and does not ask. He does put a hand up. That autumn the square is the only thing in three counties that does not take the blight, and everything within a mile of it is {clean|untouched|fine}.

e_m.text:
It goes up like it was waiting to, and the fire keeps the square: it burns to the exact edge and stops.
What walks out of the middle of it is on fire too and does not appear to mind, and it walks {four paces|a short way|out} and then stops and {waits|stands|does nothing at all}, which is not what anybody was braced for.

choices.text: Put it down.
Stand still and let it be on fire.
Put the fire out. All of it, including that.

e_wait.text:
It burns for {eleven minutes|a quarter of an hour|a long time} without going anywhere and without going out, and everybody stands upwind and nobody raises anything.
When it stops burning there is a person standing in the ash, who is {nobody's|not anybody's} idea of a person, and who says one sentence about the field and then lies down in the hollow and does not get up again.

e_out.text:
Beating out a crop fire with coats at the edge of a square that is burning to its own line, and then going in after the thing in the middle of it with the same coats.
It lets them. The fire goes out. What is left is standing there smoking with {the whole square|four acres|everything} black around it, and it walks with the party as far as the gate and then goes back and sits down in the middle of its own ash.

e_meadows.title: {The Long Grass Nobody Cuts|Four Acres Left Standing|The Bench By The Stone}

n0.text:
The meadow has not been cut in years, and it should have been: it is good ground, and there is a farm on it, and the farm is working.
What stops the mower is halfway out: a stone, waist-high, with a bench next to it, and the bench is new. Somebody replaces that bench. Somebody has been replacing it for a while, judging by the four sets of post holes.
{smell}, and in the grass, {sound}.
There is a second bench, further out, {rotted to nothing|almost gone|down to its legs}, on the same line.
n0.emText:
Good ground, uncut for years, and a stone in the middle of it with a bench next to it that somebody keeps replacing.
You can feel the shape of the arrangement without being told: this is a place where a thing was agreed, and the agreement is still running, and the grass is the payment. You know about agreements you cannot remember making.
n0.bubba: "Somebody's grandma sits here," says Bubba, sitting on it. "Ooh. Comodo. Nah, I'm stayin'."

asides.calm: {member} sits down on the bench and lets the meadow get on with whatever it is doing.

choices.text: Sit on the bench and wait for whoever replaces it.
Read the stone.
Cut a swathe through the meadow with whatever is in the pack.
Go to the farm and ask.

a.text:
You wait an hour and a half and {stranger} comes up the track with a folding stool, sees the bench occupied, and sits down on the stool instead without complaint.
They have brought {food} for two. They offer you half without being asked and without looking at you.
"You'll want to be gone by dark," they say, comfortably. "It's not that it minds. It's that it forgets you're people."

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.paranoid: {member} {mutters that someone's definitely watching us from the shadows|checks their six three times and grips their holster|hisses that the signal frequency is rigged|whispers: "They knew we were coming. Look around."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Stay past dark with them.
Ask what the arrangement is, plainly.

b.text:
No name. No date. A line of letters cut with a chisel by somebody who was not a mason, and under them, more recently, in paint: {rumour}.
The stone is warm on the north face and cold on the south, which is the wrong way round for a sunny afternoon, and has been the wrong way round for as long as anybody has been coming here with a bench.

asides.scholarly: {member} {is already logging sensor anomalies with an annoyed grunt|scans the alloy and mutters about obsolete manufacturing dates|checks the survey records and complains about missing documentation|notes that the readings make zero thermodynamic sense}
asides.nervous: {member} {sweats inside their helmet and asks how much air we have left|keeps looking back toward the lander with wide eyes|jumps at every creak in the hull|wonders aloud if we can just leave right now}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Dig at the base of the stone.
Copy the letters and take them to somebody who reads that sort of thing.

c.text:
You get four metres in.
The grass is not grass all the way down: at the root it is threaded through with something white and fine, and it goes taut when you cut it, all across the meadow at once, like a net being taken up.
The farm dogs start, a mile off. Then they stop, all together.

d.text:
The farmer is a woman in her sixties who does not put the kettle on, which tells you where you stand.
"It's four acres," she says. "Four acres is nothing. My mother did the same and her mother did the same and I've a good crop off everything else, haven't I."
She pays you not to write about it. She pays in cash and in {payment}, and she watches the meadow the whole time she is talking to you.

a1.text:
After dark the meadow does something with sound: everything you say arrives about a second late and from slightly the wrong direction.
{stranger} keeps talking anyway, calmly, into the dark, and at some point stops talking to you and starts talking to something else. Whatever answers uses your voice, which they seem to expect, and which they do not appear to think is worth mentioning.
In the morning there is dew on everything but the bench, and something in your pack that was not there.

a2.text:
"The grass stands, and it keeps the rest of the farm right. That's it. That's the whole of it."
They say it the way people say the rules of a game they have played all their life. Then they teach you the two things you do if you are ever caught in the middle of it at dark, and make you say them back, twice, and correct you once.

b1.text:
Nine inches down, the chalk is packed with small brown bones, all of them bird, all of them arranged.
A foot further, in {relicWord}, is the thing the arrangement was made over. It comes out clean and the hole fills itself in behind it with a sound like somebody sitting down.

b2.text:
A woman in {region} who restores church plate reads it in about four seconds and then will not read it again.
She pays you for the rubbing, which she burns, and for the promise that you will not go back, which she cannot enforce and which you make anyway.

c_m.text:
You get four metres in. The grass is not grass all the way down: at the root it is threaded through with something white and fine, and it goes taut when you cut it, all across the meadow at once.
Nothing comes. It stays taut, the whole four acres of it, {humming|tight|like a drum head}, and it is possible to stand very still and think about the next swing.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Stop cutting.|The whole field is one thing and we just pulled on it.|Put the blade down. Slowly.}"
asides.any: {member} {does not move|puts a hand flat on the grass and feels it thrumming|counts the seconds}

choices.text: Finish the swathe.
Back out along the cut and leave the blade where it is.
Follow one thread by hand and find out where it goes.

c_back.text:
Four metres backwards down your own cut, slowly, with the blade left standing in the grass where it stopped.
The tension goes out of the meadow at the edge and not before. The blade is still there the next morning and is still there {a year later|the following season|years afterwards}, upright, and the grass has grown round it and not over it.

c_thread.text:
One white thread, followed on hands and knees for {forty metres|a long way|most of an afternoon}, under the cut and out of it, across the meadow, to the foot of the stone.
Every thread goes there. The meadow is not a meadow, it is {a single thing|one organism|the top of something}, and the bench is where you sit when you are minding it, and the arrangement is suddenly a great deal more legible.

d_m.text:
The farmer is a woman in her sixties who does not put the kettle on, which tells you where you stand, and who says four acres is nothing and her mother did the same.
What she does not say, and what is obvious from the yard, is that the farm is doing {far better|considerably better|better than it has any right to} than the land around it, and has been for {three generations|a very long time|as long as the bench has been there}.

choices.text: Leave it. Her farm, her arrangement.
Ask her what happens if nobody sits the bench.
Ask to see the farm's books.

d_bench.text:
The kettle goes on for that question, which is how the party knows it is the right one.
Nobody has ever not sat it. There is a rota, there has always been a rota, it covers {eleven|nine} households and it goes back further than the parish register, and she is the one who keeps it, and she is {seventy-one|sixty-eight|older than she says} and there is nobody after her.

d_books.text:
The books go back to {1911|the twenties|before the war} in four different hands and they are honest books, which is what makes them frightening: the yields are not extraordinary in any one year and they have never once had a bad one.
Not in the drought, not in the blight, not in the year the river came up. The woman watches the party work that out and says nothing, and then says: four acres.

e_forest.title: {The Blind|Somebody Is Sitting In The Trees|{landmark}}

n0.text:
The track in is better kept than the road that brought you to it. Somebody grades it. Nobody admits to it.
Half a mile in there is a hide up in a beech: a shooting blind, boarded, with a ladder and a felt roof and a stove pipe. It faces {landmark}. Zero game here worth a stove.
The ladder has been used this morning. In the trees, {sound}.
The grading is done with a proper blade and it is done {at night|after dark|between visits}, because the track is never grading-fresh when anybody is on it.
n0.emText:
The track is graded and the wood is quiet in the way a room is quiet when someone has just stopped talking about you.
There is a hide up a beech, boarded, with a stove pipe, facing {landmark}, and no game here worth sitting out for. Somebody watches this place professionally. You have been in the world eleven months and you already know what a professional watcher's chair smells like from underneath.
n0.bubba: Bubba looks up the ladder and back at you. "Deer blind. Sure. An' I'm the Pope. Nun c'e' sta niente 'a cacciare ccà, sugar."

asides.paranoid: {member} {mutters that someone's definitely watching us from the shadows|checks their six three times and grips their holster|hisses that the signal frequency is rigged|whispers: "They knew we were coming. Look around."}
asides.scholarly: {member} {is already logging sensor anomalies with an annoyed grunt|scans the alloy and mutters about obsolete manufacturing dates|checks the survey records and complains about missing documentation|notes that the readings make zero thermodynamic sense}
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.mischievous: {member} {grins: "Dibs on whatever looks shiny and dangerous."|is already trying to pick the maintenance lock with a wire|wonders aloud what happens if we press all the buttons at once|smirks and taps the console to see if it sparks}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Climb up.
Go and stand in whatever the hide is watching.
Wait in the brush until somebody comes back for it.
Follow the graded track to whoever grades it.

a.text:
Warm stove. A flask, still hot. A camp stool, a pair of very good field glasses, and a logbook.
The logbook is not a game book. It is a list of dates and times and, in the third column, one word each: names, mostly. Some of them are names of people. Some of them are names of days.
Today's date is at the bottom. The third column has been filled in already, and the word is yours.
a.bubba: Bubba reads over your shoulder and goes very quiet, which from him is an alarm. "Sugar. Uh-uh. Chill' ccà nun so' cacciatori."

asides.nervous: {member} {sweats inside their helmet and asks how much air we have left|keeps looking back toward the lander with wide eyes|jumps at every creak in the hull|wonders aloud if we can just leave right now}
asides.stoic: {member} {says nothing and checks the seals on their suit|nods once and takes up a defensive position|stands guard by the door, completely silent|keeps their eyes on the horizon without a word}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Take the logbook and go.
Sit in the stool and wait for the owner.
Write a fourth column of your own.

b.text:
You walk out into the middle of what the glasses are pointed at, which is {landmark}, and you stand there, and nothing happens for four full minutes.
Then the birds stop. Not all at once: in a ring, closing, the way silence goes across a room when the wrong person comes in.

asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Stand your ground and let it come.
Speak first. Say what you are doing here.

c.text:
Two hours in the wet brush, and then somebody comes: not up the track, out of {landmark}, walking as if the wood were a corridor in their own house.
They climb the ladder, they light the stove, and they open the logbook. Then they lean out of the hide, look directly at where you are lying, and wave you in for tea.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Go up and have the tea.
Leave, quickly, while they are being polite.

d.text:
The track ends at a forestry hut with a Britannia licence plate on a Varlenian van and a woman doing paperwork on the bonnet.
She is not surprised. She has a folder with your route in it, drawn in the same pencil the chart on the buoy was drawn in, if you have ever seen one of those.
"Two questions," she says. "Then either you work for us this afternoon or you never came up this track."

choices.text: Work for her this afternoon.
Never came up this track.

asides.authoritative: {member} {barks out orders to secure the perimeter|demands status reports on the double|reminds everyone to maintain radio discipline|takes charge of the entry team with a brisk nod}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

a1.text:
You are three miles off before you look at the earlier pages properly.
It is a register of everybody who has come up that track for nineteen years, and what became of them, and the last column for most of them reads the same short word. The Foundation office in {region} buys it off you in a corridor, standing up, and pays what it costs to make you stop asking about the word.

a2.text:
You sit in a dead man's stool for an hour and forty minutes and then the ladder creaks and somebody comes up who is not carrying a rifle.
What you talk about is the third column. What they leave you with, because you sat and waited instead of running, is {relicWord} out of the stove bench, and a rule about this wood you will use twice more this year.

a3.text:
You write down what each of them was wearing.
It takes twenty minutes and it is the most petty thing anybody in this party has done all month, and the wood does not like it. Something comes up the ladder that does not use the rungs.

b1.text: It comes out of the trees at a walk, on the wrong number of legs for the sound it was making, and it has been eating what the hide was for.

b2.text:
You say your name and your business, out loud, to a wood.
The ring stops closing. Something the size of a door leans out of the dark to look at you, decides, and goes away, and the birds come back on one after another like lights.
Where it stood there is a gap in the leaf litter with something in it that was pressed into the earth by weight and time.

c1.text:
Tea in a hide with a stranger who has been watching this wood for nineteen years and has never once been paid for it.
They tell you what the third column means, and what to do if you ever see your own name in it, and then they give you {payment} and put you back on the track facing the right way.

c2.text:
You go, and the wood lets you, and behind you the stove smoke comes up straight in a wind that is bending every tree it passes.
On the road you find the flask in your pack. Nobody put it there. It is still hot in {region}, four hours later, and it is still hot the next morning.

d1.text:
The afternoon's work is carrying four sealed boxes from {landmark} to the van without stopping, resting, or putting them down on ground.
You earn every note of it. One of the boxes is warm on one side and something in it moves when you take the corner.

d2.text:
You never came up that track. She writes that down too, in the folder, and thanks you sincerely.
What you take away is the sight of what was in the open folder: a map of this wood with nineteen hides on it, and a note in the corner about which of them are still manned.

a1_m.text:
The logbook goes in the coat and the ladder comes down and you are {three miles|two miles|a good way} off before anybody looks at the earlier pages properly.
The third column is dates, and the fourth column, which nobody noticed in the hide, is a column of {times|durations|numbers in minutes}, and every entry in it is under {nine|eleven} except the last three, which are blank.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Blank means still running.|Three people are still being timed.|Whoever is in the fourth column is not finished.}"
asides.any: {member} {reads the last three lines out loud|checks the dates against today|closes the book and does not open it again}

choices.text: Keep it. Sell it. It is nineteen years of somebody's work.
Work out what the fourth column is counting.
Turn round and put it back in the hide.

a1_col.text:
It is how long each of them was in the wood. Not how long they were seen: how long they were {inside the line|in there|unaccounted for}, measured against a watch, and the three blanks are three people who went in and are counted as still in.
One of the three dates is {this spring|four months ago|recent}. The wood is two miles across. There is nowhere in it to be for four months.

a1_back.text:
Three miles back, up the ladder, and the logbook on the table with the flask moved to hold the page, which is {more care|a courtesy|more than was taken removing it}.
The stove is still warm. The glasses have been moved. On the bottom rung of the ladder on the way down there is a {pencil|new pencil|freshly sharpened pencil} that was not there on the way up, and it is for the party, and everybody understands that.

d1_m.text:
The afternoon's work is carrying four sealed boxes from {landmark} to the van without stopping, resting, or putting them down on ground.
The first three are heavy and awkward and ordinary. The fourth is {light|much lighter|almost nothing}, and the woman watches that one the entire way across the clearing without pretending not to.

choices.text: Carry it to the van and take the money.
Put it down.
Ask what is in it, on the walk, without stopping.

d1_down.text:
It goes down on the leaf mould for {four seconds|about four seconds|no time at all} and the woman does not shout, which is the frightening part: she just stops writing.
It is picked up again. The mark it leaves on the ground is the shape of the box and stays there, and is {still there|visible|unfaded} the following spring, and nothing grows in it.

d1_ask.text:
Asked on the move, at the right distance, with the box on the shoulder, she answers, which she would not have done sitting down.
It is not what is in the box. It is what the box is: {four of them|one a season|a set}, carried out of that clearing every year since the war by whoever she can hire, to a van, to a ferry, to an address the party is given and told to forget.

e_forestice.title: {The Long Cold|Woodsmoke And No Chimney|Ninety Trees Marked In Blue}

n0.text:
Snow to the knee between black trunks, and ninety trees marked in blue paint at chest height, in a line that runs straight through a wood that has nothing straight in it.
There is woodsmoke. Zero chimney, no hut, no track, and no footprints but yours, and the smoke is coming up out of the snow itself about {distance} along the line.
The blue on the ninetieth tree is wet, and the nearest road is {eleven miles|a day's walk|a long way} back.
n0.emText:
Ninety trees marked in blue, dead straight through a crooked wood, and woodsmoke coming out of the snow where nothing is burning.
Somebody drew a line here and the world took it seriously. You know how that works. You were a line somebody drew once, and the world took you seriously too, and look at you now.
n0.bubba: Bubba puts his hand over the smoke and pulls it back sharpish. "Cold smoke. That ain't a thing. That ain't a thing, sugar. Uh-uh. Mamma mia."

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.scholarly: {member} {is already logging sensor anomalies with an annoyed grunt|scans the alloy and mutters about obsolete manufacturing dates|checks the survey records and complains about missing documentation|notes that the readings make zero thermodynamic sense}
asides.stoic: {member} {says nothing and checks the seals on their suit|nods once and takes up a defensive position|stands guard by the door, completely silent|keeps their eyes on the horizon without a word}
asides.artistic: {member} says the blue is the same blue as the paint on a school corridor. {member} is right.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Follow the blue line.
Dig where the smoke comes up.
Make camp on the line and see what walks it.
Go back the way you came, quickly.

a.text:
Ninety trees, and at the ninetieth the paint is fresh.
Beyond it there is no more wood: there is a clearing the shape of a room, floored in ice you can see down into, and under the ice, laid out and neat, a surveyor's kit, a coat, and a pair of boots with the laces still tied.
The blue paint tin is standing on the ice, open, unfrozen.

asides.melancholic: {member} looks at the laces for a long time. Somebody tied those.
asides.nervous: {member} {sweats inside their helmet and asks how much air we have left|keeps looking back toward the lander with wide eyes|jumps at every creak in the hull|wonders aloud if we can just leave right now}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Cut through and bring the kit up.
Take the tin and finish the line.

b.text:
Two feet of snow, then a hatch: a proper one, steel, with a wheel, warm to the hand.
It is a bunker, and it is lit, and there is nobody in it, and the stove in the middle of the main room is burning something that is not wood and is not coal and does not go down as it burns.
b.bubba: "Alright," says Bubba, hands on hips, entirely happy. "Now we're talkin'. Sotto 'a neve, 'nu palazzo."

asides.paranoid: {member} {mutters that someone's definitely watching us from the shadows|checks their six three times and grips their holster|hisses that the signal frequency is rigged|whispers: "They knew we were coming. Look around."}
asides.scholarly: {member} {is already logging sensor anomalies with an annoyed grunt|scans the alloy and mutters about obsolete manufacturing dates|checks the survey records and complains about missing documentation|notes that the readings make zero thermodynamic sense}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Strip the place of anything useful.
Find out what the stove is burning.

c.text:
You keep a fire and you keep watch, and at some point between three and four in the morning the wood goes quiet in the way it goes quiet when the snow stops.
Something walks the line. It is upright. It stops at each blue mark and puts its hand on it, the way a person counts stairs in the dark, and it is coming this way at exactly the speed of somebody who is not in a hurry.

asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.timid: {member} is very still and very quiet and does everything right.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Let it come and speak to it.
Put the fire out and {Let it pass|Hold fire and wait|Stay hidden until it moves on|Let it walk by}.

d.text:
You get out, and it takes longer than it took to come in, and the last mile has blue marks on trees you swear you did not pass.
On the road you find the count in your own notebook in your own hand: ninety, then ninety-one, then a mark that is not a number.

a1.text:
The ice does not want to be cut and then, all at once, it does.
The coat pockets hold {paper}, a compass frozen to north whichever way you turn it, and a survey book with the last entry written from underneath the ice, in the same blue.

a2.text:
You take the tin and you paint the ninety-first tree, and the wood makes a sound like a held breath being let go.
The cold breaks. Snow comes off branches for a hundred metres in every direction at once, and the clearing behind you is only a clearing, and the boots under the ice are only boots.
Somebody's work is finished. Something in your pack is heavier than it was.

b1.text:
Tinned food that is still good, forty litres of lamp oil, tools, wire, two coats and a crate of the kind of ammunition nobody stocks any more.
You take what three people can carry uphill through snow, which is less than you would like and more than you should.

b2.text:
You open the door of the stove.
What is in there is not fuel. It is looking back, and it has been burning for a very long time, and it would like the door shut, or opened all the way.

c1.text:
It stops at your fire, puts its hand on the tree beside you as if the tree were the next number, and waits.
You talk. Doesn't, but it turns its head when you get to the part it wants, and when you have got it right it takes something out of the snow at your feet that was not there before and puts it in your hands.

c2.text:
You kill the fire and it goes by close enough to hear it counting, and it counts in a language that stops being a language about halfway along.
In the morning the blue marks are gone off every tree, and the line is still there, worn into the snow, and it goes somewhere you will not be going today.

b1_m.text:
Tinned food that is still good, forty litres of lamp oil, tools, wire, two coats and a crate of the kind of ammunition nobody stocks any more.
And a duty board by the door, with {four|five} names on it and a rota written up to the end of next month, and the most recent tick is against {yesterday|two days ago|a date this week}.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Somebody is on shift.|That tick is fresh. We are in their house.|Take what you like, but be quick about it.}"
asides.any: {member} {reads the rota twice|puts a hand on the stove|looks at the door}

choices.text: Strip it and go before anybody comes back.
Wait for whoever is on shift.
Work out what the rota is a rota for.

b1_wait.text:
Four hours in a warm bunker in a wood that is {forty below|cold enough to kill|not survivable outside}, which is the easiest waiting anybody has done all year.
Whoever comes in at dusk is {nineteen|very young|younger than the rota}, is alone, is not armed, and is visibly relieved to find people, and has not had anybody to talk to since {the autumn|October|a long time ago}.

b1_rota.text:
It is not a watch rota. It is a {feeding|stoking|burn} rota, and the column headings are hours, and the thing that has to be done at each of them is done at the stove.
Which puts the party's understanding of the bunker, the wood, the ninety blue trees and the smoke that comes up through two feet of snow in an entirely different order, and it is now {four hours|two hours|not long} until the next entry is due.

c2_m.text:
The fire goes out and it goes by close enough to hear it counting, and it counts in a language that stops being a language about halfway along.
It stops at {the thirtieth|a tree|the trunk it has reached} and goes back three, and counts those three again, and gets a different answer, and stands there in the dark {for a long time|not moving|working at it}.

choices.text: Stay down. Let it work it out.
Count the three trees out loud, correctly.
Mark the three trees with the blue tin while it is turned away.

c2_count.text:
Three numbers said out loud from behind a dead fire, in the right language, in the right order, by somebody whose voice is not steady.
It takes them. It goes on. Ninety trees become ninety-three and the line runs on into wood the party cannot see, and at first light there is a path where there was no path, going the same way, and it is walkable.

c2_mark.text:
Three trunks marked at chest height with a tin of paint that is nearly empty, done in the dark, {four metres|not far|a stone's throw} from something that is counting.
It finds them. It is satisfied. It goes on and the wood lets go all at once, the way a held breath goes, and the party sleeps where they are and wakes with {the snow off the branches|a thaw|water dripping} and blue on their hands that does not wash off for a fortnight.

e_foresttropical.title: {The Canopy|Forty Metres Up And Somebody's Kettle|The Green Room}

n0.text:
Heat like a hand on the back of the neck, and a research platform forty metres up in the canopy with a rope ladder hanging down to head height.
There is a kettle up there. You can hear it. It has been whistling for as long as you have been standing here, and nobody has taken it off.
At the foot of the tree, arranged in a neat square: eleven pairs of boots.
Eleven camp beds, eleven plates, and {ten|nine} pairs of boots in the square by the ladder.
n0.emText:
Heat, green light, a platform forty metres up with a kettle screaming on it, and eleven pairs of boots laid out in a square at the foot of the tree.
The square is deliberate. Somebody made an arrangement here, and the arrangement is still running, and the kettle is the metronome. You are getting quite good at spotting other people's spells. Yours is the one you cannot see.
n0.bubba: Bubba counts the boots twice. "Eleven. Aoh. Eleven pairs an' no feet. Vuo' sape' 'a verita'? I don't like it. Let's go up."

asides.nervous: {member} {sweats inside their helmet and asks how much air we have left|keeps looking back toward the lander with wide eyes|jumps at every creak in the hull|wonders aloud if we can just leave right now}
asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.adventurous: {member} {grins: "Now this is what I signed up for."|is already climbing the rubble to see what's on the other side|can't wait to see what's behind the blast door|rushes ahead to get the first look}
asides.scholarly: {member} {is already logging sensor anomalies with an annoyed grunt|scans the alloy and mutters about obsolete manufacturing dates|checks the survey records and complains about missing documentation|notes that the readings make zero thermodynamic sense}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Climb.
Take a pair of boots and see what happens.
Shout up first.
Cut the ladder down and leave.

a.text:
The platform is boards and mesh and it moves under you. There is a stove, the kettle, eleven camp beds, and a table with a meal laid out on it for eleven, gone bad in the heat, except one plate, which has not.
There is nobody. There is also, quite clearly, somebody: you can hear the platform take weight when you are all standing still.

asides.paranoid: {member} {mutters that someone's definitely watching us from the shadows|checks their six three times and grips their holster|hisses that the signal frequency is rigged|whispers: "They knew we were coming. Look around."}
asides.calm: {member} takes the kettle off the heat, because somebody should.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Sit down at the good plate and eat.
Search the platform properly.

b.text:
You lift a pair off the square and the whole canopy above you moves at once, without wind, like an audience leaning in.
The kettle stops. In the silence you can hear something come down the trunk on the far side, fast, and stop, and wait for you to put them back.

choices.text: Put them back and step away.
Keep them.

asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

c.text:
Your voice goes up into the green and does not come back, and about four seconds later somebody up there answers, in your voice, saying the same words, in the same order, with one word changed.
The changed word is a name. It's not a name any of you has heard, and one of you flinches at it anyway.

asides.melancholic: "That was my mother's name," says {member}, very quietly, and then will not discuss it.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Answer it. Use the name.
Climb up and see who is doing it.

d.text:
It comes down in a heap of rope and the platform above you does not react at all, which is somehow worse.
Two days later, in {region}, a woman from a university you have never heard of buys your account of it over three coffees and pays for the coffees, and asks you, as you leave, whether the kettle was still going when you cut it.

a1.text:
It is the best meal you have had in a month and it is still hot and it should not be.
Halfway through, the platform takes weight opposite you and the chair moves, and you have the very strong sense of being kept company by somebody being polite about not appearing.
When you finish there is a gift under the plate, in the way there always is when you eat what is offered properly.

a2.text:
Eleven field notebooks, all of them useful, and one of them wrong: the last three weeks are written by a hand that gets better at handwriting each day, the way somebody learns.
You take the eleven, and the mesh floor under the wrong one is worn where something has sat there a great deal.

b1.text:
You put them back in the square, and the canopy relaxes, and the kettle starts again.
On the way out you find a pair of boots on the track that fits one of you exactly. They were not there on the way in. Everybody agrees not to talk about it, and everybody keeps them.

b2.text: The thing that came down the trunk would like them back and it is not going to ask twice.

c1.text:
You say the name into forty metres of green and the wood answers by going completely, absolutely silent: no insects, no birds, no leaf noise.
Into that silence, something comes down to head height and looks at whichever of you flinched, and gives them what it has been holding for eleven people's worth of time.

a2_m.text:
Eleven field notebooks, all of them useful, and one of them wrong: the last three weeks are written by a hand that gets better at handwriting each day.
The first entries in it are {barely legible|a child's|shapes}. The last ones are indistinguishable from the notebook next to them, including the signature, and the date on the last one is {today|this week|two days ago}.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Something is learning to be one of them.|It is up to eleven. We are the twelfth.|Put the book down and go down the ladder.}"
asides.any: {member} {compares the two hands side by side|looks at the ten pairs of boots and then at the beds|counts the plates again}

choices.text: Take all eleven notebooks and climb down.
Work out which of the eleven it has been copying.
Leave the eleventh notebook and take the other ten.

a2_copy.text:
It has not been copying one of them. It has been copying {all of them in turn|each in order|one a week}, and the order is the order of the camp beds, and it has reached the last bed.
That bed is made. The notebook belonging to it is the only one that is not on the table: it is under the pillow, unopened, blank, and the party is {four metres|not far|the width of the platform} from it when the ladder below starts taking weight.

a2_ten.text:
Ten notebooks in the pack and the eleventh left open on the table at the page where the handwriting is still going wrong.
The platform is quiet all the way down the ladder. {Four months|A season|Some months} later, in {region}, ten field notebooks are handed to an institute and ten families get a letter, and there is no eleventh family to write to, which is exactly the point.

b2_m.text:
The boots go in the pack and the canopy above holds its breath, and the thing that comes down the trunk comes down it {head first|the wrong way up|like water going the wrong way}.
It stops at head height, {four metres|a few paces|no distance} off, and puts out one hand, palm up, which is a gesture nothing in this wood should have.

choices.text: Keep the boots.
Put the boots in the hand.
Put something better in the hand instead.

b2_hand.text:
The boots go into the hand and the hand closes and goes back up the trunk with them, and the canopy lets go, and the kettle starts again.
There are {nine|eight} pairs in the square now. On the track out there is a pair that fits {leader} exactly, set down in the middle of the path, laced.

b2_trade.text:
What goes in the hand is {a notebook|a compass|something of the party's own that has a name in it}, which is worth more than boots to anything that is trying to learn how to be eleven people.
It takes it, and reads it, in the sense that it holds it and goes still for {nine seconds|a count of nine|a while}. Then it gives back the boots, and something else, and goes up the trunk, and the platform is empty of it from that day.

e_spiritwoods.title: {The Lantern|Somebody Is Walking A Light Between The Trees|Nine Steps Behind}

n0.text:
There is a light in the wood, and it is a lantern, and it is being carried: it swings the way a lamp swings on a person's arm, and it goes behind trunks and comes out the other side.
Whoever is carrying it stays exactly nine steps ahead. When you stop, it stops. When you go back, it comes back with you.
{smell}. Under that, faintly, {smell2}.
The lantern has been going the same round for as long as anybody in the nearest village has been alive, and the round is {nine|nine trees|nine turns} wide.
n0.emText:
A lantern in the wood, carried, nine steps ahead, matching you.
Everything here is thinner than it is elsewhere: the trees have the quality of a held idea. You know exactly where you are. You are in the part of the world that has not made up its mind, and you woke up in one of these on the first of January and walked out of it alone.
n0.bubba: "Nine steps," says Bubba, counting under his breath. "Nove. Ogni vota nove. That's a fella wit' a system, sugar."

asides.nervous: {member} {sweats inside their helmet and asks how much air we have left|keeps looking back toward the lander with wide eyes|jumps at every creak in the hull|wonders aloud if we can just leave right now}
asides.calm: {member} is walking at exactly the pace they were walking before, and it helps.
asides.artistic: {member} says the light is the wrong colour for oil, or gas, or anything they can name.
asides.fatalistic: {member} {sighs: "Well, we were going to die eventually."|shrugs: "If the reactor blows, at least it's quick."|mutters that the universe always finds a way to ruin your day|expects the worst and isn't disappointed}
asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Follow it, at nine steps, for as long as it goes.
Put your own light out and see what it does.
Call to it. Ask what it wants.
Walk directly at it, fast.

a.text:
An hour, maybe two: the wood does not agree with your watch.
It takes you to a clearing with a well in it, boarded over and weighted with a stone, and it sets the lantern down on the boards, and it is not there any more, and the lantern goes on burning.
Under the boards, something says a word. Once.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.scholarly: {member} {is already logging sensor anomalies with an annoyed grunt|scans the alloy and mutters about obsolete manufacturing dates|checks the survey records and complains about missing documentation|notes that the readings make zero thermodynamic sense}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Open the well.
Take the lantern and go.
Answer the word.

b.text:
You put your light out and the wood goes absolutely black except the lantern, which stops, and turns, and comes back three steps.
Then it waits, at six, which is the closest it has been, and holds itself a little higher, the way somebody holds a light up to see a face.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.paranoid: {member} {mutters that someone's definitely watching us from the shadows|checks their six three times and grips their holster|hisses that the signal frequency is rigged|whispers: "They knew we were coming. Look around."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Stand still and be looked at.
Light up again and close the distance.

c.text:
"Nine," it says. Not a voice: the number arrives in the same way a smell arrives.
"Nine," it says again, and the lantern swings, and you understand that it is not telling you the distance. It is telling you the price, and it is waiting to hear what you are counting in.

choices.text: Offer nine days.
Offer nine of something else.
Offer it nothing and say so plainly.

asides.hedonistic: {member} offers nine drinks. Doesn't laugh. Neither does anybody else.
asides.disciplined: {member} {follows standard breach protocol by the book|clears every corner with military precision|keeps a steady firing stance and monitors the sensors|checks the ammo count and maintains position}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

d.text:
You cover nine steps and it does not move, and at the end of the nine you are standing in front of a lantern hanging in the air at the height of a hand, with nothing holding it, in a wood that has gone completely still.
Then the lantern goes out, and everything that was standing nine steps behind you all afternoon is now standing directly in front of you, in the dark.

a1.text:
The stone comes off, and the boards come up, and the well is dry, and there is a ladder, and at the bottom of the ladder there is a room that is older than the well, with the wood's own name written round the walls about four hundred times.
What is in the middle of the room has been waiting to be given to somebody who came the whole way at nine steps and did not rush it.

a2.text:
It burns for eleven days in your pack without oil and then stops, and after that it is a lantern.
While it burns, nothing follows you at night, which you only notice properly on the twelfth day.

a3.text:
You answer it, and you get it right, which is largely luck and a little bit of listening.
The boards do not move. The word is said again, gently, and this time it is a thank you, and the wood opens a way out that is about a fifth as long as the way in.
On the path there is {relicWord}, put down where you will trip over it, because it has never had to give anybody anything before and it is not sure how.

b1.text:
It comes to arm's length and looks at each of you for as long as it takes, and at one of you for longer.
Then it puts the lantern in that person's hand, closes their fingers on the handle, and is not there, and the wood is an ordinary wood full of ordinary night.

c1.text:
Nine days go somewhere. You are not aware of losing them; the calendar is.
What you have when you come out of the wood is nine days older, nine days poorer, and holding something that is worth a great deal more than nine days.

c2.text:
Nine coins, nine steps, nine words, nine of anything: it takes what is offered, if it is offered in nines, which is the only rule it has ever had.
What it gives back is not what you asked for and is worth having anyway.

c3.text:
"Nothing," you say. "We have nothing for you and we are not going to pretend otherwise."
The lantern goes down, and stays down, and burns on the ground where it was set, and the wood lets you out in the direction you actually wanted rather than the direction it was taking you.
Honesty is not always paid. It is, however, always noticed.

a2_m.text:
The lantern is taken off its hook and it comes {easily|without argument|as though it had been put there for the purpose}, and it burns without oil.
What is standing where it was standing does not follow, but it does speak, once, and what it says is a question in the shape of a number, and the number is nine.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{It is asking what we will pay.|Everything out here costs nine.|We have taken something and it has noticed.}"
asides.any: {member} {holds the lantern out at arm's length|counts nine of something without being asked|does not let go of it}

choices.text: Take it and go. Do not answer.
Answer with nine of something.
Ask what the lantern is for before carrying it anywhere.

a2_for.text:
It is for the well. It has always been for the well: it is carried nine steps ahead of whoever is going to the well so that the well knows somebody is coming and has time to {compose itself|be ready|stop}.
Carrying it out of the wood does not break anything. It does mean that for {eleven days|as long as it burns|a while} there is a well somewhere with nothing walking ahead of it, and the party knows exactly what that costs and chooses it anyway.

c1_m.text:
Nine days are offered and the number is accepted the way a shop accepts a note: without ceremony, with a small movement of the lantern.
Then it waits, because nine days is a price and a price is paid at a counter, and the counter is {the well|the clearing|somewhere it intends to take the party}, and it starts walking.

choices.text: Follow it and pay.
Pay here. Sit down and let the nine days go.
Follow, but count the steps.

c1_here.text:
Sitting down in a wood and deliberately letting nine days go is the single strangest thing the party does all year, and it takes {four seconds|no time|an instant} from the inside.
From the outside it takes nine days. The wood is exactly as it was. The party is nine days hungrier, nine days thinner, and carrying something that was not in any pack when they sat down.

c1_steps.text:
Counted, the walk to the well is {nine hundred|nine hundred and nine|nine times nine times nine} steps, which is not a coincidence and is not a distance the clearing is from here.
Knowing that, it is possible to pay at the four hundred and fifty-first step instead of at the well, which is exactly half, and half is a price the lantern will take from somebody who has bothered to count. Four and a half days go. The party keeps the rest.

e_mountain.title: {The Cairn|Somebody Comes Up Here Every Week|The Offering At The Col}

n0.text:
Three hundred metres above the last house in {country}, at the col, there is a cairn with things left on it.
Not flowers. On the top stone, in a row: {offering}, {offering2}, and a third that somebody has taken away and left the mark of.
The stones are dry. It rained here two hours ago.
The offerings are sorted. Small ones on the top stone, heavier ones in the ring at the base, and none of them {rusted|weathered|spoiled} despite the weather.
n0.emText:
A cairn at the col with things left on it: {offering}, {offering2}, and the dry ring where a third stood until recently.
The stones are dry in weather that has soaked you to the shoulders. Something up here is holding a small patch of the world exempt, and doing it politely, and doing it every week.
n0.bubba: Bubba sets his hat on the stone next to the rest of it, thinks better of it, takes it back. "Nah. You don't leave nothin' at a table you ain't ate at. 'A regola e' chesta."

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.scholarly: {member} {is already logging sensor anomalies with an annoyed grunt|scans the alloy and mutters about obsolete manufacturing dates|checks the survey records and complains about missing documentation|notes that the readings make zero thermodynamic sense}
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.melancholic: {member} looks at the child's glove and has to walk to the edge of the col for a minute.
asides.grumpy: {member} {complains loudly about the freezing temperature|curses under their breath at the terrible footing|mutters that this job isn't worth the hazard pay|kicks a piece of debris and grunts in frustration}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Leave something of your own and go on.
Wait for whoever brings these up.
Take the cairn apart.
Follow the path the offerings come up.

a.text:
