d.emText:
She is delighted, and gets it out of the stack immediately, which means it was already in the stack.
It is four pages. Two are about what you have done. One is about what you are going to do. The fourth is in a hand that is not hers and is dated 1984, the year you were born in Wimbledon, and the only thing written on it is a list of what was taken and where each part of it went.
She watches you read it. "I'm not allowed to give you that," she says, and does not take it back.
d.bubba: Bubba reads the fourth page over your shoulder and, for the first time since you have known him, says absolutely nothing.

a_m.text:
You read eleven pages of somebody's worst year and the number is on the tip of the tongue and the courtroom is waiting for it.
On page eleven, in the margin, in pencil, in a hand that is not the file's, there is {a note|four words|something added}, and it is not about the accused. It is about whoever is reading the file, and it is {addressed|correct|written to the party}.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Somebody wrote in the margin for us.|Do not read the number out until you have read the pencil.|That is her hand. Or it is not.}"
asides.any: {member} {reads the margin twice|looks at her|does not say the number}

choices.text: Say the number anyway.
Read the margin out loud instead.
Refuse. Say you will not sentence somebody you have never met.

a_margin.text:
Four words read out in an empty courtroom by somebody who has worked out, in the last {nine seconds|moment|minute}, that they are not the reader of this file but an item in it.
She takes her feet off the bench. The file goes back in the stack unsentenced, which has not happened in {a very long time|this court|anybody's memory}, and what she says next is said to a person rather than to a room.

d_m.text:
She is delighted. She gets it out of the stack immediately, which means it was in the stack, and puts it on the bench face down and leaves her hand on it.
It is {thin|four pages|not as thick as the others}. She does not open it. She says that the party can read it, or she can read it, or it can go back in the stack, and that all three are real choices and that she has never offered anybody the third one.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{The third one is the offer. The other two are furniture.|Four pages. That is not much of a life.|Do not let her read it.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts a hand on the file|looks at the stack|says nothing at all}

choices.text: Read it.
Let her read it out loud.
Put it back in the stack unopened.

d_her.text:
She reads four pages of somebody's file out loud in an empty courtroom to the person it is about, in a voice that is {careful|not unkind|doing its best}, and does not skip anything.
There is one page the party did not know was in it. There is one line on that page that is not true and she stops, and goes back, and reads it again, and looks up, and asks {who wrote that|where that came from|which of us is wrong}.

d_back.text:
Four pages back into a stack, face down, unopened, by somebody who has just been offered their own file by the only person who has it.
She takes her hand off it. Then she says {"good"|"all right then"|"that is the first time"}, and shuts the court, and the door in the wall is a wall again by the time anybody is four paces down the street.

z_eris_fair.title: {She Has Bought All The Tickets|The Whole Fair, For The Afternoon|Nobody Else Is Allowed In}

n0.text:
{The fair is running: lights, generator, waltzer, four stalls, the smell of hot sugar. There is nobody on any of it.
{eris} is at the gate with a roll of tickets she has bought outright, all of them, and a look of somebody who has arranged a surprise and is not sure it was a good idea.
"I've got it till six," she says. "I paid. Ask them. They're all in the van having their tea."|The situation is pretty straightforward: The fair is running: lights, generator, waltzer, four stalls, the smell of hot sugar. There is nobody on any of it.

The generator is running and there is nobody on any ride and every light is on.
n0.emText:
A fair, running, lit, empty. {eris} at the gate with every ticket in the roll and the operators sitting in a van having their tea because she paid them to.
"I've got it till six. I paid."
The waltzer will throw you into the rail. The hook-a-duck will not hook. The candy floss will go in your hair. She has arranged all of it and she has also, genuinely, bought a fair for an afternoon because she wanted company, and both of those things are true at once and that is the entire problem with her.
n0.bubba: Bubba is on the waltzer before the sentence is finished, hat in the air. "AOOOH! Jamme ja'! Sugar, get on, she paid!"

asides.hedonistic: {member} is gone. {member} has been gone since the word 'waltzer'.
asides.nervous: {member} {sweats inside their helmet and asks how much air we have left|keeps looking back toward the lander with wide eyes|jumps at every creak in the hull|wonders aloud if we can just leave right now}
asides.artistic: {member} says an empty fair with the lights on is the most beautiful thing they have seen since {timeAgo}.
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: {Go on everything. All of it. Twice.|Try to go on everything. all of it. twice|Go ahead and go on everything. all of it. twice|Take a chance and go on everything. all of it. twice}
{Ask her why.|Try to ask her why|Go ahead and ask her why|Take a chance and ask her why}

{Get the operators out of the van and open the fair to the town.|Try to get the operators out of the van and open the fair to the town|Go ahead and get the operators out of the van and open the fair to the town|Take a chance and get the operators out of the van and open the fair to the town}

a_m.text:
Four hours of an empty fair with the lights on and nobody queueing, and the waltzer at a speed the operators would never have allowed.
At about the third hour the generator {coughs|stumbles|runs rough}, and every light on the field dips, and in the half-second of dark the fair is {not empty|full|the way a fair is on a Saturday} and every ride has people on it.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{There were four hundred people here for half a second.|Do not ask her. Look at her face.|The fair is not empty. We are the ones who are not here.}"
asides.any: {member} {stops the waltzer|looks at her|counts what they saw}

choices.text: Say nothing and go on the waltzer again.
Go and fix the generator.
Ask her whose fair this is.

a_gen.text:
It is {a fuel filter|the governor|a lead} and it takes {ten minutes|a quarter of an hour|no time} on a field with a torch held by a goddess who is genuinely interested in what you are doing with a screwdriver.
The lights come up and stay up and do not dip again. The fair runs until {four in the morning|it gets light|the generator is dry}, and nobody else ever appears on it, and she does not say thank you and does something considerably better instead.

a_whose.text:
It is not hers. That is the answer and she gives it straight: the fair belongs to {the four hundred|the people in the half-second|whoever was on it}, and it has been running for them since {the night it closed|a particular evening|the year of the accident}, and she comes to it because it is the only place she goes where nobody is in front of her or running.
What she is doing, on a field, at that speed, with the lights on, is {queueing|waiting her turn|being one of them}, and she has never told anybody that.

q_beacon.title: {The Keeper's List|What The Mast Needs|Dead Air}

n0.text:
{brokenthing} stands over {place}, dead, panels open to {ground}. {asker} is halfway up it with {instrument} and comes down without hurrying, because hurrying stopped helping {a while ago|on day two|before the party landed}.
The list of what it needs is short. It needs {qty} {material}. {sound}, and the mast does nothing about it. He lets you hear that.
{member} walks the mast's footing while the talking happens and finds the same thing twice: the anchor bolts have been out and back in, recently, by somebody who did not have the right spanner and did not care.
Whoever serviced this last was not the keeper.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.disciplined: {member} {follows standard breach protocol by the book|clears every corner with military precision|keeps a steady firing stance and monitors the sensors|checks the ammo count and maintains position}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Hand over the {material}.
Fix it out of the ship's own spares.
Ask what a working mast is worth first.

b.text:
The keeper thinks about it {for nine seconds|a while|without blinking}. Payment is named: {payment}.
The mast, it is mentioned on the way back up, was listening for what moves out here before it went dark. It has not been listening for {few} days now, and the keeper has been sleeping in shifts of one.

choices.text: That will do. Hand over the {material}.
Not at that price.

g.text:
The panels close over the new {material} and the mast comes back with a sound like a struck shelf.
The first thing it hears gets written out longhand and handed over, along with what was promised, and the keeper {stops sleeping in shifts|sleeps a whole night for once|puts the kettle on and sits down}.

f.text:
It takes {an afternoon|four hours|the rest of the light} and it is not pretty, but a governor off the ship's own stores will hold the load if nobody tells it what it used to be.
The mast comes up. The keeper pays over the odds, on the grounds that a fix that costs the fixer is a different {class of fix|kind of fix altogether|order of favour}.

x.text:
The spare that fit was not a spare. Something back at the ship will miss it at the worst possible moment, and the flywheel had one more turn in it, which {leader} finds out at close range.
The mast stays dark. The keeper says nothing, which is {worse than saying something|worse than anything they could say|the worst of the available responses}.

e.text:
The mast stays dark and the keeper goes back up it, alone, with the whistle in the rebreather keeping its own time.
{member} takes a bearing on the site {in case|for the log|without being asked}, and nobody talks for the first kilometre back.

g_m.text:
The panels come off properly this time and the fault is not the fault the keeper described. {The {material} will fit|The part will go in|It will take the {material}}, but it will fit over the top of something that was put in wrong on purpose: a shunt, hand-made, with the maker's initials filed halfway off.
The keeper watches the party find it and says nothing at all, which is its own kind of answer.

asides.cynical: {member}, quietly: "{Someone wanted this mast deaf.|That's sabotage with a signature on it.|Somebody paid for this silence.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts a thumb over the filed initials and looks at the horizon|photographs the shunt before anybody can object|counts the days since the mast went dark, out loud}

choices.text: Fit the {material} over the shunt. Not our sky, not our argument.
Pull the shunt and read what is filed off it.
Ask the keeper who has been up the mast besides them.

g_name.text:
Under the file marks the initials come back up in raking light, and they are not initials: they are a station code, and the station is {three valleys over|one ridge east|the only other thing out here with power}.
The mast goes up working. The keeper writes the code on the inside of the panel door in a hand that presses too hard, and pays the party in what they came for and a little more, for the part of the job nobody asked for.

g_burn.text:
The shunt comes out of the housing {live|hot|still carrying}, which nobody expected of a mast that has been dead for {few} days, and it takes the skin off two fingers on the way.
The mast works afterwards. The initials are gone for good, burned flat by their own last trick, and the keeper pays what was agreed and not a coin over.

g_told.text:
Nobody, says the keeper. Then, after the length of time it takes to decide to say a true thing: nobody since the supply run, and the supply run was {two|three} men and one of them went up the mast to be helpful.
The {material} goes in. The mast comes up. The keeper gives the party the supply manifest as well as the payment, and asks, without asking, that somebody look at the names on it later.

f_m.text:
The ship's spares are laid out on a sheet on {ground} and there is exactly one governor in the box that will take the load, and it is the one the ship is currently using.
{asker} understands the arithmetic before anybody explains it, and offers, seriously, to trade something back: the mast's own recorder, with {few} days of dead air on it and the last hour before the dark on the front of the reel.

choices.text: Take the governor out of the ship. Both of us limp.
Take the recorder instead and build a governor out of scrap.
Leave the ship whole. Tell them what to order.

f_reel.text:
The scrap governor is ugly, undersized and correct, and it comes up on the second attempt with the load singing through it.
The reel is the payment and the reel is worth it: the last hour before the mast went dark has something on it that was not weather, repeating, patient, and getting {closer|louder|nearer} on every pass.

f_bodge.text:
The scrap governor holds for {eleven|nine|six} minutes and then lets go in a way that puts the whole mast head through its own cycle at once.
Nothing is {on fire|actually alight|burning} afterwards, which everyone agrees is the good news. The reel is in the party's pack and the mast is still dark and the keeper has stopped being polite about it.

f_order.text:
It takes an hour to write down exactly what to order, in the part numbers the supply run will actually recognise, with the two substitutions that will also work in the margin.
The mast stays dark for {another fortnight|three more weeks|a while yet}. The keeper says so, and shakes hands anyway, and the party leaves with nothing except somebody a long way out here who will remember them.

q_stranded.title: {Two Hundred Days|The Lander At The Wrong Angle|Parts And Sky}

n0.text:
A lander sits at {place} at the wrong angle, and {asker} has been living in it {long enough to have a system|long enough to have opinions about the view|since before the last storm season}.
The ask is exact, rehearsed, word-perfect: {qty} {material}, for the {stabiliser|fuel governor|coil housing}, and then the sky again. {wrongness}.
The ground around the lander is wrong in a way that takes a minute to name: there are no paths worn into it. Two hundred days of living somewhere and nothing has walked anywhere twice.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Hand it over and help with the fitting.
Something here is off. Look the lander over first.
Offer a lift instead of parts.

h.text:
The fitting takes an hour and the castaway's hands know the work better than the manual does.
Payment is the only coin left aboard: something learned in two hundred days of listening to {tone}, taught on the walk back to the pad, once, properly, with {the wind for a blackboard|the wind taking most of it|nothing to write on but the air}.

w.text:
The lander has never flown. The undercarriage grows straight out of {ground}, and under the hull there are {many} small heaps of the kind of kit a courier carries and a courier is never parted from.
Whatever is doing the asking has been fed by the asking for a long time.

choices.text: Back away without changing pace.
Put it down, here, where it sleeps.

t.text:
It looks like a lander right up until {the hold closes|it opens along a seam no lander has|the ramp comes down the wrong way}.
It's not {a hold|anything of the kind|a hold and never was}.

k.text: It stops pretending the moment {the first shot goes in|anybody raises anything|it is looked at properly}, and the lander shape comes off it {like weather|the way a coat comes off|in one long motion}.

l.text:
The lift is refused {fast|flatly|before it is fully offered}, with both hands, before the sentence is even finished.
Parts, it says. Parts and nothing else. Doesn't look at the party when it says it; it looks at {the pack|the straps|what is in the pack} the party is carrying.

choices.text: Hand over the {material} then.
Leave, and keep the pack on the far side of the group.

e2.text:
The lander is still in the mirrors a long way past where {the horizon|the curve of the ground|distance itself} should have taken it.
Nobody suggests going back for a second look, and nobody {has to say why|says why|asks why}.

h_m.text:
The stabiliser bay is open before the party has finished agreeing, and the hands working in it are good hands, fast and sure and entirely wrong at the wrists.
The fitting will take an hour. The castaway talks the whole time, and everything it says about two hundred days here is {true, checkable and dull|verifiable and boring|the kind of detail nobody invents}, which is the part that will bother {member} later.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Nobody is this normal.|It is doing an impression of a person and it has practised.|Nothing out here talks this much.}"
asides.any: {member} {keeps the pack on the far side of the group without being obvious about it|watches the wrists|does not put anything down}

choices.text: Fit the part and take the payment.
Watch its hands and name what is wrong with them.
Fit the part, take nothing, leave early.

h_wrist.text:
{The wrists do not rotate.|The wrists never turn.|Nothing at the wrist moves at all.} The whole forearm turns instead, smoothly, in a socket that is not in any body the party has ever opened, and once it is seen it cannot be unseen.
It notices being seen. The hour ends there, politely, on both sides, with the part fitted and the party walking backwards for the first {forty|fifty|sixty} metres.

h_late.text:
The hour goes by and the hands are only hands, and it is a long way back to the pad before {member} works out what was wrong with them, which is the worst possible time to work it out.
The lesson that was taught on the walk back is real. So is the feeling, arriving late, that the lesson was the point of the entire afternoon.

h_early.text:
The part goes in, the payment is declined twice, and the party is over the ridge before the light goes.
Nothing follows. {member} checks anyway, {three times|twice, then once more|at every rise}, and the lander sits at its wrong angle getting smaller, and nothing follows.

q_cache.title: {Sealed On Purpose|The Case Under The Ice|What The Seal Is For}

n0.text:
A case of {maker}'s make sits under {remnant}, sealed, with {a dial that turns too smoothly|a latch that has been forced once already and reset|writing worn down to dents}.
{instrument} reads something inside worth the walk. {hazard}, so the walk was not free either.
The dents in the lid are writing, and the writing was done from the inside.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.impulsive: {member} has already tried the latch once, gently, as a scientific matter.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Work the seal properly.
Break it.
Leave it sealed.

a.text:
The seal gives the way a good seal gives: {all at once, undamaged, almost gratefully|cleanly, without argument, as if it had been waiting|in one movement, and stays whole}.
Inside, packed the way things are packed by somebody who expected to come back: everything in order, nothing spoiled, and room left at the top for {one more thing that never arrived|something that was never brought|a last item nobody carried in}.

c.text: The case opens {the hard way|badly|with a noise the whole site hears}. About half of what was shelved inside survives the opening, which everybody agrees, afterwards, is {still half|better than none|half more than nothing}.

b.text:
Whatever the seal was holding shut, it was not holding it shut against thieves.
It was holding it {IN|SHUT FROM THE INSIDE}. The case is empty now, and the air around it costs the party {something|a good deal|more than anybody says out loud} on the way back.

e.text:
Sealed by {maker}, left sealed. {member} takes a rubbing of the lid for the diary and puts {ground} back over it the way it was found.
Some walks are for knowing where a thing is, not for having it.

a_m.text:
The seal comes off clean and the case is not a case. It is a lid on a shaft, and the shaft is lined, and the lining goes down further than {instrument} has patience for.
What is on the top shelf of it is worth the walk on its own: packed, dated, labelled by somebody with a system. What is under the top shelf is dark, and the air coming up out of it is {warmer than the day|moving|the wrong temperature entirely}.

choices.text: Take the top shelf and put the lid back.
Read the labels properly before anybody carries anything.
Go down the shaft.

a_label.text:
The labels are an index, and the index is not of the contents. It is of the shaft: what is on each shelf, in order, all the way down, in a hand that gets {worse|shakier|harder to read} with depth and stops entirely {four|three|five} shelves from the bottom.
The party takes the top shelf, and takes the index, which is worth considerably more than the top shelf.

a_down.text:
Four shelves down the lining stops being lining and starts being the thing the lining was copying.
The party comes back up with full packs, {faster than they went down|two at a time|without discussing it}, and the lid goes back on with {ground} piled over it and a cairn on top that nobody agreed to build.

n0.text:
The one way through {place} is a gap wide enough for one, and something is sitting in it. Not hiding. Sitting.
It has {a bowl|a set of scales|an open crate} in front of it and patience behind it. The toll is {qty} {material}. The alternative is not discussed, because it does not need to be.
There are bones in the scree on the far side, arranged the way a tidy person arranges things they have finished with.

asides.aggressive: {member} measures the gap, then the thing in it, and does not share the result.
asides.calm: {member} notes that a toll implies traffic, and that traffic implies the toll gets paid.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Pay the toll.
Stare it down.
Go through it.

p.text:
It counts without touching, {nods once|inclines whatever that is|makes a small formal movement}, and leans back a whole hand's width, which is apparently the open position.
As the last of the party passes, it puts something of its own in the bowl and pushes it after them: change, or a tip, or a receipt. {The categories may not apply|None of those three words quite fits|Nobody decides which}.

s.text:
{It blinks first|It looks away first|Something in it gives first}.
It stands, which takes longer than it should and involves more of it than seemed to be there, and steps out of the gap, and leaves the bowl where it sits, full, as a matter the party is invited to {interpret|make of what they will|settle among themselves}.

f2.text: The stare goes wrong {somewhere in the middle|about four seconds in|at the point where it should have ended}. What is at the bottom of it looks back up the whole length of it, and the gap stops being {a toll booth|an arrangement|anything with rules in it}.

fgt.text: It stands up before the {second|third} step. There is {more of it than the gap explained|a great deal more of it than the gap suggested|more of it than there was room for}.

p_m.text:
{It counts the toll without touching it|It counts without touching anything|It reads the toll off the bowl without reaching for it} and does not move, because the toll was never the whole price.
It puts one appendage flat on the rock beside the bowl and waits, and the meaning is clear enough: something else is owed, and it will take {a name, a story, or an hour of somebody's time|a name, a story, or an hour|an hour, a story, or a name}, and it does not care which.

choices.text: Give it a name. Not one of ours.
Sit down and tell it something true.
Put a hand flat on the rock beside its own.

p_lie.text:
The name given is a real name belonging to nobody the party will ever meet again, and it takes it, and folds whatever it has instead of a face around it, and is satisfied.
The gap opens. On the far side, {a hundred metres|a while} on, there is a marker with that same name cut into it, freshly, and nobody looks at anybody for a kilometre.

p_caught.text:
{It knows.|It knew.|It has known the whole time.} Not in the moment: it lets the name be given, lets it be finished, and then puts the appendage down flat in a way that means the lie is on the scales too now, and the scales are its own.
{The toll doubles.|The toll is doubled.|The price goes up by exactly as much again.} It is paid, out of the pack, because the alternative is standing behind it.

p_hand.text:
The rock under both hands goes cold enough to hurt and stays that way for a count of nine, and something moves through the contact that is not warmth and is not information and is definitely not nothing.
It gets up. It is the first time it has got up for anybody. The gap is left open behind it, and the bowl is left full, and it walks off into {the narrows|the scree|whatever is past the narrows} without looking back.

fgt_m.text:
It stands before the {second|third} step, and standing is the whole argument: there is more of it than the gap explained, and it unfolds upward with the unhurried confidence of something that has done this at this exact spot many times.
There is a moment, about {a second|two seconds|a breath} long, in which it is still possible to stop walking.

choices.text: Keep walking.
Read the bones on the far side. How does it fight?
Stop walking. Put the toll in the bowl.

fgt_read.text:
The bones say the same sentence a dozen times: everything it has finished with was broken {high, on the left, once, hard|on the left, high, in one go}.
The party goes in knowing which side to stand on. It is still the worst {four|five|three} minutes of the week, but it is four minutes, and everybody walks out of the narrows on their own feet.

q_wager.title: {Stones|The Game At The Fire|Fair, Which Is Worse}

n0.text:
{asker} has a fire going at {place} and a game laid out on a flat rock: {stakegame}.
The rules take a minute to learn and a life to like. The stake is coin. The pot on the other side of the rock is {visible|real|already sitting there, which is either confidence or bait}.
There is a second set of stones in a bag by {asker}'s knee, worn smoother than the ones on the rock.

asides.hedonistic: {member} is sitting down before the rules are finished.
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Sit down and play.
Play for information instead of coin.
Watch a few rounds from the warm side of the fire.

w2.text:
The pot crosses the rock. {asker} pays without a word and re-racks the stones for the next traveller, because there is always a next traveller.
The fire is shared for an hour on the strength of it, and the directions given at parting are, as far as anyone can later tell, {honest|entirely honest|correct in every particular}.

l2.text:
The stake is gone in {few} moves.
The game was fair. Everybody at the fire is quite sure the game was fair, which is {somehow worse|the part that stings|worse than being cheated would have been}.

i.text:
The winnings are not coin. They are {a lesson|the teaching itself|a thing that has to be shown}: the game itself, taught across the fire, once, properly, with the mistakes named as they happen.
It travels. Everything else on this rock stays where it is, but the game {travels|goes with them|packs}.

l3.text:
Somewhere in the third round it becomes clear the information has been flowing the other way.
{asker} now knows where the party landed, what the ship carries, and which of the party sleeps lightest, and paid for {none of it|not a coin of it|precisely nothing}.

v.text:
An hour goes by at the fire watching other people lose {interestingly|in ways worth studying|slowly and then all at once}.
No money changes hands in either direction, which by the local arithmetic makes the party the evening's {big winner|only winner|clear winner}.

v_m.text:
An hour at the warm side of the fire is an hour of watching {asker}'s hands, and the hands are the game.
The stones from the bag come out once, in the fourth round, against a traveller who is losing anyway and does not notice. Nobody at the fire notices. The fire is very good at not noticing.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{There it is.|Second bag. Every table has one.|Told you.}"
asides.any: {member} {watches the bag and not the rock|counts the swap under their breath|says nothing and keeps watching}

choices.text: Say nothing. Enjoy the fire.
Call it, quietly, to {asker} alone.
Call it out loud, to the whole fire.

v_quiet.text:
It is taken the way a professional takes it: no denial, no offence, a long look, and the bag goes back into the coat.
The rest of the evening is honest and {asker} plays it that way, badly, and loses, and pays, and afterwards teaches the party the swap itself at the edge of the firelight as a matter of professional respect.

v_loud.text:
The fire stops being a fire and becomes a room with people in it.
{asker} is gone over the rocks inside twenty seconds, the pot goes with them, and the travellers left behind divide their opinion of the party evenly between grateful and furious, and it is the furious half that is still there at dawn.

q_specimen.title: {The One That Keeps Coming Back|A Fixed Hour|What Took Theirs}

n0.text:
{asker} wants one animal out of {ground} dead or carried off: the one that has taken {few} of theirs and will be back for more.
It comes at {a fixed hour|the same hour every day|whatever hour the wind drops}, which is the only polite thing about it. There is payment: {payment}.
The kills are in a line. Whatever is doing it is not hunting the herd, it is walking a route, and the route ends at {asker}'s door.

asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.nurturing: {member} asks after the ones already taken, and the silence answers before anybody does.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Track it to where it sleeps first.
Wait for the hour and take it head on.
Not this one. Not today.

tr.text:
The trail reads like a sentence with the grammar wrong, but it reads.
It sleeps below {remnant}, downwind of its own front door, alone, which changes {the whole arithmetic of the afternoon|everything about the afternoon|the shape of the afternoon}.

amb.text: {Half an hour|An hour|Twenty minutes} into the tracking it becomes clear from the freshness of the ground that the roles have been reversed for at least {twenty minutes|half an hour|some time now}.

head.text: {It is punctual|It arrives on the hour|It comes when they said it would}. That is the last thing about the next ten minutes that goes to {anybody's plan|the plan|plan at all}.

e3.text:
{asker} nods like somebody filing an answer with all the other answers.
The fire gets built up a little higher for the coming hour, and the party is a long way off before it {burns down|goes out|is out}.

tr_m.text:
The trail reads like a sentence with the grammar wrong, and it reads all the way to a scrape under {remnant} where something large sleeps downwind of its own front door.
It is asleep now. It will not be asleep at the hour. There is time to do exactly one thing well.

choices.text: Take it in its sleep.
Set the ground against it and let it come to us.
Drive it off the route instead of killing it.

tr_trap.text:
The ground is made ready in the last hour of light: the line narrowed, the footing spoiled, the one good approach left open on purpose.
It walks into all of it exactly on the hour, and the fight is over before it is properly a fight. {asker} pays the full price and then some, having watched the whole thing from the roof.

tr_snap.text:
The line is set wrong by {one pace|a single pace|half a pace} and the thing that walks into it is not the thing it was set for: something smaller, earlier, noisier, and now extremely awake.
By the time the real one arrives the whole approach is ruined and everybody is standing {in the open|out in the open|where nobody wanted to be standing}.

tr_turn.text:
It is not driven off so much as argued with, in the only language it has: noise at the right pitch, in the right place, three nights running, until the route stops being worth walking.
{asker} gets no corpse and does not much care, because the kills stop. The payment is smaller and comes with a standing invitation to the fire that turns out, over the following season, to be worth a great deal more than the payment.

e3_m.text:
{asker} nods like somebody filing an answer with all the other answers, and starts building the fire up higher for the coming hour, alone, with what they have, which is not much.
The party is a hundred metres out when it becomes clear that the fire will not be high enough.

choices.text: Keep walking.
Turn round. Stay for the hour.
Leave what we can spare at the door and go.

e3_gift.text:
The {material} is left inside the door with no explanation, which is the only way it would have been accepted.
What happens at the hour happens without the party there to see it. Some weeks later, a long way from {place}, somebody the party has never met buys them a meal on the strength of a description and will not say who sent them.

qe_pump.title: {The Pump|Dead Iron At The Worst Hour|What The Yard Needs}

n0.text:
The pump at {place} has died at the worst possible point of the week, {weather}, and {stranger} is standing over it holding {tool} in a way that says {tool} has already been tried.
What it needs is {qty} {material}. The merchant that stocks it is {distance}, and shut on account of {misfortune}, and the trough line goes dry by dark.
The yard behind the pump has {nine|eleven|a good many} beasts in it and all of them are already at the fence, watching the trough, which is how everybody knows exactly how long this has left.

asides.nurturing: {member} has the side panel off before anybody has agreed to anything.
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Hand over the {material}.
Strip it down and machine the part from scrap.
Man the hand pump until the job is done, however long that is.

g.text:
The part goes in, the pump picks up mid-stroke like it never stopped, and the yard comes back to life around it.
Payment is {payment}, pressed on the party over two refusals, and dinner is not optional {either|and is not up for discussion|at all}.

f.text:
There is a part in the scrap pile that has never heard of the pump but can be talked into the job with a file and an hour.
It runs rough and it runs. {stranger} watches the whole operation like a sermon and pays over the asking, {on principle|out of principle|because it was done properly}.

x.text:
The flywheel had one more turn in it, which {leader} finds out with the smallest bone in one hand.
The pump stays dead. The dinner happens anyway, out of guilt, and is very good, which does not entirely settle {the grimorie|matters|it}.

m.text:
Two hours on the hand pump in shifts, {weather}, with the light going.
The trough line holds. By the end half the district has come past to watch, and the party leaves with more invitations than it can eat through in a month.

g_m.text:
The {material} is out of the pack and on the bench before the sentence is finished, and {stranger} has the side panel off to meet it.
The housing underneath is not what either of them expected: somebody has been in here before, recently, and has fitted a part that is {nearly right|almost the right part|the right shape and the wrong metal} and has bodged the seat to make it go.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Somebody has already been paid for this once.|That is a repair with a bill attached.|Look at that seat and tell me that was free.}"
asides.any: {member} {runs a thumb round the seat and whistles|holds the lamp closer without being asked|looks at the bodge for a long moment}

choices.text: Fit ours over the top and get the trough running.
Cut the seat back to true first. Do it once, properly.
Find out who fitted the wrong part.

g_true.text:
Cutting a seat true by hand in a yard in {weather} is not a job anybody would choose, and it takes {two hours|the rest of the light|longer than the job is worth}.
The pump runs afterwards the way it ran when it was new, which {stranger} notices inside a minute and does not stop talking about for the rest of the evening. The payment is doubled, twice, over the party's objections.

g_scrap.text:
The seat goes from bodged to ruined in about {one pass|a single pass|four seconds} of a tool that was never meant for it.
The {material} is now no use to anybody and neither is the housing. The trough line goes dry at dark, exactly as advertised, and the beasts are walked {two fields over|to the next farm|a long way} in the morning by everyone including the party.

g_who.text:
It takes {one name|a name and a half|two questions at the right gate}: a man who does the rounds of the district fitting nearly-right parts at proper prices to people who cannot check.
The pump is fixed with the party's own {material}. The name goes round the district by {nightfall|the following evening|dark} and does not come back, and three other yards find out what is in their housings before the week is out.

m_m.text:
Two hours on the hand pump in shifts, {weather}, with the light going, and the trough line holding by {about a finger's width|a hand|not much}.
At the end of the second hour it becomes clear this will hold all night if somebody keeps at it, and that {stranger} intends to be that somebody, alone, having already been up since {four|three|before light}.

choices.text: Take the night in shifts with them.
Rig a counterweight so the pump works itself.
Hand it over at dark and go.

m_night.text:
Four hours on, four off, in a barn that smells of {everything a barn smells of|hot iron and beasts|hay and wet wool}, with somebody else's animals making somebody else's noise all night.
The line holds. The party is fed at dawn like visiting royalty and sleeps until noon in a loft, and there is a standing bed in this district from that morning onward.

m_rig.text:
A beam, a bucket of stone, and the trough line's own overflow to fill it: the pump lifts itself on the down-stroke and resets on the up, slowly, {all night|for as long as the water runs|indefinitely}.
It is still working eleven months later. People come to look at it. Nobody in the district has ever been able to explain which of the party thought of it, including the party.

qe_debt.title: {Forty Minutes Ahead Of The Bailiff|The Boxes On The Step|Small Arithmetic}

n0.text:
{stranger} is on the step of a house at {place} with the door open behind and everything they own in {few} boxes.
The bailiff is forty minutes away by {vehicle}. The debt is real and the arithmetic is small, and the house is not small, and that is the whole story in one sentence.
The boxes are packed the way people pack when they have done it before: {heavy at the bottom, kitchen last|properly|by room, and labelled}.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Pay it.
Read the paperwork. Paperwork always has a flaw.
Say nothing about money and carry boxes.

p2.text:
The bailiff arrives to a settled grimorie and hates it, quietly, {in a van|from the gate|with the engine running}, for some time.
Nobody inside the house says thank you more than once, because more than once would mean starting to cry, and there is {a kettle on instead|tea instead|a kettle going instead}.

t2.text:
The flaw is in the dates, where the flaws live. The debt is real; this WEEK'S seizure is not, and {leader} explains why in the doorway with the paper held at reading distance.
The bailiff, to his credit, checks, swears once with feeling, and leaves. Everyone understands this is a postponement. A postponement is {a currency|worth having|not nothing}.

t3.text:
The arithmetic holds all the way down. Whoever drew this up has been to the same school as the flaw and got there first.
The party stays for the loading anyway. There is a right way to {carry a box out of a house|empty a house|do this} and it involves not being alone {while it happens|for it|when it happens}.

c2.text:
{few} boxes, one van borrowed off a neighbour, one dog that rides in the front or nowhere.
At the end {stranger} shakes every hand twice and gives the party {payment}, and will not hear a word about it.

p_m.text:
Paying it is {four minutes|a signature and a count|the easiest thing anybody will do today}, and the bailiff is forty minutes out, and the sum is genuinely small.
{stranger} says no. Twice, and then a third time with a reason: the debt is not theirs, it is their {brother's|son's|late husband's}, and paying it is how the next one starts.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{So it is a tap, not a bill.|Pay once and it is a subscription.|That is not a debt, that is an arrangement.}"
asides.any: {member} {sits down on the step and waits this out|looks at the paperwork over a shoulder|says nothing and counts the boxes}

choices.text: Pay it anyway. Today is today.
Pay it into the court, not to the man.
Do not pay. Find the brother.

p_court.text:
Paid into court, the money stops being a favour and becomes a fact, with a number on it and a date, and the tap that was going to be opened cannot be.
The bailiff arrives to a receipt he cannot argue with. {stranger} understands what has been done about {an hour|two hours|a day} later and comes {a long way|four miles|across the district} to say so.

p_brother.text:
He is {two streets|a village|not far} away and is not hiding, exactly, and has {three|two} more of these running elsewhere under the same arrangement.
What is said to him is said quietly and lands. The debt is paid by the person who incurred it, in the doorway, in cash, {watched by four strangers|in front of witnesses|with everybody present}. The house stays packed for a week anyway, out of superstition.

p_cold.text:
Two streets of asking gets {four|five} versions of where he might be and none of them are where he is, and the forty minutes go by out on the road rather than on the step.
The party comes back to a van, a loaded van, a closed door and a neighbour who says the dog went in the front. There is nothing to be done that is not {embarrassing|worse|too late}.

c_m.text:
{few} boxes, one van borrowed off a neighbour, one dog that rides in the front or nowhere, and nobody mentioning money in either direction.
The last box out is the one nobody wants to lift, because it is books and photographs and it goes in last and comes out first {everywhere|in every house|every time}. {stranger} carries it themselves and gets to the van and has to put it down.

choices.text: Take the weight. Say nothing.
Sit on the wall with them until they can stand up.
Find out where the van is actually going.

c_wall.text:
It takes {eleven minutes|a quarter of an hour|as long as it takes} on a garden wall with a box between two people and nothing much being said.
What comes out of it is not about the house. It is about {a name|somebody|the person the photographs are of}, and it has not been said out loud to anybody in {two years|a long time|years}, and saying it is the whole of the afternoon's work.

c_where.text:
Nowhere, is the answer, phrased as a place: a cousin's yard {for now|until something turns up|for a fortnight}, with the boxes staying on the van because unloading them would make it real.
The party knows {four|three} people between here and there with a spare room, and by dark two of them have been asked and one of them has said yes.

n0.text:
A cart is in the ford at {place} to the axle, and {animal} that pulled it in has developed strong views about pulling it out.
{stranger} is up to the knees in it, holding the bridle, the load, and their temper, in descending order of success. {weather}, which is not helping.
The load on the cart is roped down badly on one side, and it is the {upstream|deep|wrong} side.

asides.calm: {member} rolls up both sleeves in a way that has ended arguments before.
asides.hedonistic: {member} points out, from the bank, that the water looks cold, which is confirmed from the water.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Get behind it and heave.
Take {animal}'s head and talk it round.
Walk on.

h2.text:
The cart comes out on the third heave with a sound like a boot leaving deep mud, scaled up.
{stranger} insists on payment with the stubbornness of somebody who has decided the story needs a proper ending: {payment}, and names to go with it, and the promise of a dry seat by the fire at the next farm along.

w3.text:
{animal} listens the way they listen: sideways, one ear, ready to disagree.
Then it leans into the collar like the whole argument never happened and walks the cart out at its own pace, and {stranger} looks at {leader} as if witchcraft has been performed, which is left uncorrected.

hx.text:
The cart comes out. One boot does not, for a while, and the water gets its full say in the matter before everything is back on dry ground.
The thanks are real and so is {the cold|the cold, for hours afterwards}.

e4.text:
The view back from the next rise: the cart still in the ford, {smaller now|further off|no smaller than it looked}, and the sound of the argument continuing without any need of the party's opinion.
Some afternoons belong to {other people|somebody else|other people entirely}.

h_m.text:
Getting behind it puts everybody in the water to the thigh and the water has {opinions|a temperature|a great deal to say}.
On the second heave the bad ropes give and the load shifts, and what is under the tarpaulin is not farm goods. It is {crates|boxes|cases}, stencilled, with a customs mark that has been painted over once.

asides.cynical: {member}, in the water: "{And there it is.|A cart stuck in a ford at this hour. Of course.|Nobody carts turnips at this hour.}"
asides.any: {member} {gets the tarpaulin back over it without being asked|looks at the stencil and then at {stranger}|says nothing, and heaves}

choices.text: Cover it back up and get the cart out.
Read the stencil properly.
Let go of the cart and step back.

h_stencil.text:
It is a hospital mark. The crates are {drugs|medicine|dressings and ampoules}, the shipment was written off as lost {three weeks|a month|some time} ago, and {stranger} is not a smuggler, {stranger} is the one taking them the long way round because the short way has a checkpoint on it.
The cart comes out on the fourth heave with everybody pushing including the party's opinion of the afternoon.

h_step.text:
Stepping back in a ford is a loud decision even when nobody says anything, and {stranger} watches it happen from the bridle end with water to the knee.
The cart comes out an hour later with two other people's help. The party is a long way up the road by then, dry from the thigh down, and slightly worse company than they were at noon.

e_m.text:
The view back from the next rise: the cart still in the ford, {smaller now|further off|no smaller than it looked}, and the argument continuing without any need of the party's opinion.
Then the water comes up. Not much and not fast: {a hand's width|four inches|enough to notice} in the time it takes to watch, which means there is weather somewhere upstream that nobody at the ford can see.

choices.text: Walk on. Not our river.
Go back and say so.
Read the water and work out how long they have.

e_warn.text:
Shouting it from the bank is enough. {stranger} takes one look upstream, cuts the load free with a knife rather than untie it, and has {animal} out of the shafts inside {two minutes|ninety seconds|no time at all}.
The cart goes. The load goes. Everything with a heartbeat in it is standing on the bank when the water comes through, which is the only arithmetic that matters and which {stranger} will not stop saying.

e_flood.text:
Read properly, there is {eleven minutes|a quarter of an hour|about ten minutes} in it, which is enough for the beast, the load and the cart, in that order, if nobody stands about.
Nobody stands about. Everything is on the bank with {two minutes|ninety seconds|a minute} to spare and the ford is impassable for two days afterwards, and the story of it is worth a free bed at either end of this road for a year.

n0.text:
Snares on posted ground at {place}: {few} of them, set {this morning|recently|badly, which is a cruelty of its own}, and one of them holding something still alive.
The land belongs to {stranger}, by {sign} on the gate. Whoever set the wire will be back before dark.
One snare is set differently from the others: {tighter|higher|with a knot the rest do not have}, by somebody else's hands.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.aggressive: {member} has picked out a waiting spot with a view of the gate and is standing in it.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Spring the snares and free what is in them.
Wait for the one who set them.
Take the catch and the wire both.

s2.text:
The wire comes off {few} pegs without a single one snapping back, and the live one is gone into the hedge before the coat is back on.
Good wire, this. It goes in the pack, on the reasoning that it has resigned from its {previous employment|last job|former line of work}.

sx.text:
The {last|third} snare has a temper. The wire whips, and takes its fee out of the back of a hand on its way past.
The animal gets away clean, which everybody involved, including the hand, rules {a fair trade|a fair exchange|about right}.

fight.text: Whoever comes over the stile at dusk comes armed for {wire and rabbits|rabbits|an empty field} and finds the afternoon has other plans.

theft.text:
The catch, the wire, and the pegs, all of it, gone inside {ten|fifteen} minutes.
Somewhere behind, a poacher is going to stand in an empty field working out that somebody has poached the poaching, and there is a small ugly satisfaction in that which does not entirely survive {the walk|the walk back|the first mile of it}.

fight_m.text:
Waiting takes the last {hour|two hours|of the light} behind the hedge with the wire in view and the live one in the snare going quiet in a way that is hard to sit through.
Whoever comes over the stile at dusk is {small|not large|nowhere near the size of the problem}, comes armed for rabbits, and stops dead at the sight of four strangers in a posted field.

choices.text: Take them. They are poaching.
Talk first. Find out who set the odd snare.
Let them go and say nothing to anybody.

fight_talk.text:
Four of the snares are theirs and they say so without much prompting, because they are {twelve|fourteen|not old} and hungry and out of arguments.
The fifth is not theirs. The fifth belongs to somebody who has been using this field for {a season|months|longer than that} and who does not set wire for rabbits, and the description of them is worth more than the catch and the wire together.

fight_let.text:
They are over the stile and gone in {four seconds|no time|the time it takes to decide not to move}, leaving the wire, the catch and the field.
The live one goes into the hedge. The wire goes in the pack. Nobody on either side of the hedge mentions the afternoon again, and {two months|a season|some weeks} later a bag of something edible is left on the party's step by somebody who does not knock.

theft_m.text:
The catch, the wire and the pegs go in the packs inside {ten|fifteen} minutes, which is the easy part.
The odd snare is the hard part. It is set with a knot nobody in the party can tie, it is set for something {larger|a great deal larger|the wrong size for this field}, and it is set across a run that comes out of the wood rather than out of the hedge.

choices.text: Take that one too and go.
Leave it exactly as found and get off the land.
Set ourselves up on the run and see what it is for.

theft_leave.text:
The wire the party took is the party's. The wire the party did not take stays set, across a run, exactly as found, with the knot undisturbed.
A fortnight later, at a fire {two valleys|a district|a long way} from here, somebody describes that knot and the whole table goes quiet, and the party discovers what they walked away from without ever having to see it.

theft_wait.text:
Three hours on the run with the light going and the wood behind, and what comes down it at {full dark|the end of the light|the worst possible hour} is walking on two legs and is not a poacher.
It is in the snare for four seconds, which is three seconds longer than it expects and one second less than the party needs, and then the field is a different kind of place entirely.

qe_stall.title: {Short A Roof|Open To The Sky|The Missing Course}

n0.text:
A roof at {place} stands open to the sky with {stranger} on top of it, and the yard below says the job stopped mid-course: trestles out, ladder up, nothing moving.
The job is short {qty} {material}. The supplier is {distance}, and between here and there is {misfortune}, and the sky is not going to wait on any of it.
The trestles are set up for {two people|a pair|somebody and a mate}, and there is only one person on the roof.

asides.disciplined: {member} {follows standard breach protocol by the book|clears every corner with military precision|keeps a steady firing stance and monitors the sensors|checks the ammo count and maintains position}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Hand over the {material}.
Go up and make what is there stretch.
Take the supplier's name and move on.

g2.text:
The course goes on before the light goes, and the roof is a roof by dark.
{stranger} pays over the odds and will not be argued down: {payment}, counted into {leader}'s hand on the tailgate, and the first rain that night lands on finished work.

hh.text:
An afternoon of passing, holding, and not looking down, and what is there stretches further than the arithmetic said it could.
The gap that is left is small enough to tarpaulin with dignity. Payment in {payment}, and a standing welcome under the roof the party {helped close|closed|got a course onto}.

hf.text:
A batten gives, and for one long second the yard is a good deal closer than planned.
Caught, mostly, by the trestle and partly by {stranger}, at the cost of a bruise shaped like carpentry. The tarpaulin goes on in silence.

e5.text:
The supplier's name goes in {the diary|the book|the back of the diary} under things that can be fixed by somebody with a full pack and a free morning.
Behind, on the roof, the hammering starts again anyway, slower, {weather}.

g2_m.text:
The {material} goes up the ladder in two loads and the course goes on before the light goes, and about halfway along {stranger} stops and sits back on their heels.
Under the old course the deck is {soft|gone|holding on out of habit} for about a metre and a half, and it has been that way a good deal longer than this job has been running.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{So we are roofing a hole.|Lovely. New tiles on wet cake.|That is not a roof, that is an opinion.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts a knife into the deck and it goes in too easily|holds the ladder and looks up|whistles once}

choices.text: Cover it. It is their roof and their money.
Cut the bad deck out and splice new in.
Come down. Tell them what it will cost done properly.

g2_deck.text:
A metre and a half of deck out, new in, scarfed at both ends, and {two hours|the rest of the light|longer than anybody wanted} gone on a job nobody was being paid for.
The roof is a roof by dark and will be one in ten years. {stranger} pays the agreed price and then comes {four miles|across the district|a long way} the following week with the difference and an apology for not having it on the day.

g2_through.text:
The bad metre and a half turns out to be {three|four} metres and the saw finds all of it at once, from above, standing on it.
Nobody goes through to the yard, which is the only reason this counts as a near miss rather than a story. The roof is open wider than it was at noon, the tarpaulin goes on, and everybody comes down the ladder in a specific silence.

g2_quote.text:
It is not a conversation anybody wants at the bottom of a ladder in {weather}, and it takes {ten minutes|a quarter of an hour|two goes} because the first version is too gentle to be useful.
The number is bad. {stranger} takes it standing up, thanks the party for saying it before the tiles went on rather than after, and goes to sell {the trailer|a field|something they were keeping}.

e5_m.text:
The supplier's name goes in {the diary|the book|the back of the diary} under things that can be fixed by somebody with a full pack and a free morning.
The morning is free. The supplier is {distance} and shut, and the yard behind the shutter has exactly what the roof needs stacked against the wall where anybody can see it.

choices.text: Walk on. It is shut and it is not ours.
Find whoever holds the key.
Take what the roof needs and leave the money on the stack.

e5_key.text:
The key is with a {daughter|nephew|neighbour} four doors down who has been waiting three days for somebody to ask, because the supplier is in hospital and nobody thought to say so.
The yard opens. The roof gets its course. The supplier gets paid, properly, by post, and hears about the whole business from {three|four} directions before the week is out.

e5_take.text:
Over the wall, off the stack, exact money left under a brick where it will be found and not blown away.
The roof is finished by dark. Whether the money is found before the brick is, is a matter nobody in the party finds out, and it stays in the back of {member}'s head for {a fortnight|some weeks|longer than it should}.

qe_bet.title: {The Fair|The Stall That Does The Arithmetic|Small Stake, Big Pot}

n0.text:
A fair at {place}: {many} stalls, one band, and one stall taking money on {a strength machine|a ring toss that is not as easy as it looks|a card the whole crowd is sure it can follow}.
{stranger} runs it with the face of somebody who has done the arithmetic and sleeps well on it. The stake is small. The pot is not.
There is a second man at the back of the stall doing nothing at all, {well dressed|hands in pockets|watching the crowd rather than the game}.

asides.hedonistic: {member} has already lost twice and is having a wonderful time.
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Put the stake down and play.
Read the trick before spending a coin.
Just enjoy the fair.

wb.text:
The pot pays out to a stall-holder's round of applause, which is how a professional buries a bad quarter of an hour.
The crowd carries {leader} to {bar} on the strength of it and the story is already growing on the way.

lb.text:
The arithmetic was theirs all along, the way it always was.
The stake is gone, the crowd is kind about it, and the {drink} afterwards tastes of being one more person the stall has put through the same {short education|brief education|short lesson}.

rb.text:
The trick is {in the thumb|in the felt|in the count}, and once seen it cannot be unseen.
One play, placed properly, and a quiet exit at the pace of somebody who knows exactly how long a stall-holder takes to {work out what just happened|catch up|do that arithmetic}.

lb2.text:
After {forty minutes|an hour|half an evening} of watching, the only firm discovery is that the stall has been watching back, with professional interest, since minute five.
No coin has changed hands. Both sides understand it is a draw, and there is a strange courtesy in {the nod exchanged at parting|the nod at the end of it|how the nod is given}.

v2.text: The band is {loud|too loud|loud and not good}, {food} is exactly what it should be and no better, and for one whole evening the party's line of work does not come up once.

rb_m.text:
The trick is {in the thumb|in the felt|in the count}, and once seen it cannot be unseen, and the whole stall unfolds into arithmetic in about {four seconds|a moment|the space of one play}.
The man at the back has seen the party see it. He does not move. He {smiles|nods|raises his chin} very slightly, which is either an invitation or a warning and is almost certainly both.

choices.text: One play, placed properly, then leave quickly.
Go and talk to the man at the back.
Tell the crowd how it works.

rb_back.text:
He is not the muscle and he is not the owner. He is the man who buys good hands drinks at the end of a fair, and he has been standing there since noon watching {four hundred|a great many|the whole county's worth of} people not see it.
The conversation lasts an hour and costs the party nothing and ends with an address, a name to use at it, and work for anybody with eyes, whenever they want it.

rb_out.text:
He listens to the whole approach with the patience of somebody who has heard it in {nine counties|a dozen towns|every county between here and the coast}, and then explains, kindly, that the stall is his, that the trick is his, and that the party has about as long as it takes to finish a drink.
The drink is finished. Nobody is touched. The fair is a great deal less fun from that point on.

rb_crowd.text:
Explaining a trick to a crowd that has been losing at it all afternoon works exactly as well as it deserves to, which is to say {instantly and then very badly|beautifully for ninety seconds|too well}.
The stall goes over. Somebody's coat gets torn and it is not the stall-holder's. The party leaves the fair by the far gate at a good pace with {a share of the float|the pot|a handful of somebody's money} and a description of them going round the field.

v2_m.text:
The band is {loud|too loud|loud and not good}, {food} is exactly what it should be and no better, and for one whole evening the party's line of work does not come up once.
At about {ten|eleven|the hour the band stops} somebody starts shouting near the gate, and it is the sort of shouting that has {a name|a person|somebody's child} in the middle of it.

choices.text: Stay at the fire. Not tonight.
Go and help look.
Get the gates shut before anybody leaves the field.

v2_found.text:
Under the flap of the beer tent, asleep, {four metres|a few feet|no distance at all} from where everybody had already looked twice.
The shouting stops. The band starts again. The party drinks free for the rest of the night at three separate stalls and has to be talked out of the field at {two|one|some hour} in the morning.

v2_gate.text:
Getting a fair's worth of people to stay put takes one voice, one lie about the police, and about {ninety seconds|two minutes|less time than it should}.
The child is found inside the field, which is what everybody wanted, and it is found by their own mother, which is better. Nobody afterwards is entirely sure whose idea the gates were, which is how the party prefers it.

v2_long.text:
It goes on for {two hours|most of the night|a very long time}, with lamps, and a field, and everybody calling the same name in the same four directions.
They turn up at dawn {two fields over|by the river|asleep in a van}, cold and fine, and the relief goes through the whole fair like weather. The party sleeps badly and is not sorry.

qe_pilgrim.title: {The Pilgrim|Short Of The Shrine|A Vow With A Deadline}

n0.text:
{stranger} is sitting against {sign} at {place}, sweating, {weather}, a good way short of where a vow says they must stand by dark.
Something's wrong in the chest and they will not name it, on the reasoning, common among the devout and the frightened, that naming a thing invites it in.
There is a second set of prints on the verge, {stopping where they are sitting|coming back the other way|walking off the road and not returning}.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Give what medicine the pack holds.
Treat it in the field, bare-handed.
Carry them the rest of the way.

gm.text:
The herbs do what herbs do, slowly, and the colour comes back in the wrong order but it comes back.
The pilgrim pays in the only coin the order deals in: a prayer that works, taught word-perfect on the walk that is left, with strict instructions about {when never to use it|the one hour it must never be used|who it must never be used on}.

wt.text:
Breathing settles under {leader}'s hands the old way: posture, pressure, and a voice kept deliberately boring.
The last stretch is walked slow, together, and at the shrine the pilgrim stands there before dark, and does not look back, and does not need to.

wf.text:
Whatever is wrong in that chest is above field repair and everybody kneeling on the verge knows it.
What can be done is done: shade, water, and company, which is not nothing. The vow is missed. The pilgrim says the deadline mattered less than the walking, and almost sounds {convinced|as if they mean it|like somebody who believes it}.

ct.text:
{distance}, most of it uphill, all of it in the open, {weather}, in relays.
The shrine appears around the last bend with ten minutes of the light left, and the pilgrim arrives carried, which their order, consulted afterwards, rules is arriving all the same.

cf.text:
Four kilometres of it, and then the party's legs file a formal objection on a wet slope.
Everybody sits on the wet slope for a while, wrecked together, and the pilgrim laughs for the first time all day, which is worth something even if nothing else was {reached|arrived at|got to}.

gm_m.text:
What is in the pack is {herbs|what a pack holds|two or three useful things} and none of it is for a chest, and everybody kneeling on the verge knows it.
The pilgrim will take the herbs. The pilgrim will not take the offer of a hospital, a vehicle, or a delay, and says so in the tone of somebody quoting a rule at themselves rather than at the party.

asides.nurturing: {member} has a wrist between two fingers and is counting before anybody has finished arguing.
asides.any: {member} {gets the pack open|shades them with a coat|sits down on the verge to be at eye level}

choices.text: Give the herbs. Respect the vow.
Work out what is actually wrong first.
Argue the rule with them on its own terms.

gm_diag.text:
It is not the chest. It is {the gut|dehydration and the gut|three days of bad water}, presenting high, the way it does, and it is entirely fixable on a verge by anybody who knows to look.
An hour of water taken in sips and the pilgrim is walking, badly, and then walking. They stand at the shrine with {twenty minutes|the light|time} to spare and the vow whole.

gm_rule.text:
The rule says unaided. It does not say alone, and it does not say untreated, and there is {four hundred years|a great deal|two centuries} of argument on the subject that the pilgrim has clearly never been shown.
Being given permission by a stranger who can cite it is not something they were ready for. They take the help. They arrive. Afterwards they write to their order about it, at length, and the letter does the rounds.

ct_m.text:
{distance}, most of it uphill, all of it in the open, {weather}, in relays, with somebody on your back who weighs more at every kilometre.
At the halfway stone there is a choice of road: the pilgrim road, which is longer and marked and correct, and a track over the shoulder of the hill that is {shorter|an hour shorter|steeper and shorter} and is not the pilgrim road.

choices.text: The pilgrim road. It is the whole point.
Over the shoulder. Arriving matters more.
Put them down and go and fetch a cart.

ct_short.text:
The shoulder is {forty minutes|half an hour|an hour} of ground nobody should carry anybody over, and it is done in relays with one person always braced below.
The shrine comes up from the wrong side with {half an hour|a good half hour|more time than anybody hoped} in hand. The pilgrim stands. Then sits. Then stands again for the whole of it, which takes until dark.

ct_cart.text:
The nearest cart is {two kilometres|a mile and a half|the wrong way} back and belongs to somebody who takes {ten minutes|a while|some persuading} to be persuaded.
It gets there. The pilgrim arrives on wheels rather than on feet or on a back, and their order, consulted afterwards, is divided about this in a way that will keep {two|three} scholars busy for a season.

qe_lockup.title: {Lot 41|The Lockup Nobody Claimed|Keys That Do Not Fit}

n0.text:
A lockup at {place}, sold at auction {timeAgo} to a bidder who never came for it.
{stranger} has a ring of keys that do not fit, a paper that says the contents are theirs if the door is open by dark, and an offer: the party opens it, the party gets a share of whatever is shelved inside.
The dust at the foot of the door has been disturbed {recently|in the last day or two|by somebody who was careful about the rest of it}.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.impulsive: {member} has tried three keys already, on the grounds that somebody had to.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Pick it.
Force the door.
Read the auction paper properly first.

pl.text:
The lock is old and proud and gives up its dignity one pin at a time.
Inside: shelves, packed by somebody methodical, and the party's share of it fills the packs to the straps. {stranger} keeps the paper and the story, and considers it {a bargain|a good trade|well bought}.

fl.text:
The door loses{, eventually| in the end| on the fourth go}, but takes its toll on the way down: half of what was shelved behind it does not survive the argument.
The half that does is still a good afternoon's work by {weight|weight alone|any measure}.

pf.text:
The door wins the first two rounds and part of the third, and by dark it is still shut and the paper is so much kindling.
{stranger} is decent about it, which stings worse than the knuckles.

ip.text:
The paper is genuine, and better than genuine: down in the schedule, in the small type, is an inventory the seller never read.
{leader} names a fairer split before a single key turns, with the inventory as the argument, and it is agreed to at speed. The door, tried once more with feeling, opens after all on {the plainest key on the ring|a key nobody had bet on|the one key that looked wrong for it}.

e6.text:
The small type defeats {the light|the eyes|everybody in turn} and the light is going.
Some doors keep their afternoons. The keys go back in a pocket, the paper back in its envelope, and the lockup keeps its shapes, plural, for {another owner|the next owner|somebody else entirely}.

pl_m.text:
The lock is old and proud and gives up its dignity one pin at a time, and on the third pin it becomes obvious that somebody has been in here {this week|recently|before the party and after the auction}: the pins are bright where they should be black.
The door opens on shelves, packed by somebody methodical, with {one gap|a gap in the middle shelf|a rectangle of clean floor} where something the size of a trunk used to be.

choices.text: Fill the packs and go. Plenty left.
Work out what stood in the gap.
Shut it, relock it, and watch the lockup until dark.

pl_gap.text:
The shelves either side of the gap are an inventory in themselves: everything on them is {the same trade|from one profession|part of one kit}, and what is missing is the part of that kit worth killing for.
{stranger} goes very quiet when told, and then names the bidder who never came, and then says that man has been dead {two years|since the spring|a while}.

pl_watch.text:
Four hours across the road in a doorway with the light going and {stranger} losing patience in {ten-minute|regular|increasingly loud} instalments.
At dusk somebody comes with a key that works. What follows is a conversation rather than a fight, conducted at a distance of {four metres|some yards|the width of the road}, and at the end of it the party has half of what is inside and the whole of a name.

fl_m.text:
Forcing it means a bar, a shoulder, and somebody counting, and the door loses{, eventually| in the end| on the fourth go}.
Halfway through the third go the noise brings somebody out of the yard opposite: {an old man|a woman with a dog|somebody in a dressing gown} who watches the whole performance with their arms folded and does not go back inside.

choices.text: Finish it. Let them watch.
Stop, and go and explain ourselves.
Stop, and ask them what they know about the lockup.

fl_cover.text:
The paper is genuine and the story is told with the paper held up, which is {ninety per cent|most|nearly all} of how anything is believed.
They go back inside. The door comes down on the fourth go. Half of what was shelved does not survive it and the half that does is a good afternoon's work by weight.

fl_cops.text:
The story is a little too smooth and the paper is a little too far away to read, and the dressing gown goes back inside and picks up a telephone.
What is in the lockup is in the packs by the time anybody arrives, which is {the good news|the only good news|something}. The rest of the evening involves a great deal of standing in a yard being asked the same four questions.

fl_ask.text:
They know everything. People in dressing gowns opposite lockups always do: who bid, who never came, who has been round {twice|three times|since the spring} with a torch at night, and what colour van they drive.
The door still has to come down and it still costs half the contents. The information costs nothing and is worth considerably more than the half that broke.

q_leyline.title: {The Broken Line|Where The Magic Stopped|Dry Ground}

n0.text:
