Nothing casts at {place}. Not badly: at all. {member} tries the smallest cantrip anybody knows and {ground} takes it like a stone taking rain.
Somebody broke the line here, and did it on purpose, from the look of the burn pattern. {asker} is camped a hundred metres off the dead spot with {instrument} and a face that says this is week three.
The burn pattern has a second burn inside it, older, {the same shape but smaller|identical and half the size|from the last time somebody did this}.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.disciplined: {member} {follows standard breach protocol by the book|clears every corner with military precision|keeps a steady firing stance and monitors the sensors|checks the ammo count and maintains position}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Splice the line with {qty} {material}.
Read the burn and work out who broke it.
Whatever wanted this ground dry is still here. Find it.

sp.text:
The splice is ugly work with the party's own stock and it holds on the second attempt.
The line comes back the way a tap comes back: air first, then everything at once. Every hair on the away team stands up, and for one second {leader} can feel where every other line on this {rock|world|whole rock} runs.

rd.text:
The break was cut from underneath and cut clean, which takes a contract and a specialist, not an accident.
{asker} looks at the diagram for a long time and then names a price for the party never having drawn it: {payment}, and the diagram goes in the fire.

rf.text:
The burn reads as an accident right up until the party is a day gone and {member} sits up in the dark having worked out what was wrong with the third measurement.
By then it is somebody else's {dead ground|problem|dead ground entirely}.

oil.text:
Down under {remnant}, in a cut nobody made with tools, something is sitting in its own weight and waiting for the line to come back.
Without the leyline it cannot regenerate. That is the entire reason the line was cut, and whoever cut it never came back to {finish the job|finish it|do the second half}.

amb.text: {It finds the party first|It is already moving when they turn|It comes up out of the cut first}, which on dry ground means finding them without {a single spell|one spell|anything at all} between them and it.

sp_m.text:
The splice is ugly work with the party's own stock, and halfway through it {asker} says, conversationally, that the last people to splice this line did it {eleven months ago|last season|the winter before} and were never seen leaving.
The line is a hand's width from being joined. It would take {a minute|thirty seconds|one more turn} to finish, and about the same to undo.

choices.text: Finish the splice.
Finish it, but earth it first so whatever drinks first is not us.
Stop. Go and find what is downstream of this before joining it.

sp_earth.text:
An earth strap into wet {ground}, a spike, and the whole first surge goes into the planet instead of into the four people standing over the joint.
The line comes back in its own time and comes back tame. {asker} looks at the strap, and then at the party, and revises something about them upward without saying what.

sp_shock.text:
The strap goes in the wrong side of the joint and the first surge takes the shortest road, which is through the joint, the tools, and {whoever is holding them|whichever hands are on them|the nearest pair of hands}.
The line is fixed. Everything up to the elbow is numb until {the following afternoon|the next day|well into the next day} and hums, faintly, whenever anything nearby is cast.

q_grimoire.title: {The Book That Is Eating Itself|Bad CamelCase|Burn It Or Do Not}

n0.text:
A book at {place}, out of the weather under {remnant}, open, with something wrong on the left-hand page.
One formula in it has the words apart. It has been copying itself into its neighbours for a while now, and the neighbours have started agreeing with it. {sound}, and the pages are warm.
On the right-hand page, in the margin, somebody has written the same word {eleven|nine|fourteen} times, getting smaller, in a hand that starts as one hand and ends as another.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Burn it. That is the procedure.
Cut out the clean pages first.
Copy the infected formula down properly before it goes.

burn.text:
It goes up fast and it argues on the way, which books do not usually do.
What is left is a clean patch of {ground} and the flat certainty of having done the correct thing, which is worth {less on the walk home than it should be|surprisingly little on the walk home|almost nothing by the time the ship is in sight}.

cut.text:
{few} pages come out clean with the knife, taken from the outside in, ahead of the spread.
The rest burns. What is saved is worth carrying: workings from before whoever wrote this got careless, in a hand that never once {separated a word|let a word come apart|got one wrong}.

cop.text:
Writing it out correctly is the hardest {hour|two hours} anybody has spent sitting down. The formula does not want to be joined up and says so in the wrist.
Joined up, it is a real thing, and a considerable one. The book goes on the fire immediately afterwards and nobody {argues|says a word|objects}.

spread.text:
It gets into the party's own notes before anybody notices the handwriting changing.
Everything written down in the last {few} days has to be burned in a heap on {ground}, and it takes a piece out of everyone to do it.

burn_m.text:
It goes on the fire and it argues, which books do not usually do: the pages turn against the draught, and the formula with the words apart is on top of the pile every time the pile shifts.
It is going to take {a while|longer than a book should|three armfuls of wood}. Long enough to change one's mind in.

choices.text: Stand there until it is ash. That is the procedure.
Take one page off the top first. Just the one.
Say the words over it while it burns. Properly.

burn_page.text:
One page, folded twice, into the inside pocket, while the rest of it goes up.
It is a good page. It is worth money and it is worth reading and it is, for {eleven days|a fortnight|nine days}, perfectly ordinary, and after that {member} starts noticing that it is never quite where it was left.

burn_rite.text:
The words are said in the right order over a fire that does not want to hear them, and the fire goes from arguing to ordinary between one syllable and the next.
What is left is ash and a clean patch of {ground} and the particular satisfaction of a procedure done correctly and completely. The Guild hears about it from somebody who was not there.

burn_loud.text:
The words are said in nearly the right order, which is worse than not saying them, and the fire takes the mistake and holds it for a long moment before letting it go.
The book burns. Everybody's ears ring until {the next morning|dark|well past dark}, and for a week afterwards nothing anybody in the party writes down comes out quite in their own hand.

q_kessler.title: {Above The Cage|The Armoured Rocket|What Came Down Instead}

n0.text:
Something came down at {place} that was built to be destroyed on the way up: layered plate, sacrificial, a hull that is nine tenths armour and one tenth room.
One of the armoured launches, then, and this one did not dock. {instrument} says there is still power in it. {wrongness}.
The hull number has been painted over, {once, badly, from a ladder|in a hurry|by somebody standing on something unsteady}, and painted over on the inside as well.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Cut in.
Power the beacon up with {qty} {material} and let somebody else come for it.
Strip the plate and go.

inn.text:
Inside: {three couches, two of them used|four couches, three of them used|three couches and two sets of boots}, and a log kept by hand right up until it was not.
They got through the debris. They got through it and the docking never happened and they came down here instead, and somebody wrote all of it down for whoever {opened the door|got here|came}.

cx.text:
Sacrificial plate is sacrificial in every direction. The layer that gives gives all at once, and takes {the back of a hand|a length of forearm|two fingers' worth of glove} with it on the way past.
The door stays shut. Whatever is behind it {stays behind it|stays there|is left there}.

bea.text:
The beacon takes the {material} and lights, and starts saying the same four words to an orbit nobody can currently cross.
Somebody will hear it eventually. The party's registry is in the header, and that is a name in a file at a space centre, which is a thing that pays out later and pays out {well|very well|better than the job did}.

str.text:
The plate comes off in {sheets|slabs|long curved pieces} and it is good plate: rated for the grinder, which means rated for anything the party is likely to walk into.
The couches stay where they are. Nobody says anything about the two that are used, and nobody {has to|needs to|does}.

inn_m.text:
The cut goes through and the air that comes out is old and dry and has been at the same pressure for longer than the party has been alive.
Inside: {three couches, two of them used|four couches, three of them used|three couches and two sets of boots}, a hand-kept log, and a locker aft that has been welded shut from the outside by somebody who was aboard at the time.

choices.text: Read the log and take what is loose.
Open the aft locker.
Take the couches' names off the boots and leave the rest.

inn_locker.text:
The weld comes out in a clean line and the locker holds what the log stops being coherent about: a sealed case, a second log kept in a different hand, and {an empty couch harness cut through at the shoulder|a harness cut open from the wrong side|one set of straps cut, not unbuckled}.
What is in the case is the reason the launch never docked, and it is worth carrying and it is not pleasant to carry.

inn_cut.text:
The weld does not come out in a clean line. It comes out in {a spray|several directions at once|two pieces and a lot of heat}, and the locker door with it, and the case inside takes the edge of the door across its seal.
Whatever was in it is air now. The party stands in it for the {four|five} seconds it takes to get the helmets sealed, and those seconds are going to be discussed for some time.

inn_names.text:
The names are inked inside the boot tongues, the way crews do it, and they come away in a photograph and a notebook page and nothing else is touched.
The launch is left sealed. The names go into a file at a space centre {eleven days|a fortnight|some weeks} later and three families find out what happened, which is worth nothing at all and is the reason anybody goes out there.

str_m.text:
The plate comes off in {sheets|slabs|long curved pieces} and it is good plate, rated for the grinder, worth the walk on its own.
Under the fourth sheet the hull stops being hull. There is a second skin under it that is not sacrificial, not rated for anything, and not on any drawing of this class: thin, seamless, and warm to the glove.

choices.text: Take the plate. Leave the skin alone.
Take a sample of the second skin.
Put the plate back over it and walk away.

str_skin.text:
The sample comes off the way a scale comes off a fish, and under it there is another one, and the drill says there are {nine|eleven|a good many} more.
What comes back to the ship in a jar will pay for the season. What it is remains an open question at every institution it is subsequently shown to.

str_burn.text:
The skin does not want to be sampled and expresses this at the temperature it chooses, which is {high|considerable|a great deal higher than the day}, and the glove is the only reason it is fingers and not a hand.
The plate still comes away. {The jar is empty.|The jar comes back empty.|Nothing goes in the jar.} The burn is dressed at the ship and talked about less than it deserves.

str_back.text:
The sheet goes back over it and is tacked down, badly, on purpose, so the next person to come out here can tell at a glance that somebody already had a look and decided against.
The couches stay where they are. The party leaves with nothing and the distinct sense of having made {the correct call|a call they will keep making|the only call}.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.loyal: {member} {positions themselves between {leader} and the door|nods firmly: "Right behind you, boss."|keeps a watchful eye on {leader}'s blind spot|stands ready to back up whatever call is made}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Finish the unload and leave the manifest signed.
Take a share and go.
Wait for whoever is coming back.

fin.text:
It is {four|five|three} hours of honest work and the ramp is clear by the end of it, everything squared, the clip signed with the party's own registry.
The crew, when they come back, come back at a run, and the arithmetic of what they were expecting to find against what is actually standing there does something to their faces. The Society pays its debts {the same day|before dark|inside the week}.

hurt.text:
A drum that had to stay upright does not, and the corner of it finds {a shin|an ankle|the outside of a knee} on the way over.
The rest gets unloaded slower and worse. It is still unloaded, and the clip {still gets signed|gets signed|is signed at the end of it}.

take.text:
What comes away fits in the packs and is worth having, and the manifest never had a fourth page to disagree with.
Somewhere {ahead|down the route|at the far end of this} there is a hauler who is going to stand at the bottom of a ramp doing arithmetic. The Society keeps a very long memory and {a very dense network|a network to match|no gaps anywhere in its network}.

wait.text:
Two hours on the ramp with {sound} for company, and then they come over the rise carrying the fourth page and a story about why.
Nobody is robbed, everybody eats, and the party leaves with a name to use at any fire on this route and the number of an old handset that {always answers|answers at any hour|has never once not answered}.

take_m.text:
The packs are open on the ramp and the arithmetic is easy: {cargo} in units small enough to carry, nothing sealed, nothing counted past page three.
Under the top layer of the third pallet there is a second manifest, in a different hand, listing the same load at {half|a third of|two thirds of} the weight. Somebody on this run was already stealing from it.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{So we would be robbing a thief.|The good news is we are not the first.|Everybody on this road has their hand in the same box.}"
asides.any: {member} {reads the second sheet twice and puts it back exactly as it was|looks up the road, then down it|does not touch anything yet}

choices.text: Take a share and go. Nobody will be counting.
Take the second manifest instead of the cargo.
Put it all back and wait on the ramp.

take_paper.text:
The two sheets side by side are a confession with a signature block at the bottom of it, and it takes {ten minutes|a quarter of an hour|less time than expected} to work out which of the run's four names it belongs to.
The Society pays for that sheet the way people pay for things they have been trying to prove for {two years|a long time|three seasons}, and the cargo goes on to where it was always going.

take_slow.text:
The numbers will not sit still. They are close enough to right to be maddening and wrong enough to mean something, and by the time the party gives up on them the light has gone and the crew are coming over the rise.
They find their load whole, their manifest handled, and four strangers standing over both. It takes {an hour|most of the evening|a long cold hour} to talk out of, and it is talked out of, barely.

wait_m.text:
Two hours on the ramp with {sound} for company. The light goes orange, then goes.
What comes over the rise first is not the crew. It is {one of them|a single figure|one man}, on foot, alone, moving badly, carrying the fourth page folded small in a fist that has been closed on it for a while.

choices.text: Get him sat down and get it out of him.
Look at him properly before he says anything.
Back off the ramp and let him come to us.

wait_med.text:
He is three hours into something that will kill him in five, and he does not know it, and the fourth page is in his fist because the fourth page is what he decided to carry instead of water.
The party has {both|the water and the hands|what he needed}. He lives. The rest of the crew arrive at dawn to find their load squared and one of their own asleep and breathing, and after that there is no fire on this route that the party pays at.

wait_back.text:
He comes up the ramp at his own speed and gets {halfway|most of the way|as far as the drums} and stops, and hands over the page, and sits down where he is standing.
The story comes out sideways over the next hour: what was on the fourth page, what came out of the scrub for it, and why the manifest stops mid-word. {Everybody eats. Nobody sleeps much.|Everybody eats. Nobody sleeps.|There is food, and very little sleep.}

q_verden.title: {The Planted Limb|What Grows Back|Two Of Them Now}

n0.text:
There is a garden at {place}, laid out in rows on ground that grows nothing, and a blue-skinned figure working it who greets the party in flawless MarkovSpeak and keeps working.
One of the rows is an arm. It is planted at the wrist, it is not dead, and it is further along than it was {last week|a week ago|when the rows were last counted}.
The rows are planted in the order somebody would plant them if they expected to be here for {two hundred years|a very long time|longer than anybody is}.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Give {qty} {material} for the beds.
Work the rows for a day.
Ask what they threw into a star, and why.

gv.text:
The beds take it and the gardener's hands go straight to work with it, no thanks offered, because thanks are for strangers.
What comes back at the end of the row is a cutting of something that should not root in {ground} and does, and instructions for it that take an hour and are given twice {to be sure|over|to make certain}.

wk.text:
A day in the rows: heavy, repetitive, done properly, in company that talks the whole time and says something worth keeping about {one hour in six|twice an afternoon|more often than that}.
By dark the party has been fed twice and given a name that works in any Verden household on {any world|any world at all|whichever world they are on}.

wf.text:
The rows win. Nobody warned the party that a Verden day is measured against a Verden back.
The gardener finds this funnier than anybody has found anything in weeks and packs the party off with food and a genuinely sympathetic pat that nearly puts {leader} in {the bed|the row|the soil}.

ask.text:
The answer takes the walk to the end of the row and back and is not a lament.
They put the whole of it into the sun on purpose, all of it, and there is nothing in the telling that regrets it, and by the end {leader} is no longer certain the party's own pockets represent the winning side of {the argument|it|that particular argument}.

ask_m.text:
The answer takes the walk to the end of the row and back, and it is not a lament: they put the whole of it into the sun on purpose, all of it, and there is nothing in the telling that regrets it.
At the turn of the row the gardener stops and asks a question back, which has not happened before, and the question is whether the party would like to see {what was kept|the one thing they kept|the exception}.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{There is always an exception.|Nobody throws away everything.|Here it comes.}"
asides.any: {member} {says yes before anybody else can|looks at the arm in the row and then at the gardener|nods once}

choices.text: Yes. Show us.
No. Some things are not for visitors.
Ask about the arm in the row instead.

ask_kept.text:
It is in a jar under the third bed, and it is {small|not large|about the size of a fist}, and it is the only thing on this world that is not growing.
What it is takes an hour to explain and is not explained in MarkovSpeak, which is how the party learns the gardener has a first language. The jar goes back under the bed. Everybody agrees, without a vote, never to mention where.

ask_arm.text:
It is planted at the wrist because it is the only part of the plant that {will not take otherwise|roots|is willing}, and it is an arm because the species it came off was {shaped that way|built like that|not human and not far off}.
The gardener walks the party through the whole growth cycle, twice, with corrections, in the manner of somebody who has been waiting a great many years to be asked a technical question about it.

gv_m.text:
The beds take the {material} and the gardener's hands go straight to work with it, no thanks offered, because thanks are for strangers.
Halfway down the row the hands stop. Something in the new stock is {wrong|not what it should be|carrying something}, and the gardener holds it up to the light and says, conversationally, that if this goes in the bed the bed will have to be burned.

choices.text: Put it in anyway. It is what we have.
Sort the whole lot before any of it goes in the ground.
Take it all back. Bring clean stock another time.

gv_sort.text:
Sorting it is {two hours|the rest of the afternoon|a long slow job} on a cloth in the shade, with the gardener naming what is wrong with each piece as it goes on the bad pile.
The good pile is most of it. The bad pile is burned properly. What comes back at the end of the row is a cutting of something that should not root in {ground} and does, and a debt the gardener considers settled.

gv_burn.text:
The sorting is done by eye and the eye is not trained, and {two|three} pieces go in the bed that should not have.
The bed is burned nine days later. The gardener does it without blame and replants from seed and will be {two years|a long time|the better part of three seasons} getting back to where they were, and says so in a tone that has no edge on it at all, which is worse.

gv_back.text:
The stock goes back in the pack and the party comes back with clean material {eleven days|a fortnight|some weeks} later, having gone a long way out of their way to do it.
The gardener does not comment. The gardener does, however, plant the new bed in the row nearest the door, which anybody who has spent a day in this garden would understand.

q_magamui.title: {One At A Time|The Quiet One In The Camp|Whose Idea Was It}

n0.text:
A survey camp at {place}, {few} of them, and every one of them can tell you exactly whose idea it was to dig here except the one whose idea it was.
They are all agreed it was a good idea. They are agreed in the same words. {wrongness}, and one of them has not blinked since the party walked in.
The dig itself is {nine|seven|eleven} metres down and neatly revetted, and nobody in the camp can say what they are digging for without {looking at somebody else first|checking a face|glancing sideways}.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Work out which one is being ridden.
Get the camp away from the dig, all of them, now.
Not the party's dig, not the party's camp.

id.text:
It's not the quiet one. The quiet one is {exhausted|running on nothing|three days past sleeping}, and has been carrying the whole camp's shifts because everybody else keeps forgetting they agreed to take them.
It is the one who has been most reasonable all afternoon. The Guild has standing orders about this and they are one line long, and it needs doing before the thing gets time to {move house|change tenant|find somebody else}.

ev.text:
It takes the whole of {leader}'s voice and every hour of daylight, and the camp comes off the dig in one piece and stays off it.
Up on the ridge, with distance under them, {few} of them start crying and one of them starts remembering things about the last month that had not previously happened to anybody.

wrong.text:
The party picks the wrong one, and the camp closes round the mistake the way a hand closes.
It is a bad {half hour|twenty minutes|hour} and only some of it is remembered afterwards, in the wrong order, by {different people|three different people|everybody differently}.

left.text:
Behind, the camp goes back to agreeing with itself, in the same words, on the same ground.
{member} writes the coordinates down and underlines them, which is what you do when you {cannot do anything|can do nothing else|have nothing else to give}.

ev_m.text:
Getting {few} people off a dig they all agree about takes the whole of {leader}'s voice and every hour of {daylight|the light|the afternoon}, and it works, and it works because one of them helps.
The one who helps is the {quiet one|tired one|one who has been doing everybody's shifts}, and halfway up the ridge they take {leader} by the sleeve and say, very fast, that there is a second camp two valleys over doing the same thing.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Of course there is.|There is always a second camp.|One is an accident. Two is a programme.}"
asides.any: {member} {gets the bearing before the sentence is finished|writes it on a hand|looks at the two valleys and says nothing}

choices.text: Get this camp clear and go no further.
Take the bearing and go and look at the second camp.
Sit the quiet one down and get the whole of it.

ev_two.text:
The second camp is {four|five} hours over broken ground and is already {empty|down to one|past helping}, and the dig there is finished, and what came out of it went east on a sledge two days ago.
There is a manifest in the mess tent, unburned, with a route on it. It is the single most valuable piece of paper anybody has carried out of this region in {a year|two seasons|a long while}.

ev_late.text:
Two valleys is easy to say and hard to walk, and the bearing was taken off a hand in bad light, and the party arrives at the wrong valley {at dusk|with the light going|an hour after it matters}.
The right one is found the following morning by the smoke. There is nothing in it but the dig, open, and the sledge ruts going east, and a camp's worth of boots arranged in pairs by the tents.

ev_talk.text:
It comes out in the order things come out in when somebody has been holding them for {three days|a week|too long}: the shifts, the agreeing, the way the words were always the same words, and the fact that they knew on day two and could not make the sentence come.
What they know is worth the whole trip. They are also, by the end of the telling, {asleep sitting up|finally asleep|unconscious in the proper sense}, which is its own kind of result.

left_m.text:
Walking away from it takes about {a hundred metres|two hundred paces|the first rise} to start feeling like a decision rather than a direction.
Behind, the camp goes back to agreeing with itself, in the same words, on the same {ground}. Ahead there is a whole rest of the day in which nothing is required of anybody.

choices.text: Keep walking.
Leave word at the nearest station instead. Somebody else's job.
Turn round. Get them off the dig.

left_word.text:
The nearest station is {two days|a day and a half|thirty hours} out and takes the report the way stations take reports, with a form, and a number, and a promise that is not exactly a promise.
Somebody does go. {Eleven days|A fortnight|Nine days} later, by which time the arithmetic of the thing has changed considerably, and the party's name is on the form as the ones who called it in.

q_pigeon.title: {Ninety Kilometres An Hour|The Bird With The Stick|Post}

n0.text:
There is a loft at {place}, built out of {remnant} and considerable stubbornness, and {asker} keeping {many} birds in it against {hazard}.
Nothing electronic gets in or out of here. The birds do, at ninety with a tailwind, with a stick tied to the leg, and one of them has not come back.
There is a second loft behind the first, {smaller|half the size|no bigger than a wardrobe}, shut, with the entry hole boarded over from the inside.

asides.loyal: {member} {positions themselves between {leader} and the door|nods firmly: "Right behind you, boss."|keeps a watchful eye on {leader}'s blind spot|stands ready to back up whatever call is made}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Go and find the bird.
Give {qty} {material} for the loft and carry the post yourselves.
Ask what is on the sticks.

fnd.text:
It is down under {remnant} with a wing that will mend and a stick still on the leg, and it puts up a fight about being picked up, which is a good sign in a bird.
What is on the stick is somebody's whole year. The loft pays in the only currency that means anything out here, which is being owed something by {a keeper of birds|the keeper of a loft|somebody who keeps birds}.

nof.text:
Two days of {ground} and {hazard} and nothing with feathers on it anywhere.
The keeper takes the news the way keepers do, which is by going to feed the others.

car.text:
The loft gets its {material}, and the party gets a satchel of sticks and a route, and does the round on foot because a hull would never make the last leg.
Every stop on it is somebody who has not heard from anybody in a season. Nobody lets the party leave without feeding them {first|first, properly|before anything else}.

asked.text:
Births, mostly. Prices. Two deaths that people needed to know about in an order that mattered.
One stick is not read out. It goes in a box with {lots} others, and the keeper says the box is for after, and does not say {after what|what after means|any more than that}.

asked_m.text:
Births, mostly. Prices. Two deaths that people needed to know about in an order that mattered, and one stick that is not read out and goes in a box with {lots} others.
The box is not locked. {asker} does not stop anybody looking at it, and does not offer, and goes to feed the birds in a way that means the offer is {never going to come|not going to be made|the party's own to make}.

choices.text: Leave the box alone. Ask about the second loft instead.
Read the box.
Ask, straight out, what the box is for.

asked_box.text:
They are all in the same hand and all to the same person and none of them were ever sent, because the person they are to has been {dead|gone|past reading} since before the loft was built.
The last one is dated this season. The party puts the lid back on and does not mention it, and {asker} knows they have read it, and something between the two parties settles that neither of them will ever name.

asked_loft.text:
The second loft is where the birds go that come back wrong: the ones that arrive with the stick gone, or with the wrong stick, or {with two|carrying two|with a stick tied by somebody who ties knots differently}.
{asker} keeps them alive and keeps them separate and has never once cooked one, and the reason for the boards on the entry hole is that {twice now|on two occasions|more than once} something has come in through it that was not a bird.

choices.text: Open it. Have a look.
Read the wrong sticks instead.
Leave the boards where they are.

asked_open.text:
Inside: {nine|eleven|a dozen} birds, quiet, healthy, all of them facing the same wall.
There is nothing on the wall. There has never been anything on the wall. The boards go back up within the minute and {asker} helps, without a word, having clearly been waiting for somebody else to look first.

asked_code.text:
The wrong sticks are not wrong. They are a second correspondence running through the same birds, in a substitution anybody who has done a season of this would spot, which means whoever set it up assumed the loft-keeper {never would|would never look|had no reason to}.
They are route reports. Somebody has been using a bird loft in the middle of nowhere as a relay for {a fortnight|the better part of a season|months}, and the party can now read every word of it.

car_m.text:
The loft gets its {material}, the party gets a satchel of sticks and a route, and the round is done on foot because a hull would never make the last leg.
On the third stop there is nobody home and the door is open, and the stick for that address is still in the satchel with {nowhere to go|nobody to take it|no hand to put it in}.

choices.text: Finish the round. Bring the undelivered one back.
Read the ground at the open door before moving on.
Wait at the third stop until dark.

car_track.text:
Two sets out, one set in, all of them going the same way and the incoming set on top of the outgoing one, which means whoever came back came back after the people who left.
They are half a day ahead on an easy line. The party catches them at a water stop, hands over the stick, and gets the whole story plus a meal plus a name worth having at {four|five} more doors on this route.

car_wait.text:
Dark comes and nobody comes with it, and the party sleeps in a stranger's house with the door propped as it was found, out of {a superstition nobody admits to|manners|something like manners}.
In the morning the stick is put on the table under a cup, the round is finished, and the loft-keeper says only that the third stop has done this {before|twice before|more than once} and always comes back.

q_father.title: {What Fell|The Piece Of Him|Nothing Grows Around It}

n0.text:
Something came down at {place} that is not debris, and {ground} for {few} metres around it has stopped doing anything at all: no dust settling, no {sound}, nothing rotting.
{instrument} will not read it. Reading it is not the sort of thing it is for. {asker} is kneeling at the edge of the circle, and has been for some time.
The kneeling one has been there long enough for the knees to have made two shallow cups in ground that {does not otherwise take a mark|nothing else has marked|has taken nothing else}.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Touch it.
Get it covered and get word out.
Leave it where it fell.

touch.text:
It is cold and it is not stone and something goes up the arm and keeps going.
When it lets go, the world is arranged slightly differently and {leader} has something they did not {Walk in|Step through the entrance|Cross the threshold|Head inside} with, and no training anywhere accounts for it, {which is what it came for|which is what it wanted|which is the trade}.

cov.text:
The {material} goes over it and the circle goes under a cairn, and the position is written down twice in two different hands.
The kneeling one thanks the party in a language that ran out of speakers a while ago, and pays in the way of people with nothing: {everything they have|all of it|what little there is}.

lv.text:
It stays where it fell with somebody kneeling at the edge of it, and the party walks out through ground that starts behaving normally again about {forty|thirty|fifty} paces on.
It is a relief. Nobody expected it to be {a relief|that|one}.

touch_m.text:
It is a hand's breadth away and the cold off it arrives before the hand does. The kneeling one does not look up, and does not stop the party, and does say one thing in the dead language, twice, in the cadence of {a warning|an instruction|something rehearsed}.
Nobody in the party speaks it. Everybody in the party can hear that it matters.

choices.text: Touch it anyway.
Get the words down and work them out first.
Have {member} touch it instead of {leader}.

touch_word.text:
The sentence is an instruction and the instruction is about the hand: which one, and that it must be the one you write with, and that it must be flat.
Done properly, what goes up the arm goes up it the way water goes up a wick rather than the way a current goes up a wire. {leader} keeps everything they came with and gains something besides, and the kneeling one weeps, which is apparently what the instruction was for.

touch_other.text:
{member} puts a hand on it without ceremony and goes very still for {nine seconds|a count of nine|longer than looks safe}.
What comes back is not what went in. {member} is fine, says so, keeps saying so, and does not sleep properly for a fortnight, and knows three things on the way home that nobody taught them.

cov_m.text:
Covering it is easy. Getting word out is the part with a decision in it: the nearest thing to a transmitter out here belongs to somebody who will sell the coordinates on within {a day|hours|the week}, and everybody standing at the cairn knows it.
The kneeling one waits to be told what the party has decided, in the manner of somebody who has already decided not to argue.

choices.text: Send it clear. Let whoever comes, come.
Send it in a cipher only the Empire reads.
Send nothing. Put it under the cairn and forget the number.

cov_cipher.text:
The message goes out as {four groups of five|twenty characters|a block of nonsense} and is repeated twice and is never referred to again by anybody.
What arrives eleven days later arrives quietly, in the right colours, with the right paperwork, and takes the thing away under a tarpaulin. The party is thanked in writing by somebody who signs with a title and no name.

cov_leak.text:
{The cipher is good.|The cipher holds.|Nothing is wrong with the cipher.} The operator is better, and sells the block on unread, which turns out to be worth more than selling it read.
Three parties arrive inside a week and none of them are the Empire. The cairn is opened, the circle is walked in by people in the wrong {boots|colours|vehicles}, and the kneeling one is not there the next time anybody looks.

cov_quiet.text:
The cairn goes up properly, the position is written down twice and burned once, and the kneeling one is left with water, food and the second copy.
Nobody profits. {member} notes in the diary that the ground inside the circle had begun, very slightly, to settle again by the time they left, which is either {healing or appetite|good news or the opposite|nothing or everything}.

q_prospect.title: {The Claim|Markers In The Ground|Two Names On One Patch}

n0.text:
Two sets of claim markers at {place}, driven into the same {ground}, {few} paces apart, both of them legal on paper somewhere.
{asker} has one set. The other set's owner is due back at any hour, and there is exactly one seam under all of it. {sound}, which does not help anybody's nerves.
Both sets of markers are new. The {ground} between them has been walked over so many times in the last week that it is {polished|beaten flat|shining}.

asides.calm: {member} suggests that a seam under two claims is a bigger seam than either of them costed for.
asides.aggressive: {member} has already worked out which set of markers comes out easier.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Broker it before the other one gets back.
Survey the seam properly and let the ground decide.
Pull the other set of markers.

bro.text:
A split, in writing, witnessed by {three|four} people who do not like each other, which is the strongest kind of witnessing there is.
The other one arrives to a signed page instead of an argument and takes twenty minutes to stop looking for the catch. The party's cut is written in as brokerage, which nobody {objects to|argues with|queries}.

sur.text:
The seam runs {the other way entirely|nothing like where either paper says|at right angles to both of them}. Both claims clip the shoulder of it and neither of them sits on it.
The real body is out under open ground nobody has papered at all, which the party knows first and by {some distance|a clear margin|a day at the least}.

brf.text:
The other one gets back mid-sentence and has been rehearsing {on the walk|the whole way up|since the last ridge}.
It goes the way these go, at speed, in the wrong order, on ground neither of them will {get to keep|keep|hold by the end of it}.

pull.text:
The markers come out {easily|without much argument|one-handed}. That is the trouble with markers.
Someone's going to walk back onto this patch and find their year gone, and the party is paid in ore for having made it happen {quickly and quietly|quickly|without a word said}.

sur_m.text:
Surveying it properly takes {the rest of the day|four hours and a lamp|until the light goes} and the ground gives a clean answer: the seam runs {the other way entirely|nothing like where either paper says|at right angles to both of them}, and neither claim is sitting on it.
The real body is out under open ground nobody has papered at all. The party is, for about the next {hour|two hours|day}, the only people alive who know this.

choices.text: Tell them both. Let them work it out.
Say nothing and file on the open ground ourselves.
Sell the survey to the one who is here.

sur_file.text:
The paperwork is filed at the nearest office by the fastest route and is {four hours|half a day|a morning} ahead of anybody else's, and the ground is the party's before either claimant has finished arguing.
It is entirely legal. It is also going to be remembered, out here, where there are not many people and all of them talk.

sur_bust.text:
The office wants a bearing off a fixed monument and the nearest fixed monument is {a day|eleven hours|most of a day} away, and by the time the form is right the other claimant's cousin has filed on the same open ground off a survey they did not pay for.
The party gets nothing except the education, which is admittedly considerable.

sur_sell.text:
The survey changes hands for {payment} and a handshake that is meant, and {asker} is over the open ground with stakes before the other one is back on the ridge.
It is a good price and a fast one and it does not survive contact with the other claimant's opinion of it, which arrives {at the fire that night|a week later|by proxy, in writing, from an office}.

pull_m.text:
The markers come out {easily|without much argument|one-handed}. That is the trouble with markers.
Under the third one there is a survey peg that is older than both claims, driven properly, with a brass cap on it and a number, and the number belongs to {somebody who is not out here any more|a company that stopped existing|an office that burned down in the war}.

choices.text: Pull it too. Sell the lot.
Read the cap and find out whose ground this actually is.
Put every marker back where it was and leave.

pull_cap.text:
The number leads, by way of {two offices and a bribe|a dead registry and a friendly clerk|one long afternoon of paper}, to a holding that nobody has claimed against in {forty years|two generations|a very long time} and that is still, technically, enforceable.
What that is worth depends entirely on who the party sells it to, and it is worth a great deal to at least three of them.

pull_back.text:
Every marker goes back in its own hole, tamped, straight, exactly as found, which takes {longer than pulling them did|twice as long|most of what is left of the day}.
Nobody will ever know. The other claimant arrives at dusk to an argument they can have fairly, and the party is over the rise before it starts.

n0.text:
There is a handset at {place}, an old indestructible brick of a thing, wired into {remnant} by somebody who knew what they were doing.
It is tuned. That is the point of it being here. {asker} has been keeping the site since before the party landed and will not touch it, and is very clear that the not touching is a decision and not a fear.
There is a pad of paper beside it with {nine|eleven|a good many} numbers written down and crossed out, and one at the bottom that is written twice and not crossed out at all.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Call.
Retune it with {qty} {material} and hand it back to the keeper.
Cut the line.

ans.text:
Something picks up on the fourth ring and does not say hello.
What it says instead takes eleven seconds and is answering a question nobody in the party has asked out loud, and afterwards {leader} sits down on {ground} for a while.

wrongno.text:
Something picks up. It's not what the tuning was for. It stays on the line after the handset goes down and it is still there, faintly, under {sound}, for the whole walk out.
{member} does not sleep properly for a while after.

ret.text:
The {material} does it. The tuning comes back true and the keeper takes the handset in both hands and looks at it, and then at the party, and asks them to go outside for a minute.
Whatever gets said in there takes longer than a minute. Afterwards the keeper is different in the face and pays {over the odds|far over the odds|more than was asked}.

cut2.text:
The wire parts and the warmth goes out of the casing in about {a second and a half|two seconds|the time it takes to put it down}.
The keeper says thank you, and means it, and is crying, and means that {too|as well|just as much}.

ret_m.text:
The {material} does it. The tuning comes back true, and the keeper takes the handset in both hands and does not dial, and looks at the pad, and then at the party.
The number at the bottom is the one they have never rung, for {eleven years|a long time|as long as they have kept the site}, and the whole reason for keeping the site is to be able to ring it {one day|eventually|when it is time}.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Nobody keeps a wire alive for eleven years to not use it.|They are going to ring it the second we are over the hill.|That is not a phone number, that is a life sentence.}"
asides.any: {member} {looks at the pad and does not write anything down|steps outside before being asked|puts the kettle on, for want of anything better}

choices.text: Give them the handset and go outside.
Ask, gently, what happens if they never ring it.
Copy the number down for ourselves.

ret_talk.text:
What happens is nothing, and they know it, and saying it out loud in front of {four strangers|strangers|somebody who will leave tomorrow} is apparently the only way it was ever going to get said.
They ring it that evening with the party standing outside in {weather}. Whatever is said on it is short. Afterwards the keeper gives away the handset, the site, and the pad, and walks {east|out|down the track} with one bag.

ret_copy.text:
Eleven digits, copied on a wrist, in a hurry, while the keeper is looking at the wire.
It is not rung that day, or that week. It sits in a notebook getting easier to read every time the notebook is opened, which is not how {ink|a biro|graphite} behaves, and eventually somebody in the party is going to be alone with a handset.

cut_m.text:
The wire is old, doubled, and warm, and it would part with {one cut|a single cut|about four seconds of work}.
The keeper does not stop the party. The keeper stands slightly too close and says, in the flat voice of somebody who has rehearsed being reasonable, that whatever is on the other end has been getting {closer|louder|easier to hear} for a year and that some nights it rings first.

choices.text: Cut it.
Cut it and take the handset with us, so it cannot be rewired.
Wait for it to ring first. Listen once.

cut_take.text:
The wire parts, the warmth goes out of the casing, and the brick goes in the pack over {one objection|a single objection|an objection that is not really an objection}.
The keeper watches the party out of sight with both hands empty for the first time in {years|a long time|eleven years}. The handset never works again, which does not stop it being warm, {twice|once or twice|on certain nights}, in the pack.

cut_ring.text:
It rings at {nine minutes past|eleven minutes past|some minutes past} and everybody in the room finds out something about themselves in the time it takes to reach for it.
What is on the line is not for the party and says so, at length, in a voice that is using {somebody's|a familiar|the keeper's} vowels. The wire is cut immediately afterwards, by three people at once, and nobody sleeps at the site that night.

q_lavabath.title: {Harmless Now|The Pool That Drains You|In Up To The Knee}

n0.text:
There is a working at {place} where {ground} opens onto a pool that ought to be lethal and is not, since the Squishing took the heat out of the argument.
Doesn't burn. It drains. {asker} has {few} people going in to the knee in shifts to pull something out of the bottom, and they are coming out empty and grey.
There is a tally cut into the frame by the pool, one mark a shift, and the marks stop being neat about {a third|halfway|two thirds} of the way along.

asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Take a shift.
Rig a way to do it without anybody going in.
Ask what is down there first.

gotit.text:
Two minutes in the pool costs about what an hour of hard casting costs, and the second minute costs more than the first.
What comes up on the third shift is worth every unit of it, and {asker} says so, and pays like somebody who has been waiting {a long time|weeks|the whole season} to pay somebody.

drain.text:
It takes more than it was supposed to, all at once, near the end of the shift.
{leader} comes out on somebody else's shoulder, empty to the floor of the tank, and it takes until the next day to be worth {talking to|much|anything at all}.

rig.text:
The {material} makes a grab and a line and a frame to hang the whole thing off, and it takes three attempts and works on the fourth.
Nobody goes in the pool again. That is the part of it the shift crew care about, and they are the ones who decide {what the party is paid|the rate|what it was worth}.

what.text:
{Somebody's brother|Somebody's daughter|Somebody's mate off the same shift}, is what is down there, from before anybody knew the pool did not burn.
The shifts are not mining. They have been going in to the knee in turns for {a fortnight|three weeks|eleven days} to bring somebody home, and did not think the party would help if they said so first.

choices.text: Then take a shift.
Rig the grab instead.

home.text:
It takes {the rest of the day|until dark|another six hours} and most of what everybody has, and it is done, and he comes up.
The camp does what camps do, which is to feed everyone at once and put the party in the middle of it and not let them pay for {anything ever again|a single thing|anything, ever}.

rig_m.text:
The {material} will make a grab, a line and a frame to hang the whole thing off, and the crew watch the building of it the way people watch a thing that should have existed a fortnight ago.
On the third attempt the grab comes up with something on it that is the right size and the wrong shape, and the shift boss stops the whole operation with one hand up.

choices.text: Finish the job. Whatever it is, bring it up.
Ask the boss what shape they were expecting.
Go in after it by hand rather than drag it.

rig_hand.text:
Going in to the shoulder is a different proposition from going in to the knee, and the pool takes it out of the body in a way that has {nothing to do with heat|no connection to heat at all|nothing to do with temperature}.
What is brought up is brought up whole, in two hands, by somebody who was careful with it. The crew do not cheer. They take their {hats|helmets} off, which is a great deal louder.

gotit_m.text:
Two minutes in the pool costs about what an hour of hard casting costs, and the second minute costs more than the first, and the shift crew count out loud from the edge.
On the second shift, at about the ninety-second mark, the counting stops. Not because anything has happened: because everybody on the edge is {listening|looking at the pool|watching something that is not the party}.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{They stopped counting. Get out.|Nobody on that edge is looking at us.|Ninety seconds and the whole crew went quiet.}"
asides.any: {member} {keeps counting out loud alone|gets a hand out towards the pool|does not stop the shift}

choices.text: Finish the shift. Whatever they can hear.
Get out now and find out what they heard.
Go deeper. To the waist, on the third shift.

gotit_deep.text:
To the waist is {four times|a great deal more than|not twice} what the knee costs, and it is done on the third shift with two people holding a line and everybody else counting.
What comes up at the end of it is what {asker} has had crews going in for: not ore and not a body, but the thing that is {holding the heat back|keeping the pool cold|doing this to the pool}, and it comes up in two hands and is {small|not large|lighter than it should be}.

q_scrap.title: {A Scrap Of Creation|The Door In The Air|Test Ground}

n0.text:
There is a seam in the air over {place} about the size of a door, and behind it the light is the wrong colour and {ground} keeps going into somewhere that is not this rock.
It is one of the old test spaces. Something practised here, a long time ago, and did not clear up. {tone}.
The edge of the seam has {handprints|marks|prints} on the near side of it, at the height a person would steady themselves at, {going in|pointing in|all facing the same way}.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.impulsive: {member} has an arm through to the elbow, waving.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Go through.
Peg it open with {qty} {material} and map the edge.
Mark it and walk away from it.

thr.text:
On the far side: a room the size of {a country|a weather system|somewhere that has a name} with one idea in it, worked out over and over on every surface until whoever it was got it right.
The last version of it is still there, finished, sitting on nothing, and it is not guarded because it never occurred to anybody that the room would be {found|found at all|walked into}.

lost.text:
The far side does not keep the same layout twice, and the door is not where the door was.
It takes {many} hours to get back out and everybody arrives on {ground} lighter than they went in, in ways that take inventory to establish.

peg.text:
The {material} holds the seam at the width it was found at, which is the whole trick: a scrap that is not measured is a scrap that closes.
The measurements are worth money to four separate parties and the party sells them once, to the one that will {publish|publish it|put it in print}.

mk.text:
A cairn, a bearing, {a page in the book|two lines in the log|a sketch nobody will believe}, and the light going on being the wrong colour behind them all the way to the horizon.
Some doors are for {telling somebody about|reporting|leaving to people better equipped}.

thr_m.text:
Through is one step and the step is nothing at all. On the far side there is a room the size of {a country|a weather system|somewhere that has a name}, with one idea in it, worked out over and over on every surface until whoever it was got it right.
The door behind the party is still a door. It is also, by the time anyone checks, {nine metres|some distance|a good way} from where it was.

choices.text: Take the last version of it and get out.
Fix the way out first, then look at anything.
Read the workings from the beginning. All of them.

thr_line.text:
A line from the door to the waist and a knot that will not come undone by itself, which costs {four minutes|five minutes|a little time} and buys the whole afternoon.
The room can move the door as much as it likes. The party works the surfaces in order, takes the finished version, follows the line home, and comes out {exactly where they went in|onto the right rock|at the right seam} with full packs.

thr_read.text:
It is one idea, worked {nine hundred|a thousand|several hundred} times, and reading it from the beginning is reading somebody learn something over what must have been {years|a working life|a very long time}.
The last version is not the best one. The best one is about two thirds of the way along, before the author started being clever, and it is that one the party writes down.

mk_m.text:
A cairn, a bearing, {a page in the book|two lines in the log|a sketch nobody will believe}, and the light going on being the wrong colour behind them.
About {two hundred metres|a quarter of a kilometre|two hundred paces} out, {member} looks back and counts the cairn twice, because there are two of them now, at the same distance apart as the party is from the seam.

choices.text: Do not look back again. Walk.
Go back and knock the second cairn down.
Sit down and measure both of them properly.

mk_second.text:
The second cairn is made of the same stones as the first, which is not possible, because the first one is {still there|forty paces behind it|exactly where it was left}.
It comes down easily. Walking away from two flat patches of ground feels considerably worse than walking away from one cairn, and nobody says so until the fire that night.

mk_measure.text:
Measured, the two cairns and the seam make a triangle with one angle in it that the instruments will not agree on, and the disagreement is {consistent|repeatable|the same every time}, which makes it data rather than a fault.
The Foundation buys the figures. Somebody else buys them again a year later, having been told by the Foundation that they do not exist.

n0.text:
There are {few} people at {place} going about a working day with nothing behind the eyes at all.
They eat. They walk the same route. One of them is still doing a job that stopped mattering some time ago, in order, correctly, with nobody in there to do it. {wrongness}.
All {few} of them are wearing their own clothes, correctly, {down to the buttons|including the buttons|fastened properly}, which is somehow the part that is hardest to look at.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Find what took them.
Feed them and keep the routes clear.
Put them down.

found.text:
The residue is on {ground} in a ring, and it is not the sort of thing that goes off by itself, and there is a serial on the fragment.
That serial is a matter of very considerable interest to people who will pay for it and to people who will kill for it, and the party gets to choose which conversation to {have|have first|be in}.

nofound.text:
Whatever it was cleaned up after itself {thoroughly|to a standard|the way a professional does}, and the only evidence left walks around eating breakfast at the correct hour.
The party writes down what they saw. Writing it down is {what there is|all there is|the whole of what can be done}.

feed.text:
The stores go into the hoppers along the route and the route gets swept and the doors get propped where the doors were sticking.
They will go on until {the bodies stop|the last of them wears out|something else stops them}. Zero argument in which this was the useful thing to do, and everybody does it {anyway|anyway, all day|regardless}.

down.text:
It is quick, and quiet, and correct by every standard anybody has written down.
Nobody talks on the way back to the pad. {member} is sick behind a rock at the halfway mark and nobody mentions it {then or afterwards|then|at any point afterwards}.

feed_m.text:
The stores go into the hoppers along the route, the route gets swept, the sticking doors get propped.
On the second day one of them stops in the middle of the route, turns, and {looks straight at {leader}|faces the party|looks at somebody rather than through them} for about four seconds, and then goes on walking.

asides.nurturing: {member} is at the hopper before anybody has decided anything, and stays there.
asides.any: {member} {writes down the hour|marks the place on the route|says nothing and watches the same one all afternoon}

choices.text: Keep feeding them. Keep the routes clear.
Work on that one. See what is left in there.
Follow that one's route to the end of it.

feed_one.text:
It takes {nine days|a fortnight|eleven days} of sitting with somebody who is not there, and on one of those days there is a name, and two days after the name there is a sentence with a want in it.
What comes back is not all of them and is unmistakably somebody. They will not be walking the route again. The rest still are, and that is the arithmetic the party has to carry out of here.

feed_none.text:
Nine days, and then a fortnight, and there is nothing in there to come back: the four seconds on the route were the whole of it, a groove worn by something that used to be a person walking past something that used to matter.
The party leaves the stores stacked and the doors propped and goes, and {member} does not eat properly for {a week|days|some time} afterwards.

feed_route.text:
The route ends at a door that is not on any of the others' routes, and behind the door there is a room set up for {one person|somebody|a single occupant} to wait in comfortably for a long time.
There is food in it, replaced recently. Somebody out here has been keeping one of them, and it is not the party, and it is not any of the {few}.

down_m.text:
It would be quick, and quiet, and correct by every standard anybody has written down, and everybody in the party knows which of them will do it and has known for {an hour|some time|most of the afternoon}.
The one still doing the job that stopped mattering is at the far end of the route. It will take four minutes to walk there, and the four minutes are the worst part.

choices.text: Do it.
Check, properly, that there is nothing left in any of them first.
Put the weapons down. Feed them instead.

down_check.text:
Pupils, reflexes, the small tests that mean something: {two|three} of them are empty in the way a coat is empty, and one of them is not, and the one that is not is the one doing the job nobody needs done.
The empty ones are seen to, correctly. The other is carried out, and wakes up {eleven days|a fortnight|nine days} later a long way from here, and the whole business is thereafter a different story with a living person in it.

q_road.title: {The Turn-Off|Road Where No Road Is|The Encompassing}

n0.text:
There is a road at {place}. Not a track: a road, made, cambered, with a white line down it, running out of {ground} at both ends into nothing.
{asker} is parked on the hard shoulder of it with the engine running and has been for a while, working up to something.
The white line is fresh. Somebody has been {repainting it|keeping it up|out here with a brush} inside the last month.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Get the engine calibrated with {qty} {material} and take the turn-off.
Walk it to the end.
Note the bearing and stay off it.

turn.text:
Calibrated right, the road ahead folds up {like a map being put away|the way a concertina goes|into itself}, and the turn-off is somewhere else entirely by the time the wheels reach it.
Wherever that was, the party was there for about four minutes and came back with things that are not sold anywhere {on this rock|in this system|anybody can name}.

walk.text:
It takes {all day|until the light goes|the better part of a day} and the road ends the way it began, cleanly, mid-camber, with the white line stopping at a right angle.
At the end of it there is a shrine of sorts, made by drivers, and everything on it was left by somebody who got somewhere. The party leaves something and takes nothing, and the walk back is shorter than the walk out by a margin nobody {wants to discuss|is willing to name|does the arithmetic on}.

loop.text:
Somewhere past the fourth hour the road starts arriving at itself. The same white line, the same {remnant} on the same side.
It takes {member} spotting their own bootprint going the other way to break it, and everybody comes off the surface onto honest {ground} feeling several hours poorer than the clock says.

off.text:
The bearing goes in the book and the road goes on lying there being a road.
{asker} is still parked on the shoulder when the party is a kilometre out, still working up to {it|whatever it is|the turn}.

walk_m.text:
It takes {all day|until the light goes|the better part of a day} and the road ends the way it began: cleanly, mid-camber, with the white line stopping at a right angle.
At the end of it there is a shrine of sorts, made by drivers out of what drivers carry, and a paint tin, and a brush standing in it that is {still wet|not yet dry|wet enough to use}.

choices.text: Sit at the shrine a while and go back.
Paint the line on. Another few metres of it.
Read what the drivers left at the shrine.

walk_paint.text:
Three metres of white line onto ground that was not road when the brush went down and is road by the time it lifts.
Nobody discusses this on the walk back. The road is three metres longer. {member} checks the odometer of a vehicle that was not moving and finds it {four|three} kilometres further on than it was.

walk_read.text:
What the drivers left is not offerings, it is a procedure: {nine|seven|eleven} instructions in as many hands, about what to do at the end of the road, in what order, and what not to do on any account.
Followed properly it takes forty minutes and involves a great deal of standing still. At the end of it the road is still there and something about the party's relationship to it has been formally settled.

off_m.text:
The bearing goes in the book and the road goes on lying there being a road.
{asker} is still parked on the shoulder when the party is a kilometre out, engine running, and then the engine stops, and in the quiet that follows it is possible to hear a door.

choices.text: Keep going. Not our road.
Go back for them.
Watch through the glass from here.

off_back.text:
The vehicle is on the shoulder with the door open and the seat warm and the handbrake off, and the road ahead of it is {empty|clean|exactly as long as it was}.
The party pushes it off the surface onto honest ground, which takes all four of them, and the engine starts on the third try and will not go near the road again. Whoever was driving is not found, then or later.

off_watch.text:
Through the glass, at a kilometre, it is possible to watch somebody get out of a vehicle, walk to the white line, stand on it, and {stop being there|not be there|go from being a person to being a length of road} without any part of it looking sudden.
The party marks the spot, marks the hour, and does not go back. The notes on it are read, later, by people who pay for that sort of note.

qe_bubble.title: {The Edge Of It|Eighty Or Nothing|Tuesday Again}

n0.text:
{hour}, on the road out of {place}, the air ahead goes wrong in the way air does about {few} metres from the edge of one of them.
The map marks it. The map has not been redrawn since {timeAgo}, and the edge has moved. {stranger} is standing just on the safe side of the line with a bicycle and a face that says today is not the first time.
There are {two|three} vehicles on the verge this side of the edge, parked neatly, {with the keys in|unlocked|all of them facing out}.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Go in and bring whoever is in there out.
Re-mark the edge properly, all the way round.
Take the long way and say nothing to anybody.

outt.text:
Inside it is the same Tuesday it has been for a while and everybody in it knows, which is the part nobody prepares you for.
Getting out means going outward over eighty, and {vehicle} is not built for it, and it is done anyway with three people in the back holding on to each other and one of them {counting|counting out loud|watching the needle}.

stuck.text:
The run at the edge comes up short, and short means the whole thing again from the top, on the same Tuesday, with everybody's confidence a good deal thinner.
They get out on the {fourth|third|fifth} go. Some of the fourth go is not remembered, and the party comes out with a day of their own {missing|gone|unaccounted for}.

mark.text:
Posts and paint the whole way round, at the real edge, which takes until dark and a good deal more {material} than anybody estimated.
Everything that comes down that road for the next twenty years will slow for those posts. Nobody will ever know the party did it. The Society hears about it within a week.

away.text:
The long way is {an hour and a half|two hours} of bad surface and it is {an hour and a half|time|a detour} nobody complains about.
Behind, the map goes on saying what it has said since {timeAgo}, and the edge goes on being where it actually is.

mark_m.text:
Posts and paint the whole way round at the real edge, which means walking the real edge, which means {four kilometres|the better part of a day|a long circuit} of finding out exactly where it is by the only method available.
About two thirds of the way round, the edge crosses a farm track, and on the far side of the track, inside, there is a house with a light on.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Do not knock.|We are marking it, not visiting it.|That light has been on since the map was right.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts a post in on the near side of the track and looks at the house|checks the watch against the sun|counts the windows}

choices.text: Post it, paint it, and walk on round.
Knock.
Work out how long it has been in there.

mark_knock.text:
It is answered inside {four seconds|no time|the time it takes to lower a hand}, by somebody who is delighted, who has the kettle on, and who asks after {a war|a government|somebody's coronation} that finished a long time ago.
The party stays {twenty minutes|half an hour|too long} and comes out onto the track with the light going and the distinct sense of having left something behind in there that they cannot inventory.

mark_date.text:
The clouds inside are the wrong clouds for the season and have been the wrong clouds for a while, and the growth on the near side of the edge gives the rest: {eleven|nine|fourteen} years, give or take a spring.
The figure goes on the posts along with the paint. Every hauler on this road for the next twenty years slows at those posts and reads that number, and it is the number, not the paint, that makes them slow.

away_m.text:
The long way is {an hour and a half|two hours} of bad surface and it is time nobody complains about.
Half an hour along it there is a {vehicle} coming the other way, fast, with a load on and a driver who does not know, and there is exactly one chance to flag them down.

choices.text: Let them go. Not our road.
Flag them down.
Get across the road and make them stop.

away_flag.text:
They see the arms, they slow, they stop, and they listen with the engine running because that is how these conversations are had on a road.
The map in the cab is the same map. They turn round. At the next fire down the line the party's description goes round attached to the phrase {"the ones on the bad road"|"those four on the detour"|"whoever flagged Kolya down"}.

away_block.text:
Standing in a road in front of a loaded {vehicle} is a way of finding out what your own nerve is worth, and it works, at the cost of {a wing mirror|the near-side mirror|somebody's jacket}.
The driver's opinion of the party takes {twenty minutes|a while|the rest of the layby} to come round, and then comes round entirely, and there is food in the cab and it gets shared.

qe_note.title: {The Security Strip|Notes With The Thread Picked Out|Small Denominations}

n0.text:
In a back room off {street} there is a table, a lamp, and {stranger} taking the security thread out of euro notes with a needle, one note at a time, into a saucer.
There is a lot in the saucer. The notes go back into circulation afterwards and nobody has ever noticed, because nobody has ever had a reason to look.
The needle work is {beautiful|extremely fine|the work of somebody who has done thousands}, and the hands doing it are shaking the entire time.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
