asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Buy the saucer.
Work out what it is for.
This is a currency offence and a considerably worse one underneath.

buy.text:
It changes hands into a tin and the tin goes into the pack wrapped in {cloth|a shirt|two layers of the same cloth}, because the pigment does not care for light.
What it is worth is not really a price. A round of it will kill somebody standing in a loop, and there is enough here for a round or two, and now that is the party's {problem to carry|problem|to carry}.

for.text:
Not counterfeiting. Coating.
There is a workbench under the table with {few} rounds on it, half done, and a list of names, and every name on the list is somebody who has been sitting inside a bubble being untouchable for years while people on the outside {had opinions about it|argued about it|wrote letters}.

forf.text:
The story holds all evening: {a hobby, a pigment, a private eccentricity|an old habit, a pigment, nothing in it|a collection, a pigment, a way to pass an evening}, and the saucer is just a saucer.
It is a good story and it is told by somebody who has had a long time to practise it, and the party leaves with nothing but a slight itch about the {third|second|fourth} answer.

rep.text:
It goes on paper and the paper goes in at the desk with {paper} attached, and the room is cleared within a day.
The party never learns which of the two possible reasons it was cleared for, {which is an answer of a kind|which answers it well enough|which is answer enough}.

buy_m.text:
The saucer changes hands for {payment} and goes into a tin, wrapped in {cloth|a shirt|two layers of the same cloth}, because the pigment does not care for light.
{stranger} does not count the money. {stranger} asks, instead, whether the party would like the list as well, and the list is a page of names, and the name at the top has been crossed out {recently|this week|since yesterday}.

choices.text: Take the tin. Leave the list. Not our business.
Take the list and find out what the crossing out means.
Ask why the hands are shaking.

buy_list.text:
Crossed out means done, and done means a round was made and a round was used, and the man at the top of the list has been {untouchable|inside a bubble|beyond reach} for {eleven years|a decade|a very long time} and is not any more.
The rest of the list is {nine|eleven} names of people who are about to find out the same thing. What that is worth depends entirely on which of them the party warns, and whether they warn any.

buy_heat.text:
Asking about a crossed-out name in a back room off {street} is a question that leaves the room {inside the hour|before the party does|faster than the party does}.
The tin is in the pack and the pack stays shut for a fortnight, because for a fortnight there is somebody at the end of every street the party walks down, not doing anything, just being at the end of it.

buy_hands.text:
It is the pigment. It has been the pigment for {two years|a long time|longer than anybody should}, and it goes in through the fingers and it does not come out, and {stranger} has known this since about the third saucer.
They take the treatment offered, badly and grudgingly, and they do not stop working. But the gloves the party leaves behind are used, which is visible on the table the next time anybody passes.

rep_m.text:
It goes on paper in {four lines|a short paragraph|as few words as will do} and the paper goes in at the desk with {paper} attached.
The clerk reads it twice, which clerks do not, and asks whether the party would prefer the currency desk or the other one, and does not say what the other one is.

choices.text: The currency desk. A currency offence is what we saw.
The other one.
Take the paper back. Go and warn {stranger} instead.

rep_other.text:
The other desk is {up a staircase|at the back|on a different floor} and has nobody queueing at it and a man behind it who listens without writing anything down.
The room off {street} is cleared inside {four hours|the afternoon|a day}. So are {two|three} other rooms in other towns that the party never mentioned, which means the man behind the desk already had most of it and was waiting for the last piece.

rep_warn.text:
The paper comes back off the desk, which takes {a lie|some nerve|a story about a name being wrong}, and the walk back to {street} takes {twenty minutes|a quarter of an hour|no time at all}.
The room is empty by the time the party gets there. The table, the lamp and the saucer are gone and the needle is still on the floorboards, and somewhere out there somebody has {four hours|half a day|a start} that they would not otherwise have had.

qe_naguka.title: {Corpse Paint At The Crossroads|The One With The Wrong Face|Kin}

n0.text:
There is a Naguka sitting at the crossroads outside {place} with the paint half off, holding a broken instrument and no idea which direction is which.
The horde went that way {timeAgo}. This one did not, and cannot explain why in more than about {six|five|seven} words at a time, and keeps saying one of them.
The paint that is left on it is the horde's own marking, and somebody has tried to scrub it off {from the outside|with sand|not very kindly}.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.aggressive: {member} has counted the crossroads' sightlines and does not like any of them.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Feed it and take it as far as the next town.
Fix the instrument with {qty} {material}.
Hand it in at the barracks.

take2.text:
It eats like something that has not, and walks in the middle of the group without being asked to, and by the second hour is telling a story with about {eleven|nine|a dozen} words in it and using all of them twice.
At the town it is taken in by somebody who has done this before. The collective knows, within the day, that the party did not leave one of theirs {at a crossroads|in a ditch|standing at a crossroads}.

fix.text:
The {material} does it, roughly, and the first note out of it stops the conversation dead.
What it plays at the crossroads is not for the party and is not for anybody. Halfway through, {member} realises they are hearing something the horde is also hearing, {distance}, and gets very quiet.

hand.text:
The barracks take it and sign for it and are correct throughout, and the sergeant does not meet {anybody's eye|the party's eye|anybody's eye at all} while doing the signing.
The collective unconscious does not have a subtle way of registering an opinion, and it {registers one|registers this one|makes it known}.

take_m.text:
It eats like something that has not, and walks in the middle of the group without being asked to, and by the second hour is telling a story with about {eleven|nine|a dozen} words in it and using all of them twice.
At the third hour there is a checkpoint on the road into the next town, and it is manned, and the Naguka stops walking about {two hundred metres|a distance|well} short of it without being told to.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{It knows what a checkpoint is. Think about that.|It stopped before we did.|Somebody taught it that.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts a coat over its shoulders|walks back to it and waits|looks at the checkpoint and then at the ditch}

choices.text: Walk it through the checkpoint. Straight in, heads up.
Talk it through. Paperwork and a straight face.
Go round. Ditches, fields, the long way.

take_through.text:
The story is that it is a hired hand, deaf, and being taken to family, and it holds because it is told by somebody who is bored of telling it and because the Naguka {says nothing at all|is silent|does not open its mouth} for the whole two minutes.
On the far side it takes {leader}'s sleeve and does not let go for a hundred metres. At the next town it is claimed by somebody from the horde within a day, and the word goes back down the line about who brought it.

take_round.text:
It is {four kilometres|a long loop|two hours} of ditch, field and one fence, in the dark, with something that does not see well and will not be carried.
It arrives filthy and entirely delighted. The route gets used again, by other people, within the month, and nobody ever writes down whose route it was.

take_held.text:
It is held at the checkpoint for {four hours|an afternoon|most of a day} while somebody rings somebody, and the party is held with it, which is the only reason the four hours stay four hours.
It is released to the party at dusk with a form and a condition: out of the district by morning. That is done. Something about it, though, does not talk for the rest of the walk.

hand_m.text:
The barracks are {four hundred metres|up the road|across the square} and the sergeant on the desk has signed for {two|three} of these this season already.
He says so. He also says, without being asked and without looking up, that none of them went where the form says they went, and that he writes the form anyway because the form is what he has.

choices.text: Hand it in. It is the lawful thing.
Ask him, straight out, where they actually go.
Take it back out of the barracks and walk it north.

hand_where.text:
He tells it in {four sentences|the fewest words available|one go}, looking at the desk, and then asks the party to leave, and then asks them not to come back through this town for a while.
Where they go is not far and is not a barracks and is not on any form. Knowing it is worth something to the horde, and it will be worth a great deal more to somebody else in about a year.

qe_ttd.title: {Tinfoil|The Idea Going Round|Everybody Had It At Once}

n0.text:
Half of {place} is wearing hats and the other half is laughing at them, and the half wearing hats have a point.
There is a thought going round: the same {rumour}, arriving in the same words, in people who have not spoken to each other. {stranger} keeps a list of who has had it and the list is the wrong shape for gossip.
The hats are not all foil. {Two|Three} of them are older than that and are made properly, by somebody who has done this before.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.disciplined: {member} {follows standard breach protocol by the book|clears every corner with military precision|keeps a steady firing stance and monitors the sensors|checks the ammo count and maintains position}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Dam it. Foil for everybody, {qty} {material} worth.
Find patient zero on the list.
Sit with it and see what it wants.

dam.text:
It looks ridiculous and it works, which is the whole history of the countermeasure in one sentence.
Inside two days the list stops growing. Nobody in {place} will ever be able to say whether it would have stopped anyway, and everybody {keeps the hat|keeps wearing the hat|hangs on to the hat}.

zero.text:
The list sorted by hour comes to a point, and the point is a man who has not left his house in {timeAgo} and did not think the thought either.
He received it. There is a difference and he is the only person in {place} who understands it, and he has been waiting for somebody to {come and ask|ask|turn up and ask}.

want.text:
Sat with properly, it is not a message. It is a shape, and the shape is trying to be held by enough people at once to become a thing.
{leader} does not let it, which is harder than it sounds and takes until the small hours, and the shape goes {looking elsewhere|somewhere else|off to be held by somebody else}.

caught.text:
Everybody in the party has it by the evening, in the same words, arriving at the same time.
It takes {few} days and a great deal of foil to get it back out, and for a while afterwards nobody trusts an idea they {had on their own|arrived at alone|came up with}.

dam_m.text:
Foil for everybody looks ridiculous and works, which is the whole history of the countermeasure in one sentence, and it takes {an afternoon|half a day|two hours and a lot of arguing} to hand out.
The people with the proper hats will not take the foil. They also will not say where the proper hats came from, and one of them asks the party, quietly, whether they have started {dreaming about the same room|having the same dream|hearing it in the dream too}.

choices.text: Finish the distribution. Ignore the question.
Answer honestly and ask where the good hats come from.
Sleep in {place} tonight and find out.

dam_hats.text:
They come from {a woman two villages over|an old man on the coast|somebody in the next valley} who has made them since before anybody in this town was born, and who makes about {four|five} a year, and who has never explained the pattern to anybody.
The pattern is not a pattern. It is writing, very small, all the way round the inside, and the party is shown it and permitted to copy it, which has happened {twice|once|three times} before in fifty years.

dam_dream.text:
It is a room, and it is the same room, and everybody in the party is in it at the same time, which none of them mention at breakfast until somebody describes the wallpaper.
The thought does not arrive in words this time. It arrives as {an instruction|a preference|a direction}, and it is about the well behind the chapel, and by the time anybody is properly awake two of the party are already dressed.

zero_m.text:
The list sorted by hour comes to a point, and the point is a man who has not left his house in {timeAgo} and did not think the thought either.
He received it. There is a difference, and he is the only person in {place} who knows there is a difference, and he has been waiting for somebody to knock on his door about it for {four days|nearly a week|the whole of this}.

choices.text: Sit down and let him explain.
Find out what he was doing at the hour it arrived.
Get him out of {place} tonight.

zero_set.text:
He was doing what he does every evening, which is listening to a set he built himself in {1974|the seventies|a long time ago} on a band nobody uses.
The set is still on the table. It is still receiving. What it is receiving is {a shape|not speech|the thing, unfolded}, and now that four other people have heard it, it is no longer only his problem, which he says is the best news he has had all year.

zero_out.text:
Getting somebody who has not been outdoors in {timeAgo} into a vehicle takes {two hours|most of the evening|longer than the drive}, and the first {four hundred metres|hundred metres|part} of the journey are very bad for him.
The thought stops spreading in {place} within a day of him leaving it, which is either a cure or a coincidence and will never be distinguishable. He does not go back. He does, eventually, thank the party, by letter.

qe_wellhead.title: {The Wellhead|Where The Line Comes Up|Oil And Blood}

n0.text:
There is a capped wellhead in the field beyond {place} with {sign} rusted off it, and everything green for {few} metres around it is growing the wrong way round.
The line comes up here. {stranger} has been paid by somebody to sit and watch it and has never been told what for, and has worked most of it out anyway.
The grass is growing the wrong way round in {a perfect circle|a circle|a ring}, and the circle is not centred on the wellhead.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Reseal it properly with {qty} {material}.
Open it.
Read the ground and find where the line actually runs.

seal.text:
The cap goes back on right this time, gasketed, with the {material} doing the work the original contractor was paid for and did not do.
The grass round it will take a season to remember which way up it goes. The cheques keep coming to the watcher, who is now watching a wellhead that is actually sealed, and says so, and pays {a share|a share of it|the party a share}.

open.text: What comes up is not {oil|oil at all|what the cap was for}, or is oil {in the way that a person is meat|the way a body is chemistry|only in the sense that it came out of the ground}.

line.text:
Doesn't run where the survey says. It runs under {place} itself, under the school and the market and the road, which is why everything in that town has always felt like it is about to happen.
What that map is worth depends entirely on who is shown it, and the party is holding the only {copy|copy there is|copy anybody has}.

linef.text:
The ground says four different things in four different places and none of them agree, which is what leylines do to anybody without the training.
{leader} comes away with a headache that lasts into the next day and a very clear sense of having been {read back|read in return|looked at by the ground}.

seal_m.text:
The cap goes back on right this time, gasketed, with the {material} doing the work the original contractor was paid for and did not do.
Bolting it down, it becomes obvious the flange is drilled for {twelve|sixteen} bolts and has only ever had eight in it, and the four that are missing are missing in a pattern, on the side the circle of grass is centred on.

choices.text: Eight bolts held it before. Finish and take the cheque.
Drill and fit the missing four properly.
Find out why somebody left four bolts out on purpose.

seal_bolts.text:
Four holes drilled through old flange steel in a wet field takes {the rest of the day|hours|a long afternoon} and the last one is done by lamp.
Sixteen bolts, torqued in sequence. The circle of grass starts straightening out within {a fortnight|the month|weeks}, which nobody predicted and which is reported in a letter the party never sees to an office that does not answer it.

seal_shear.text:
The third hole goes through into something that is not the annulus, and what comes back up the drill is {warm|under pressure|moving}, and the drill has to be left in the hole to plug it.
The cap is finished with eight bolts and a drill bit. The cheque clears. The circle of grass is {four metres wider|larger|noticeably bigger} by the spring.

seal_why.text:
Because the four bolts would have closed it, and the contractor was paid to leave it {breathing|open a crack|able to vent}, and the payment came from somebody who was not the company.
That is worth knowing and is worth more written down. The party seals it properly anyway, which takes the rest of the day, and posts the rest of it to {two|three} places at once so that it cannot be lost.

open_m.text:
The cap comes off in {four minutes|no time|less time than sealing it would take} and the smell arrives before anything else does: not oil, or oil {in the way that a person is meat|the way a body is chemistry|only in the sense that it came out of the ground}.
What is in the shaft is not coming up yet. It is aware that the cap is off, which is a different thing, and there is a short interval in which the cap could go back on.

choices.text: Stand our ground. Whatever comes up, comes up.
Cap it again, now, and weight it.
Put a light down the shaft and see what is on the walls.

open_recap.text:
The cap goes back on in {ninety seconds|under two minutes|a great hurry} with four people on it and everything heavy in the field piled on top, which is not a seal and is a great deal better than nothing.
It holds. {stranger} stops taking the money from whoever was paying them and starts taking it from the party instead, which is a smaller amount and a considerably better arrangement for everybody.

open_shaft.text:
A lamp on a line, down {forty metres|a long way|as far as the line goes}, and the walls of the shaft are not lined with anything anybody put there.
They are worked. Cut, by hand, in a pattern that goes all the way down, and it is old, and the wellhead was drilled through it {forty years ago|in the fifties|at some point} by people who plainly decided not to write that down.

qe_grimoire.title: {The Shelf It Was Left On|Bad Spelling|Do Not Leave It Beside Anything}

n0.text:
A house clearance at {place}, and {stranger} standing in the doorway not going back in, holding the door with a boot.
On the shelf inside there is a book with a formula in it written with the words apart, and it has been on that shelf beside other books for {timeAgo}.
The boot in the door is there because the door has closed on its own {twice|more than once|three times} already this morning.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.disciplined: {member} {follows standard breach protocol by the book|clears every corner with military precision|keeps a steady firing stance and monitors the sensors|checks the ammo count and maintains position}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Burn the shelf, the lot of it.
Sort the clean ones out of it.
Take the whole shelf to somebody who wants it.

burn2.text:
The whole shelf goes into the yard and goes up, and it takes longer than paper should and makes a noise about it.
{stranger} watches the entire burn from the gate and does not go back into the house until the ash is cold, and then pays the party in cash out of {a tin|a biscuit tin|the tin on the mantelpiece}.

sort.text:
Working from the far end inward, ahead of the spread, {few} volumes come off clean and one of them is not a grimoire at all: it is somebody's working notebook, and it is better than the grimoire ever was.
The rest goes on the fire and it is {a considerable fire|a fire the whole street comes out for|a bigger fire than the shelf accounts for}.

sp2.text:
It has been on that shelf {a long time|years|longer than anybody said} and it has been busy.
The formula is in the party's own pack before anybody checks, and everything written down in there has to come out and go on the fire, including {the map|the map, which hurts|two months of the map}.

sell.text:
There is always somebody who wants a shelf like that and never any difficulty finding them, which is the thing about people who want shelves like that.
The money is {good|better than good|more than the job was worth}. The buyer is delighted. Nobody involved has done anything that will look {well written down later|well in writing afterwards|good in anybody's account of it}.

burn2_m.text:
Getting the shelf out of the house means going into the house, and the whole shelf comes out in {four|three} armfuls with everybody holding their breath in a way nobody is prepared to justify.
On the last armful the book with the words apart is not in the stack. It is on the kitchen table, {open|face up|at the same page}, in a room nobody has been into.

choices.text: Put it on the pile. Burn the lot.
Do it properly. Salt, order, the words said over it.
Leave the house. Burn the house.

burn2_rite.text:
It takes {an hour|the best part of an hour|longer than the burning does} and most of it is spent standing still in a kitchen saying the same four lines in the correct order.
The book goes on the fire like a book. {stranger} goes back into the house before the ash is cold, which they have not been able to do in {a fortnight|three weeks|some time}, and the clearance is finished by Thursday.

burn2_wild.text:
The words are said in a kitchen by somebody who has read about it, which is not the same as having done it, and about halfway through the room {gets very cold|goes quiet in a specific way|stops having a draught}.
The shelf burns. So does the back of the house, eventually, which everybody agrees afterwards was probably necessary and definitely not what was planned.

burn2_house.text:
It is not a decision anybody makes out loud. It is a look, and then a conversation with {stranger} at the gate that lasts {forty minutes|most of an hour|longer than the fire does}, and then an insurance question that resolves itself surprisingly cleanly.
The house goes. The shelf goes with it. Nothing from inside ever turns up in a market anywhere, which is not true of any of the other options.

sell_m.text:
There is always somebody who wants a shelf like that and never any difficulty finding them, which is the thing about people who want shelves like that.
The one who comes is {polite|extremely polite|well dressed and unhurried}, pays in cash, counts it twice, and asks, as an afterthought, whether the party would be willing to say where it came from and who lived there.

choices.text: Take the money. Say nothing about the house.
Tell them. It is only an address.
Find out who they are buying for first.

sell_addr.text:
It is only an address, and it is given, and the money is a little better for it.
{stranger} has people at that house for the rest of the month: at the gate, at the door, {twice|three times|on more than one occasion} in the garden after dark, and none of them will say who sent them, and all of them know exactly which shelf it was.

sell_who.text:
It takes {three questions|two questions and a silence|one badly answered question} to establish that the buyer is not a collector, is not Guild, and is buying to complete a set that is {one volume short|missing one|nearly whole}.
That is worth knowing and worth selling on. The shelf goes for the asking price. What the party knows about the set goes, {a week later|some days later|shortly afterwards}, to the Guild, for considerably more.

n0.text:
{stranger} at {bar} in {place} has an old handset on the table, the indestructible kind, and it has rung twice this evening with no network anywhere near it.
Nobody has answered it. That is a house rule now, arrived at democratically, and the second ring emptied the far corner of the room.
The house rule has a second half nobody mentions until the party asks: it also does not get taken out of {bar}.

asides.brave: {member} {steps up front with a weapon ready: "I'll take point."|grins and racks the slide: "Let's see what wants to die today."|is already at the hatch before anyone can argue|steps over the threshold without flinching}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Answer it.
Buy it off them.
Get it retuned properly, {qty} {material} of parts.

ansr.text:
It is somebody's grandmother, and she died in {timeAgo}, and she is not confused about that at all and would like the party to pass something on.
What she passes on takes ninety seconds, is entirely practical, and settles an argument in a family in {place} that has been running since before {anybody in the room was born|the war|any of them were born}.

bad.text:
Something answers that is enjoying being answered.
It asks {leader} a question by name, waits, and hangs up first, which is the part that {stays with everybody|nobody gets over|is still there in the morning}.

buy2.text:
The whole {bar} watches the money change hands and the whole {bar} is visibly relieved, and somebody stands the party a round on the strength of it.
It is a talisman as much as a phone: near it, a loop sits still and a fracture stays shut, and it rings when it wants to.

tune.text:
Retuned it stops ringing at random and starts ringing on purpose, which is either better or worse depending on the week.
{bar} keeps it on a hook behind the taps and treats it like a fire extinguisher, and the party drinks there free for as long as {the place stands|the doors are open|there is a bar there}.

buy_m.text:
The whole {bar} watches the money come out and the whole {bar} is visibly relieved, and then somebody at the end of the taps says, into their glass, that the last person to buy it brought it back inside {a week|nine days|the fortnight}.
They brought it back, is the phrasing. Not returned it. There is a difference and everybody in the room is letting it sit there.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Ask what happened to them. Go on.|Nobody is finishing that sentence.|We are buying a problem with a handle on it.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts their glass down|turns round on the stool to face the room|asks the barman a question with their eyebrows}

choices.text: Buy it anyway.
Ask the room what happened to the last buyer.
Buy it and leave it on the hook. Ours, but it stays here.

buy_last.text:
It comes out slowly and in the wrong order, the way a room tells a thing it has agreed not to tell: a name, a fortnight, a van found at {the coast|the reservoir|a place that is not on the way to anywhere}.
And the detail that matters, which is that it stopped ringing at random for them and started ringing at the same time every night. The party buys it knowing that, which is the only sensible way to buy it.

buy_hook.text:
Bought, paid for, and hung straight back on its hook behind the taps with the party's name against it in the cellar book.
It rings {twice|three times|more than once} a week for the next year, and {bar} answers it, and takes messages, and posts them on. Some of the messages are for the party. All of them arrive.

tune_m.text:
Retuning it takes {qty} {material}, a bench, and the better part of an evening with the whole {bar} pretending not to watch.
Halfway through it becomes clear the handset was retuned once before, badly, and that underneath the bad tuning there is an original one, factory, {still live|intact|perfectly good}, pointing at something that is not the exchange.

choices.text: Tune it to the exchange properly and be done.
Restore the factory tuning and see what it points at.
Pull the tuning stage out entirely. Make it a phone and nothing else.

tune_fact.text:
Factory tuning restored, the handset does not ring. It listens, which is a different posture entirely and is obvious within a minute of watching the meter.
What it is listening to is {a long way off|not nearby|somewhere with a lot of space around it} and is broadcasting a list, slowly, on a loop, and one of the things on the list is a road the party has driven.

tune_dead.text:
The tuning stage comes out and goes in the bin, and after that it is a handset with a wire and nothing else, and it never rings again.
{bar} is {relieved|delighted|quietly grateful} and says so with a tab that stays open for longer than the party is in town. Nobody in the room mentions that the list of things it might have said is now permanently unavailable.

qe_flood.title: {Sandbags|The Water Is Coming Up Through The Floor|By Morning}

n0.text:
The water is coming up through the floors on {street} in {place}, not down from the rain but up, and it has been rising since first light.
There are {many} houses on that row and about a third as many people to do anything about it. {stranger} is filling bags off the pile with the wrong shovel and will not stop long enough to be given a better one.
Somebody's chest freezer has come up through a kitchen floor at the low end and is going round in the current like a boat with nowhere to be.

asides.nurturing: {member} has taken one end of a bag before anybody agrees anything.
asides.calm: {member} sends the first four people they can find to the top of the row instead of the bottom, and is right.
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Bags, all night.
Give {qty} {material} to plug it at the source.
Get the people out and let the houses go.

held.text:
The row holds. It holds at about {four|half three|five} in the morning, and the last bag goes on at a point where nobody has anything left, and then it holds.
In the light everybody sits down in the mud at the same time. Somebody's mother goes down the row with tea and does not accept {any refusals|a single refusal|no for an answer}.

lost2.text:
It goes at the low end at about three and takes {few} houses with it, and the rest of the night is carrying furniture upstairs in the dark.
Nobody blames anybody. Everybody looks like they might, for a while, which is {worse|the harder part|worse than being blamed}.

src.text:
It's not the river. It is a culvert somebody built over {timeAgo} and nobody has looked at since, and the {material} plugs the mouth of it in an hour and a half by lamplight.
The water stops rising while people are still filling bags, and it takes the row {twenty minutes|the best part of an hour|a while} to believe it.

evac.text:
Everybody out, {up the hill|onto the high road|to the church, which is the high ground}, with what they can carry and the animals loose behind them.
The row goes. Nobody drowns, which was the actual question all along, and there is a difference between those two facts that takes people {a few weeks|the winter|months} to feel.

src_m.text:
It is not the river. It is a culvert somebody built over {timeAgo} and nobody has looked at since, and its mouth is under {two metres|the best part of two metres|a good depth} of moving water at the low end of the row.
Plugging it means going down to it. The {material} is in the pack and the lamps are on the bank and everybody is now looking at whoever in the party is the strongest swimmer.

choices.text: Plug it from the bank with poles and hope.
Go down and do it by hand.
Blow the far end open instead and let it drain the other way.

src_dive.text:
Three dives by lamplight into water that is {going somewhere|moving hard|pulling}, with a line on the waist and somebody counting on the bank each time.
The mouth takes the plug on the third. The water stops rising while people are still filling bags with it, and the row is dry by morning, and nobody on that street ever pays for a drink in the party's company again.

src_caught.text:
The second dive goes in slightly wrong and the culvert mouth is exactly as interested in a person as it is in a street's worth of water.
The line holds. The party on the bank get {leader} back up in {nine seconds|under a minute|a very long fifteen seconds} and the plug goes in from the bank with poles like it should have from the start. The row holds. Nobody sleeps.

src_blow.text:
The far end of the culvert comes out under {a car park|the old yard|a wall nobody owns}, and opening it is a matter of {a small charge|one charge|very little, correctly placed}.
It goes at {two in the morning|half two|some hour} with a noise the whole town hears and a fountain nobody expected, and after that the water has somewhere to be that is not anybody's kitchen. The council spends {four months|a season|the rest of the year} arguing about who to bill.

evac_m.text:
Everybody out, {up the hill|onto the high road|to the church, which is the high ground}, with what they can carry and the animals loose behind them.
At the top of the road, counting heads against a list somebody has made on the back of an envelope, the count comes up {one short|short by one|one down}, and the name it is short by lives at the low end.

choices.text: Go back down for them.
Get on a roof and find out where they are first.
Nobody goes back down. That is the rule.

evac_back.text:
The low end is chest deep and moving, and the door is shut, and the door opens inward, which in {two metres|a depth like that|water like that} means it does not open.
The window goes in. They are upstairs, on a bed, with a cat and a biscuit tin, and entirely furious about being carried. All three come out. The cat objects for the whole of the following week.

evac_spot.text:
From the church roof with a lamp it takes {four minutes|two sweeps|no time} to find the upstairs window with somebody waving a tea towel out of it.
That is the difference between a rescue and a search: three people go to one house instead of eleven people going to eleven, and everybody is on the high road by {two|half one|an hour nobody remembers}.

n0.text:
There is a borehole in the ground near {place}, capped, and the cap has been redone {few} times by different hands over the years, each one heavier than the last.
{stranger} is minding it out of a hut with a flask and no particular authority, and is not facing outward.
Each cap has a date stamped in it and the gaps between the dates are getting {shorter|smaller|noticeably shorter}.

asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Reweld it, {qty} {material} of rod.
Listen at it.
Take the watch for a night so somebody can sleep.

weld.text:
The fifth cap goes on over the fourth and it is {the best of them|better than the four under it|the first one done by somebody who wanted it to hold}, done properly, with the rod the party carried in.
The minder watches every pass of it and afterwards sits down for the first time in the conversation. Whatever is down there is a good deal further away than it was {this morning|at breakfast|when the party walked up}.

lis.text:
There is a sound at the cap and it is not {water|rock} and it is not settling. It is a long way down and it is regular, and it is getting to the top of the shaft slightly faster than it did on the previous measurement.
Somebody at a desk somewhere has that measurement in a file and has decided not to be the person who says it {out loud|first|at all}.

lisf.text:
Whatever is down there hears the listening.
It stops, all at once, for as long as the ear is on the plate, and starts again the moment it comes off, and {leader} does not sleep well for {a while|some nights|the rest of the season}.

watch.text:
A night in a hut with a flask and a chair facing the wrong way, listening to nothing for {eleven|nine|ten} hours.
The minder sleeps for the first time in a fortnight, in a bed, in a house, and comes back at dawn with breakfast for everybody and an old story that is not in {any archive|any file anywhere|the record}.

weld_m.text:
The fifth cap goes on over the fourth and the rod the party carried in is good rod, and the job is {two hours|an afternoon|most of the light} of kneeling on a steel plate in {weather}.
Half way round the run, the plate under the knees {moves|gives slightly|answers}, once, in a way that has nothing to do with anybody's weight on it.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{That was not settling.|Five caps. Five. Ask yourself why.|We are welding a lid, not a hole.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts a hand flat on the plate and keeps it there|looks at the minder, who is looking at the hut|carries on holding the rod}

choices.text: Finish the weld and do not mention it.
Weld it, and add a strongback across the whole cap.
Stop welding. Get the plate off and look.

weld_back.text:
A strongback is {two lengths|a cross|four pieces} of the heaviest section in the pack, welded across the cap and out onto the collar, which turns a lid into a structure.
It is over-engineered and everybody knows it and nobody says so. The minder puts the flask down for the first time all day, and the party is paid out of a tin that was clearly being kept for something.

weld_crack.text:
A strongback welded onto cold plate in {weather} puts the stress where the stress was not, and the cap cracks along the fourth weld while everybody is watching it cool.
It is {a hairline|four inches|a crack you could lose a coin in}. It is re-welded by morning by the minder alone, badly, and the sixth cap goes on the following spring, which is sooner than any of the others.

watch_m.text:
A night in a hut with a flask and a chair facing the wrong way, and the minder asleep in a bed in a house for the first time in {a fortnight|three weeks|some time}.
At about {two|half one|the dead hour} the sound at the cap changes: it does the regular thing, and then it does the regular thing {twice as fast|out of step|with an extra beat in it}, and then it goes back.

choices.text: Note the hour in the book and keep sitting.
Time it properly for the rest of the night.
Go and wake the minder.

watch_time.text:
Six hours with a watch and a pencil produces {four pages|a column|a page} of figures, and the figures are not random: there is a pattern, and the pattern has a period, and the period is {eleven days|a fortnight|nine days} long.
The minder's book goes back {forty years|decades|a very long way}. Laid against it, the party's six hours turn the whole archive from a superstition into a dataset, and somebody will pay for that.

watch_wake.text:
Waking somebody who has not slept in a fortnight to tell them a noise did something slightly unusual is {a decision|a call|a thing you only do once}, and it is made, and they come out in a coat over nothing at {two in the morning|the dead hour|whatever time it is}.
They listen for nine minutes. They say: yes. Then they go and sit in the hut and do not go back to bed, and the party has taken the only night off that minder was going to get this year.

qe_hauler.title: {Under Eighty All The Way|The Load That Cannot Stop|Relief Driver}

n0.text:
A hauler is stopped on the hard shoulder outside {place} with the hazards going and {stranger} asleep against the wheel in the way of somebody who has fought it and lost.
The load has to be somewhere by first light and the route has {few} marked bubbles on it, and neither of those facts is going to negotiate.
The load is sheeted and roped and the ropes are {new|newer than the sheet|not the same ropes that left the depot}.

asides.loyal: {member} {positions themselves between {leader} and the door|nods firmly: "Right behind you, boss."|keeps a watchful eye on {leader}'s blind spot|stands ready to back up whatever call is made}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Drive it. Relief for the last leg.
Sit in the cab and keep them talking to the depot.
Not the party's load and not the party's licence.

drv.text:
It is {distance}, holding a heavy thing under eighty past marked ground with somebody asleep in the bunk behind, and it is the most concentrated three hours anybody has spent this month.
The depot signs for it on the hour, exactly. The Society pays relief rates, and relief rates are not what anybody expects.

drf.text:
The speedo gets away on a downgrade for about {four|three|five} seconds and four seconds is plenty.
Correcting it costs the load a pallet and the party's nerves the rest of the day, and the depot is late, and the sign-off happens anyway with everybody being {very polite about it|extremely polite|careful about it}.

talk.text:
{Four|Five|Three} hours in a cab with a flask, keeping somebody awake by making them describe every depot between here and the coast.
By the end there is a name for every stop on that route, which of them will let you sleep in the yard, and which of them owes the Society a favour that can be {signed over|called in|passed on}.

no.text:
The hazards are still going in the mirror {a long way down the road|most of the way to the next junction|for longer than anybody watches}.
Whether they made it is a thing the party never finds out, which is the ordinary condition of most of the good one might have done.

drv_m.text:
The cab is warm, the seat is somebody else's shape, and the gearbox has {a third|a second|one gear} that needs asking twice.
Thirty kilometres in, the load shifts. Not much: {a hand's width|an inch|enough to feel through the wheel}, on a bend, in a way that a sheeted and roped load has no business doing.

choices.text: Keep going. It will hold to the depot.
Pull in and re-rope the whole thing.
Pull in and look under the sheet.

drv_rope.text:
Forty minutes in a layby in {weather} with the hazards going, doing a job properly that somebody did badly in a hurry at {four in the morning|the start of the shift|a depot two hundred kilometres back}.
The load does not move again. The depot signs for it on the hour and the sign-off has the party's name on it, and that name goes on a list of people the depot rings first.

drv_sheet.text:
Under the sheet the load is {four|five} pallets of something legitimate and one that is not on the manifest, and the one that is not is where the movement is coming from, and it is moving because there is {something|an animal|weight} alive in it.
The rest of the drive is done at the speed limit with the radio off. What is in the pallet is somebody else's business right up until the depot, at which point it very rapidly becomes several people's.

no_m.text:
The hazards are still going in the mirror {a long way down the road|most of the way to the next junction|for longer than anybody watches}.
At the next junction there is a phone box that works, and a depot number painted on the back of every hauler on this road, including that one, {legible from here|readable in the mirror|big enough to have read}.

choices.text: Drive on.
Ring the depot from the box.
Ring the depot, then go back and sit with them.

no_ring.text:
It takes {four minutes|two minutes|one coin} and a night clerk who is awake and unsurprised and already reaching for a different phone.
Relief is on the road inside the hour. The party never finds out the driver's name, and the party's own description goes into the depot's book against the words {"phoned it in"|"called it"|"rang from the junction"}, which is worth more on that road than most things.

no_back.text:
Ringing it in takes four minutes. Going back takes {twenty|fifteen}, and sitting in a cold cab with somebody who is too tired to be embarrassed takes the rest of the night.
By the time relief arrives the party knows every depot between here and the coast, which of them will let you sleep, and why {stranger} has been driving on no sleep for three days, and that last one is a story that goes somewhere.

qe_saint.title: {The Reliquary|{saint} Is Missing A Hand|Feast Day Is Thursday}

n0.text:
The reliquary at {place} is open and light and the wrong weight, and the feast is on Thursday.
{stranger} has told nobody yet and is standing in the sacristy working out whether telling nobody is a sin on its own. The lock was not forced. That is the part that has taken the colour out of their face.
The seal on the reliquary was lifted with {something thin|a blade|a paper knife} and put back, and it has been put back very slightly crooked.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Find it before Thursday.
Make a replacement nobody will question.
Tell them to announce it from the altar.

fnd2.text:
It has not left {the building|the sacristy|the parish}. It is in a drawer in a room that is used by one person, wrapped in a cloth, with a note that is halfway to being a confession and does not get finished.
It goes back on the velvet before Thursday. Nobody is named. The party is asked for nothing and given {a great deal|more than they came with|everything the parish can spare}.

nof2.text:
Thursday comes and the reliquary is carried round the square at the correct pace by {six|eight} men who do not know what they are carrying.
It is a good feast. Everybody says so. The sacristan does not {eat|eat a thing|touch anything}.

fake.text:
It takes an evening and {qty} {material} and a great deal of care about the colour, and on the velvet under glass at three paces it is beyond question.
The procession goes round the square and the town gets its Thursday. What the party is left holding is the knowledge, which is heavier than the relic was.

tell.text:
It is announced from the altar on the Sunday, plainly, without an excuse attached, and the square goes very quiet and then does not fall apart.
By Thursday somebody has left it in the porch overnight in {a shoebox|a biscuit tin|a bag with a shop's name on it}, which is how these things have {always actually been resolved|generally been resolved|been settled since anybody can remember}.

fake_m.text:
It takes an evening and {qty} {material} and a great deal of care about the colour, and on the velvet under glass at three paces it is beyond question.
At one pace it is not, and the sacristan knows that, and asks the only question that matters in a voice that has stopped pretending: does the party intend to tell anybody, ever.

choices.text: No. Nobody. It stays between the three of us.
Yes. After the feast. It gets written down.
Make the copy good at one pace, not three.

fake_record.text:
The procession goes round the square, the town gets its Thursday, and on the Friday a letter goes to the diocese with {four names|everybody's name|all of it} on it and the copy is surrendered with it.
It is the worst possible outcome for everybody's comfort and the best available one for the record, and the diocese, after {two years|a long correspondence|eighteen months}, says so in writing.

fake_perfect.text:
Done properly it is {three evenings|the rest of the week|a great deal longer}, with the right materials fetched from {two towns|a long way|somewhere that asks no questions} and the ageing done by hand.
At one pace it is beyond question. At one pace with a glass it is beyond question. The sacristan handles it for the procession and does not shake, and the party is paid out of the parish's own money with the churchwarden present and cheerful.

fake_caught.text:
It is good at three paces and at one pace it is a piece of {material} with paint on it, and the bishop's man, who was not expected, {picks it up|handles it|turns it over} on the Wednesday.
The feast happens. So does everything after the feast, which involves the sacristan, the party, a room in the presbytery, and a conversation that lasts {four hours|most of a day|until it gets dark}.

tell_m.text:
It is announced from the altar on the Sunday, plainly, without an excuse attached, and the square goes very quiet and then does not fall apart.
What happens next is that {four|five|a good many} people come to the sacristy over the following days to say something, and by Tuesday it is clear that two of them are saying the same thing about the same person and neither knows the other has come.

choices.text: Wait. It will come back on its own.
Put the two accounts together and go and see the person.
Give both names to the sacristan and stay out of it.

tell_person.text:
They are {eighty|very old|not well} and they took it because they were frightened of Thursday, which turns out to be a whole story of its own going back {sixty years|a very long way|to before the war}.
It comes back on the Wednesday in the party's own hands with nobody else told. The sacristan's note, the half-confession that was never finished, goes on the fire in the sacristy grate with both of them watching.

tell_hand.text:
Two names on a piece of paper handed over at the sacristy door, and then the party goes, which is defensible and is not comfortable.
It is dealt with {parochially|inside the parish|quietly}. The reliquary is on the altar by Thursday. Somebody in that town does not come to Mass again, and the party never finds out which of the two names it was.

qe_fence.title: {The Back Room|No Questions On Either Side|What Is In The Crate}

n0.text:
{fence} works out of a back room off {street} and has a crate that came in {timeAgo} that nobody has come to collect.
The arrangement on offer is the usual: the party moves it as far as {distance} and asks nothing, and is paid in {payment}. The crate is heavier at one end.
The crate has been moved {twice|more than once|three times} inside the back room, and the marks on the floor say it was moved by somebody in a hurry each time.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}

Open it first.
Buy it outright and it is nobody's business but the party's.

job.text:
{distance}, delivered, signed for by somebody who does not give a name and does not need to.
The money is good and the walk back is the first time all week nobody has had to think about anything, and neither of those facts survives contact with what is in {rumour} a fortnight later.

opn.text:
Opened and re-nailed so that nobody could tell, which is a skill, and what is in it is worse than the money and better than the party feared.
Knowing changes the price. {fence} pays the new price without arguing, which says everything about what {fence} already knew.

opf.text:
The lid splinters at the corner and there is no putting that right with the tools to hand.
{fence} looks at the corner for a long moment and then says the job is off and the party should go, in a voice that has {nothing behind it at all|nothing in it|no weather in it whatsoever}.

own.text:
Bought, carried out through the front {for once|in daylight|without anybody ducking}, and opened on the party's own ground in the party's own time with nobody standing over it.
What is inside was worth considerably more than the asking price, which is what happens when a thing is priced by how badly somebody {wants it gone|needs it out of the room|wants rid}.

job_m.text:
The job is {distance} with a crate that is heavier at one end and does not like corners, and the first hour of it is entirely uneventful.
In the second hour it becomes clear the party is being followed, at a distance, by {two|a pair|somebody and a second somebody} who are not trying particularly hard to be invisible about it.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Nobody follows a crate they do not know the contents of.|That is not a tail, that is an escort.|Those two knew the route before we did.}"
asides.any: {member} {changes the grip on the crate and does not look back again|counts the corners|takes the outside of the pavement}

choices.text: Deliver it and let them follow.
Lose them in the streets.
Put the crate down and wait for them.

job_lose.text:
It takes {four turns|three streets and a yard|a covered market and two alleys} and one of them is a mistake, and the mistake is what actually does it.
The crate arrives. It is signed for by somebody with no name who looks past the party up the street for {a good while|longer than is comfortable|some time} before closing the door, and the money is doubled without a word about why.

job_caught.text:
The third turn is into a yard with one way out of it and the two are already standing in it, which means they knew the route, which means {fence} sold it or somebody in that back room did.
The crate stays in the yard. The party does not, which is the good outcome available, and it is available because the two want the crate rather than a fight.

job_wait.text:
Putting a crate down in the middle of a street and sitting on it is not something either of the two have any procedure for, and it shows: they stop about {forty metres|a street's length|thirty paces} off and have a conversation with their hands.
One of them walks over. What they want is not the crate; it is to know who sent it, and they are willing to pay considerably more than {fence} is for the answer.

choices.text: Sell them the name.
Say nothing. Pick the crate up. Finish the job.

job_sell.text:
The name is worth {payment} and is handed over on a street corner in about {nine seconds|a moment|the time it takes to say it}.
The crate gets delivered anyway, because the job is the job. {fence} works out what happened inside {a week|ten days|the month}, and the back room off {street} is not somewhere the party can walk into again.

own_m.text:
Bought, carried out through the front {for once|in daylight|without anybody ducking}, and set down on the party's own ground with nobody standing over it.
It is nailed shut with {nine|eleven} nails where four would do, and there is a second lid under the first, and between the two lids there is a folded sheet of paper with a date on it {four days from now|next week|in the near future}.

choices.text: Open it anyway. It is ours now.
Read the paper first and do what it says.
Wait for the date.

own_paper.text:
It is instructions, in three languages, and the third one is not a language anybody in the party has seen written down before. What the two readable ones say is: not before the date, and not indoors.
Done outdoors, on the date, at the hour, it opens correctly, and what is inside is intact and worth {a very great deal|considerably more than the purchase price|the whole season}.

own_wait.text:
Four days of a crate sitting in the corner of wherever the party is sleeping, which is four days of everybody walking round it.
On the date it opens on its own at about {four in the morning|first light|an hour nobody chose}, both lids at once, quietly, and what is in it has arranged itself since the nails went in.

qe_dig.title: {The Contractor's Deadline|Bones Under The Foundation|Pour It Monday}

n0.text:
A site at {place} with the foundation dug and the pour booked for Monday, and something in the trench that stopped the machine on Friday.
{stranger} is the one who has to decide, and has been standing at the edge of the trench since. There is a carving on what is down there and it is older than the town.
The machine driver has not come back to the site since Friday and is not answering, and nobody wants to be the one to say that out loud.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Work it out properly. Two days, unpaid.
Shore it and pour around it, {qty} {material}.
Nothing was ever found here.

arch.text:
Two days on hands and knees and it is a boundary stone, in place, still doing its job, marking a line that every wall in {place} has quietly respected for eight hundred years without anybody knowing why.
That is a paper, and the paper has the party's names on it, and the Foundation pays for {papers|papers like that|a paper}.

archf.text:
Two days, and at the end of it the honest answer is that nobody in this trench is qualified to say what it is.
Monday arrives regardless. The pour happens. Whatever it was is under {a hundred|ninety|a hundred and twenty} cubic metres of concrete and will be somebody's problem in {the next century|a hundred years|whichever century digs it up}.

shore.text:
Shuttering, a void former, and the {material} to hold it: the pour goes ahead on Monday and the thing in the trench keeps a room to itself under the new floor.
It costs the contractor a weekend and it costs nobody the deadline, and there is a hatch, and the hatch is on {the drawings|the drawings, in ink|every set of the drawings}.

pour.text:
The machine goes back in on the Saturday and by Sunday night there is nothing in that trench but trench.
The pour goes ahead. {stranger} pays cash and does not shake anybody's hand, and the building goes up straight and stays up, which is not {the point|the point at all|what anybody was asking}.

arch_m.text:
Two days on hands and knees in a trench, unpaid, with the pour booked and the contractor watching from the edge every hour on the hour.
By the end of the first day it is a boundary stone, in place, still doing its job. By the middle of the second there is {a second one|another|the next one in the line} four metres along, and a third where the trench ends, and the line they make runs {straight under the town|off under the houses|the length of {place}}.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Monday is not moving for this.|Two days unpaid and now there are three of them.|We have found something too big to have found.}"
asides.any: {member} {gets the theodolite out of the van without asking|puts a tape on the spacing|photographs all three before anybody decides anything}

choices.text: File the report on the one stone. That is what was dug up.
Survey the whole line before anybody pours anything.
Date the stones and find out what they were for.

arch_line.text:
The line is surveyed in an afternoon and it is not a boundary. It is {one side of something|an edge|the north wall of something} that has {four|five|three} corners, and two of the corners are under standing houses.
The pour is off. It is off for {a year|two seasons|eighteen months}. The contractor loses the job and gains a considerably larger one, and the party's names are on the first page of the report.

arch_date.text:
The stones are {eight hundred|six hundred|a great many} years older than the town that has been respecting them, and they are not local stone, and they were cut somewhere that has not existed for longer than that.
What that means is above the pay grade of everybody currently standing in the trench. It is not above the pay grade of the people who arrive {eleven days|a fortnight|three weeks} later, who pay well and ask the party to say nothing.

pour_m.text:
The machine goes back in on the Saturday. It takes {forty minutes|an hour|most of the morning} and it is the easiest money anybody will make this month.
At the bottom of it, under where the thing in the trench was, the bucket brings up something that is not stone and not soil, and the driver stops without being told to, for the second time in {two days|a weekend|three days}.

choices.text: Keep going. Sunday night, nothing in the trench but trench.
Get down there and look at it.
Stop the machine. Call the two days back on.

pour_look.text:
Down in it, under lamps, with the sides of the trench {not liking it|moving slightly|as unhappy as trench sides get}, it is a void: {a metre|a metre and a half|about a metre} across, lined, going down.
What comes out of it in the next hour is worth more than the building, and the concrete goes in on Monday over the top of the rest of it regardless, because Monday is Monday.

qe_race.title: {Saturday On The Long Straight|Under Eighty Or Not At All|The Bet}

n0.text:
There is a straight outside {place} where they run on a Saturday, and the whole game is that the ones who win are the ones who do not go over.
Everybody knows where the bubble sits. {stranger} takes the money on the gate. {many} people are here for it and about half of them have opinions about {vehicle} the party arrived in.
There is a wreath on the fence at the three-quarter mark, and it is {this season's|not old|fresh}.

asides.hedonistic: {member} has put money on somebody they have never met on the strength of a jacket.
asides.cautious: {member} {watches the perimeter with a frown: "Bad idea."|checks their weapon charge and backs up a step|keeps a finger on the safety and mutters a warning|eyes the surroundings: "This has trap written all over it."}

Run it.
Flag the edge for them before somebody else goes over.

The one in the jacket holds it at {seventy-nine|seventy-eight|a shade under} the whole way down and takes it by a length and a half without ever once being interesting to look at, which is the entire art.
The gate pays out in cash and the party is bought drinks by strangers for {the rest of the evening|the rest of the night|hours}.

The one in the jacket goes over at the {three-quarter mark|last marker|top of the straight}, which everybody in the crowd sees coming about a second before it happens.
The stake is gone and the jacket is gone, and the gate keeps taking money, because there is another one in {twenty minutes|half an hour|a quarter of an hour}.

ran.text:
Holding a thing at seventy-nine the whole length of the straight, with a crowd screaming at you to do the one thing that will end you, is a test of nerve.
{leader} takes it at a walking pace by comparison to everybody else and wins, and the straight gives them the sort of silence that turns into a roar.

ranf.text:
It gets away at the top end for a moment and the moment is enough to be pulled at, and the pull is felt in the chest and the teeth before the brakes answer.
The party comes off the straight at a crawl with everybody very white. The crowd {applauds anyway|cheers anyway|makes a noise about it anyway}, which is {somehow worse|worse|the worst part of it}.

flag.text:
Posts and tape at the real edge, laid out in the afternoon before the crowd arrives, with the {material} the party carried in.
Saturday goes off with nobody lost for the first time in a season. The gate is furious for about an hour and then buys the party a drink, {twice|twice over|and then another}.

ran_m.text:
Holding a thing at seventy-nine the whole length of the straight, with a crowd screaming at you to do the one thing that will end you, is a test of nerve, and it goes well for {two thirds|most|the first half} of the straight.
Then the one in the jacket comes up the inside at a speed that says they have decided today is the day, and they are {a wheel|half a length|inches} ahead and still climbing.

choices.text: Hold seventy-nine. Let them go over if they are going.
Go with them. Match it.
Get alongside and force them off the line.

ran_match.text:
Eighty-one for {four seconds|three seconds|about a second and a half}, which is four seconds longer than the edge allows and is the reason there is a wreath on the fence.
Both of them come off the straight. Only one of them comes off it at the far end, and it is the party, and it takes {a fortnight|some weeks|a while} before anybody can say how.

ran_push.text:
There is exactly one way to do it that is not murder, and it involves {the inside|a wheel|two feet of tarmac} and the certainty that the other driver will take it rather than the edge.
They take it. Both cars come off the straight slow, sideways and whole, and the crowd does not know whether to cheer, and the one in the jacket sits in the car for {a long time|four or five minutes|a while} before getting out and shaking hands.

flag_m.text:
Posts and tape at the real edge, laid out in the afternoon before the crowd arrives, with the {material} the party carried in.
The gate arrives at {four|five|the back of four} and is furious, because tape at the real edge means everybody can see where it is, and the whole business of the Saturday is that they {cannot|can only guess|have to feel for it}.

choices.text: Stand by the tape. Let them be furious.
Make the case to the drivers, not the gate.
Take payment to move the tape back where it was.

flag_drivers.text:
The drivers are in a shed behind the start with the doors open and they listen, because the person talking has {run it|been down the straight|driven it today} and they saw them do it.
The vote is not close. The tape stays. The gate takes {a bad Saturday|a poor gate|half of what they expected} and the drivers take the whole season without losing anybody, and the following year the tape goes up before anybody asks.

flag_pulled.text:
The case is made to the wrong people in the wrong order and the gate has {four|five} men and the party has an argument.
The tape comes down at {six|half five|before the crowd}. Saturday runs the way Saturday runs. There is a new wreath on the fence by {nine|the last race|dark} and the party is a long way down the road by then, which does not help at all.

flag_bribe.text:
It is offered before it is asked for, which is how the gate does business, and it is {good money|a lot of money|more than the posts cost}.
The tape goes back where it was. The party takes the money and does not stay for the racing, and does not find out until {a month later|the spring|much later} whether anybody went over that Saturday, and by then not knowing has become a decision in itself.

qe_orchard.title: {The Orchard Nobody Owns|A Season Of It|Windfalls}

n0.text:
There is an orchard behind {place} that has been unowned since {timeAgo}, and this year it has come in heavy enough to break its own branches.
{stranger} has been picking it alone for a week. Nobody else has come. The whole crop goes over in about four days if it is not taken.
The trees are in {nine|eleven|a good many} rows and the ninth row is a different variety, planted later, by somebody who meant it.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Pick it. All of it.
Give {qty} {material} for crates and get the town up here.
Prune it properly for next year instead.

pick.text:
{Four|Five|Three} days of ladders and aching hands and more fruit than anybody has containers for, and it is all in before the weather turns.
The party leaves with as much as they can carry and the standing right to come back next year, which in a place like this is {a document|as good as a deed|worth more than paper}.

pickf.text:
The weather comes in on the second day and the rest goes over on the branch in a night.
What was got is worth having. What is left drops into the grass and feeds {animal} instead, which somebody older points out is {not nothing|not a waste|the older arrangement}.

town.text:
Crates, a cart, and word put about, and by the second morning there are {many} people in an orchard that nobody owns taking what they need and stacking the rest.
It goes to the school, the two houses on the corner, and a woman on {street} who has not asked anybody for anything in {timeAgo}.

prune.text:
The crop goes over and everybody agrees, out loud, that it was going to.
What gets done instead is the saw work nobody has done since {timeAgo}, and in {three|four} years that orchard will carry twice this and not break itself doing it, and none of that is visible {today|from here|this afternoon}.

town_m.text:
Crates, a cart, and word put about, and by the second morning there are {many} people in an orchard that nobody owns.
By the second afternoon there are two men at the gate with a paper that says somebody does own it, and the paper is {twenty years old|dated before the town was cleared|not obviously wrong}.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{Funny how ownership turns up at harvest.|Nobody owned it in March.|Twenty years of nothing and now a paper.}"
asides.any: {member} {puts the crate down and walks to the gate|reads the paper over somebody's shoulder|keeps picking}
