Read the paper properly.
Keep picking and let them stand there.

town_law.text:
The paper is real and the claim under it lapsed {eleven years ago|a decade back|long before this year's blossom} for want of anybody doing anything with the ground, which is a thing that is written down and can be shown to two men at a gate.
It is shown. They go. The picking finishes on the third day, the crop goes to the school and the two houses on the corner and everywhere else, and the lapse gets registered properly {that winter|before the year is out|by somebody who now knows how}.

town_stop.text:
Stopping a hundred people picking free fruit takes {longer than starting them|most of an hour|more voice than anybody has left}, and it is done, and the crates come back down to the gate stacked.
The two men take the orchard and do not pick it. It goes over on the branch in {a fortnight|the following week|a wet ten days}, all of it, and everybody in the town watches that happen from the road.

prune_m.text:
The crop goes over and everybody agrees, out loud, that it was going to, and the saw work starts on the second morning.
In the ninth row, the different one, the pruning uncovers what the row is: every tree in it is {the same tree|one tree|the same tree over and over}, grafted, from one stock, and at the end of the row there is a stump with {a plate on it and a name|a name plate|a brass plate and a name}.

choices.text: Finish the pruning. Leave the plate alone.
Graft from the ninth row before the saw work goes on.
Find out whose name is on the plate.

prune_graft.text:
{Nine|Eleven|A dozen} cuttings, taken correctly, waxed, and carried out in a damp cloth to somewhere they will take.
The variety turns out to be one that was written off as gone {thirty years ago|two generations back|in the war}, and there are people who will pay for a stick of it, and there are more people who will simply be very glad, and the second lot are better to know.

prune_name.text:
It takes {two afternoons|a day|some asking} in a town that has mostly stopped keeping records, and the name on the plate belonged to somebody who planted a row of one tree and then left and did not come back.
There is a granddaughter, {two valleys over|in the next town|nearer than anybody expected}, who did not know the orchard existed. She comes up the following spring. After that it is not an unowned orchard any more.

n0.text:
{stranger} in {place} has a summons with somebody else's crime on it and their own name, spelled correctly, in a hand that never makes mistakes.
Her court does not do appeals in the usual sense. It does arbitrary, and it does it fast, and the hour named on the paper is tomorrow's.
The summons is dated {tomorrow|the day after|for a day that has not happened yet} and has already been stamped as heard.

asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Build the alibi and get it filed.
Pay the fine and make it go away.
Go and stand with them.

ali.text:
It takes an afternoon of {paper} and {few} people willing to sign something, and the filing is done with an hour in hand.
It works, in the sense that the summons is withdrawn. Nobody will say by whom, or whether anybody read it, and the party is careful not to celebrate anywhere it might be overheard.

alif.text:
The filing is accepted, stamped, and has no effect whatsoever on anything that happens the following day.
It was never going to. Somewhere in the arithmetic of the thing there is a joke, and the party is not {the audience for it|the audience|who it is for}.

pay.text:
The fine is paid at a window by somebody who does not look up, and the summons is marked settled in the same hand that wrote it.
It cost what {a year|most of a year|a very good year} costs. The person on the paper will be paying the party back in instalments for the rest of their life and will {insist on it|insist|not be talked out of it}.

stand.text:
Standing in that room with somebody is not a legal strategy and it is not nothing.
It goes {how it goes|the way it was always going to|badly, and quickly}. Afterwards, out in the light, the party is thanked by somebody who has just lost a great deal and is thanking them {properly anyway|properly|carefully, anyway}.

stand_m.text:
Standing in that room with somebody is not a legal strategy and it is not nothing, and the room is {smaller|a good deal smaller|nothing like as grand} than the word court suggests.
There are {four|five} other matters on before this one and all of them go the same way, quickly, with the same phrase used each time, and by the fourth it is possible to hear what the phrase is actually asking for.

choices.text: Stand there. Say nothing. See it through.
Give the phrase back to her, correctly.
Take the blame for it instead.

stand_phrase.text:
It is said once, flatly, from the back of the room, in the same words and the right order, and the whole proceeding stops for {nine seconds|a long moment|the length of a held breath}.
The matter is dismissed without explanation. So are the two after it. Nobody in the room looks at the party on the way out and everybody in the room knows exactly what happened, which is how her court has always worked.

stand_worse.text:
It is said from the back of the room with one word out of place, and one word out of place in that room is {an invitation|an application|a volunteering}.
The matter on the paper is settled in {stranger}'s favour immediately. The matter that replaces it on the list has the party's own name on it, correctly spelled, in a hand that never makes mistakes.

stand_blame.text:
Taking somebody else's summons onto your own name is a thing the court permits, has always permitted, and has clearly been waiting all afternoon for somebody to do.
The fine is {nothing|a coin|deliberately insulting}. The condition attached to it is not, and it will come due at a time and in a manner entirely of her choosing.

pay_m.text:
The fine is payable at a window by somebody who does not look up, and the number on the paper is what {a year|most of a year|a very good year} costs.
There is a second window. Nobody is queueing at it. Above it, in the same hand as the summons, it says that payments made there are {at the court's discretion|assessed rather than charged|whatever is honest}.

choices.text: Pay the number at the first window.
Go to the second window.
Ask the clerk which window she would use.

pay_second.text:
The window opens on somebody who asks one question, which is what the party thinks it is worth, and then writes down whatever is said {without comment|without looking up|as if it were a fact}.
What is paid is either a great deal less than the fine or a great deal more, and which of those it turns out to have been is not established for {some weeks|a season|a considerable time}.

pay_clerk.text:
The clerk looks up for the first time, which by itself is worth the question, and says: the second one, always, and nobody ever does.
The party uses the second window. The clerk is, it becomes clear over the following {year|seasons|while}, a person worth knowing, and remembers being asked.

qe_smith.title: {The Forge Is Out|Cold Since Wednesday|One More Firing}

n0.text:
The forge at {place} has been cold since Wednesday and {stranger} is standing in the doorway of it with an order book that is still full.
What it takes is fuel and {qty} {material} for the tuyere, and the merchant is {distance} and has stopped extending credit to anybody in this trade.
The order book has {two|three} pages torn out of the front of it, and the stub edges are {clean|fresh|not old}.

asides.disciplined: {member} {follows standard breach protocol by the book|clears every corner with military precision|keeps a steady firing stance and monitors the sensors|checks the ammo count and maintains position}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Give the {material}.
Work the bellows and get one firing out of what is here.
Buy the whole order book off them.

give2.text:
The tuyere goes in and the forge takes about forty minutes to remember what it is for and then remembers hard.
The first thing off the anvil is not on the order book. It is for the party, made properly, in the hour the fire came back, and it is not offered so much as put in {leader}'s {hands|hands without a word|hands and closed over}.

one.text:
{Two|Three} hours on the bellows with what is in the bunker gets one firing, and one firing clears the top three lines of the book.
Those three lines are the ones with people's names on them rather than companies. That is not an accident and the smith does not {pretend it is|pretend otherwise|claim otherwise}.

onef.text:
The fire will not come up past a sulk and the bellows leather goes at the seam about {ninety minutes|an hour|two hours} in.
Everybody is filthy and nothing is made. The smith puts the kettle on the dead forge out of habit and then {laughs at having done it|laughs|sits down on the anvil laughing}.

buy3.text:
The whole book, at face value, in cash on {the anvil|the quench trough|the only clean surface in the building}, which is not how anybody in the trade does anything.
It clears the debt and it clears the credit and by the following week the forge is lit and the book is filling again, and the party holds paper on {every line in it|the whole book|each line of it}.

give2_m.text:
The tuyere goes in and the forge takes about forty minutes to remember what it is for and then remembers hard, and the light in that building changes completely.
With the fire up, the back wall is visible for the first time, and on the back wall there is work hanging that is not in the order book and is not {stranger}'s: {older|a different hand|somebody else's entirely}, and better.

asides.cynical: {member}: "{That is not their work and they know we can see it.|Whoever made that is not in this room.|The torn-out pages, the wall. Add it up.}"
asides.any: {member} {looks at the wall for a long time|puts a hand near the fire and does not say anything|counts the pieces}

choices.text: Take the piece they make for you and say nothing.
Ask about the wall.
Look at how the pieces on the wall were made.

give2_wall.text:
It was their {master|father|mother}, and the torn pages were that person's last orders, and they were torn out on the Wednesday the forge went cold because {stranger} could not look at them any more.
The pages come out of a drawer, unburned. They are worked through together over {two days|the rest of the week|the next two days}, in order, and the last one is finished with four people standing round the anvil.

give2_learn.text:
The pieces on the wall are the same joint done {nine|eleven|a dozen} ways, which is not decoration, it is a teaching wall, and reading it is being taught by somebody who is not there.
It takes an afternoon standing in front of it with a hot fire behind. What comes off the party's own anvil afterwards is measurably better, and stays measurably better.

buy3_m.text:
The whole book, at face value, in cash on {the anvil|the quench trough|the only clean surface in the building}, which is not how anybody in the trade does anything.
{stranger} does not pick the money up. What they say instead is that {four|five} of those lines are for one buyer, that the buyer is the reason the forge went cold on Wednesday, and that the party has just bought whatever that is.

choices.text: Fine. We bought it. Deliver the lot.
Find out who the buyer is before anything gets made.
Tear those four lines out and pay for the rest.

buy3_who.text:
It takes {two questions|an evening|one name at one bar} and the buyer is not a company: it is somebody who has been placing the same order, in pieces, across {four|five} forges in this district for a year, and the pieces make one thing.
What the thing is, the party works out on the back of a beer mat in about {ten minutes|a quarter of an hour|no time}, and then nobody wants another drink.

buy3_bad.text:
Asking about the buyer in the wrong bar means the buyer knows by {morning|the following day|closing time} that somebody has bought the book.
The order is collected on time by people who are correct throughout and who look at each of the party in turn on the way out, the way you look at things you expect to see again.

buy3_tear.text:
Four lines out of a book, torn cleanly, and the rest paid for at face value with the fire coming up behind.
{stranger} watches the four lines go on the fire and then sits down on the quench trough and does not get up for {a while|some minutes|a long moment}. The forge runs. The buyer comes back in {the spring|a month|due course} and finds a smith who can say no now.

qe_sleeper.title: {The One Who Will Not Wake|Breathing Fine|Since The Loop}

n0.text:
There is somebody in an upstairs room in {place} who has not woken since {timeAgo} and is in no other way unwell.
Everything works. Everything is warm. The eyes move. {stranger} has been turning them and feeding them and talking to them the whole time and has nearly run out of things to say.
The room has been kept exactly as it was on the day, {down to a cup|including a cup on the sill|with the curtains at the same half}, which was somebody's decision and has never been revisited.

asides.empathetic: {member} {looks at the wreckage and shakes their head: "Tough way to go."|checks for survivor logs with a quiet sigh|hopes whoever was here got out in time|mutters a quiet condolence for the crew}
asides.cynical: {member} {snorts: "Great. More overpriced scrap."|rolls their eyes: "Ten credits says there's nothing useful inside."|scoffs: "If there was anything valuable here, someone would have stolen it already."|shrugs: "Let's just grab the loot before something explodes."}
asides.any: {member} {keeps an eye on the sensors and says nothing|watches the approach with a neutral squint|checks their holster with quiet efficiency|stands by the entryway, ready for trouble}

choices.text: Go in after them.
Bring what medicine {qty} {material} buys and keep them alive properly.
Sit the night so somebody else can sleep.

in2.text:
Wherever they are, it is a room like this one and a day like the day they went under, and they have been having it for {timeAgo} and are perfectly content.
Convincing somebody to leave that is the hardest hour of the year. It is done, in the end, by {leader} being extremely boring about a very small practical detail, which is {what works|the thing that works|what does it in the end}.

in2f.text:
It is a room like this one and a day like that day and it is very easy to sit down in.
{leader} comes back out because {member} is shouting from the ordinary side of it, and does not talk about how close the sitting down got.

keep.text:
Proper feeding, proper turning, and enough of it laid in that the next {few} months are not a daily crisis.
Nothing about the sleeping changes. Everything about the sitting up with it does, and the difference is {the whole of somebody's life|somebody's entire life|the whole of two lives}.

sit.text:
A night in a chair by a bed, doing the turning at the right hours and talking about nothing to somebody who does not answer.
{stranger} sleeps eleven hours and comes up the stairs in the morning looking like a different person and {apologising for it|apologising|embarrassed about it}.

sit_m.text:
A night in a chair by a bed, doing the turning at the right hours and talking about nothing to somebody who does not answer.
At about {three|half two|the dead hour} the sleeper says a word. One word, clearly, in a voice that has not been used since {timeAgo}, and then nothing else for the rest of the night.

asides.nurturing: {member} is at the bedside with a hand on a wrist before the word has finished.
asides.any: {member} {writes the word down exactly as it sounded|checks the clock and writes the hour beside it|does not move, in case there is a second one}

choices.text: Note it and finish the night quietly.
Answer them. Keep talking until dawn.
Work out what the word is.

sit_talk.text:
Talking to somebody who is not there for {four hours|the rest of the night|until it gets light} is either useless or the whole treatment, and nobody finds out which until about {five|half four|first light}, when a hand closes on {leader}'s.
It does not open again for {an hour|a long time|the rest of the morning}. Nothing else changes, and that is still the largest thing that has happened in this house in years.

sit_word.text:
It is not a word in any language spoken in this town, and it is a word: {two syllables|three syllables|short}, with a stress pattern, in a family {member} has seen written down in exactly one place.
The one place is a long way from here and is worth going to. What is at the other end of it is another matter entirely, and it is the reason this house has an upstairs room that nobody uses.

keep_m.text:
Proper feeding, proper turning, and enough laid in that the next {few} months are not a daily crisis, all of which takes {a day|most of two days|an afternoon and a morning} of doing rather than deciding.
Under the bed, while the turning is being done properly for the first time, there is a case. It is not dusty. Somebody has been getting it out and putting it back for {years|a long time|the whole of the sleeping}.

choices.text: Push it back under. Not ours.
Ask {stranger} about it.
Open it while they are downstairs.

keep_ask.text:
It comes out from under the bed and onto the counterpane and is opened by {stranger}, who has clearly been waiting a considerable time to be asked and has no intention of being asked twice.
What is in it explains the sleeping, or explains what the sleeping is a consequence of, which is not the same thing and is a great deal more useful. It also explains why nobody has ever been sent for.

keep_open.text:
It opens without a key, which means it is not the sort of case anybody expects to be opened by a stranger, and what is inside takes about {nine seconds|a moment|no time at all} to understand.
It is put back exactly as found. {stranger} comes up with tea and finds four people standing in a room being very normal at them, and something in the house changes that afternoon and never changes back.
